News.title: Lando Norris comes in from the cold with dominant Hungarian GP victory
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix from the Hungaroring. This is the 40th anniversary of the race at this track and the 41st edition. I think over the years this track has had a bit of an unfair reputation but we have certainly had some interesting and exciting races over the years. Even over the last few years.

The nature of the track means it is a bit of an outlier. And that means you often get results that go away from the norm of the season. Mercedes took a couple of poles here in the ground-effect era whilst Charles Leclerc did so last year. We have had a handful of first-time winners at this track, too: Damon Hill, Fernando Alonso, Esteban Ocon, Jenson Button and… errr Heikki Kovalainen.

So far that has been true this weekend. Although McLaren and Ferrari have been closing in on Mercedes, the SIlver Arrows have usually had the edge or found it when it comes to qualifying. That was not the case yesterday: Lando Norris took the first non-Mercedes grand prix pole of the season, pipping the Ferrari of Lewis Hamilton by just 0.012sec.

Hamilton, though, takes a three-place grid penalty for impeding Oscar Piastri in Q3. Kimi Antonelli, who had qualified fourth, takes the same penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. It was Ferrari who had been expected to be the team to beat but they were the team that dropped the ball. In fairness Norris, in the upgraded McLaren had looked competitive throughout qualifying and was simply able to deliver when Ferrari could not.

The grid is slightly mixed up because of the penalties. George Russell’s season did not get any easier after qualifying seventh but he at least moves up because of those grid drops. The Mercedes’ race pace is expected to be strong but will it be enough to put them into contention with the McLarens and the Ferraris? And let’s not forget Max Verstappen in fourth, either…

We find out at 2pm BST, when the race gets under way.

News.title: Anthony Joshua knocks out Kristian Prenga after worst round of his career
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Anthony Joshua’s heavyweight clash with Kristian Prenga, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

The kingdom plays host to yet another major boxing event, and this is the second part of a weekend that serves as a build-up to a potentially huge match-up later this year.

Prenga’s 20 wins have come against pedestrian opposition, and if he wins tonight then it would be such an upset as to probably finish Joshua’s career as a real name in the sport.

Joshua, the former unified champion, has plenty of defeats to his name. Oleksandr Usyk, twice, as well as Daniel Dubois and Andy Ruiz Jnr.

Tonight should show us where he is. After his loss to Dubois in 2024 he did not fight again until December 2025, when he rearranged Jake Paul’s ability first to stand up, and second, to chew.

A win for Joshua tonight means that all eyes turn to the end of the year, when he is expected to finally meet Tyson Fury in the ring to settle their rivalry.

Now both are deposed champions, the interest has waned a tad, but it remains the biggest all-British clash that anybody could conceive.

Fury, for his part, had little trouble against Mariusz Wach last night, the 46-year-old journeyman who he fought in Thailand. While that was not broadcast live, the clips online hardly suggested it was a classic, but it was enough to keep Fury active as he maintained his focus and avoided his own banana skin.

Joshua now needs to show that he is capable of finishing a fight. If he struggles, he invites pressure for the next four or five months in the build-up to meeting Fury.

News.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty breaks down in tears after settling for bronze
News.content:
Afterwards, Ramsay-Peaty, whose alleged dispute with his own family became a major distraction during his marriage earlier this year, was visibly emotional as he criticised the media which he insisted had written “rubbish” about his personal life.

“I know the s--- I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, to be honest,” said Ramsay-Peaty, who lost his 100m breaststroke crown two years ago at the Paris Olympics. “But it does take a toll. The choices I’ve made over the last few months have been hard ones. But I’m happy at the same time that I can get here. I didn’t quit in Paris, but I deserve more.”

He added: “You don’t know who I am and people who comment, people who see the story because you read a headline, they’ve got to look themselves in the mirror,” Ramsay-Peaty told a group of reporters.

“You can’t hurt me. For me, it’s about my family and that does come at a cost. Being able to ignore that and being able to focus on my job – that hasn’t played a part in a sense of what we’re experiencing today.

“I’m still happy with that result. There’s some sense, but it has to, it has to stop. You know, look how many, how many athletes, how many people have to go for this until the media learn [a] lesson?”

Referencing Nowacki, the 18-year-old sensation from Jersey who has long been regarded as Ramsay-Peaty’s breaststroke successor, he added; “You have to learn and do better. You know, and for me, you know, I don’t want a young Filip one day to go through something like that, or these younger athletes.

“For me, that’s part of what I have to go through. I’ve got no control over that. But I think enough is enough. This is away from sport – it’s just about being decent people.”

After receiving his bronze medal, Ramsay-Peaty approached his wife, with whom he is expecting a child in December, and kissed her baby bump.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton hit with penalty in blow to Hungarian GP hopes
News.content:
Lewis Hamilton’s hopes of significantly denting Kimi Antonelli’s championship lead were dealt a blow after he was given a three-place grid penalty for Sunday’s Hungarian Grand Prix.

Hamilton looked to be the man to beat heading into qualifying at the Hungaroring and was on course for a record 10th pole position here before a messy final few minutes cost him.

Ferrari were well placed to end Mercedes’s run of having taken pole position for every grand prix this season. Instead, defending champion Lando Norris snuck in and took a superb pole for McLaren with a lap of 1min 17.207sec.

A poor final lap from Hamilton was compounded by a grid penalty for impeding the McLaren of Oscar Piastri, meaning the seven-time world champion will start fifth for the race at one of his most favoured circuits. The only consolation was that Antonelli was also given a three-place grid penalty for not slowing sufficiently under yellow flags. The Italian will start seventh while Charles Leclerc, Hamilton’s team-mate, will be alongside Norris on the front row.

Heading into the final runs in Q3, Hamilton was 0.101sec ahead of Norris, but did not improve his time. Yet Norris, who was fastest in Q1 and Q2, and was the last of the top three across the line in Q3, had no problem, beating Hamilton’s time by 0.012sec.

Hamilton was critical of his Ferrari team for sending him out first, a decision he said “shocked” him.

“I don’t know why we went first, that was a bit of a shock to me and I definitely wouldn’t have chosen to go first,” Hamilton said. “I had a clean out-lap and when I started my lap and already in turn one I had a snap [of oversteer], I was already a tenth down. The last lap was the worst lap of all... we clearly had the car to be on pole.”

Worse was on the way for Hamilton. The stewards later confirmed the three-place grid penalty to add to the disappointment of missing out on pole.

Replays showed a frustrated Piastri gesturing to Hamilton for blocking him at turn one, ruining the Australian’s final flying lap. Hamilton said he was unaware that Piastri was there, which was proved by video evidence that showed how much he impeded the McLaren. It would have been an easy decision for the stewards to make.

News.title: ‘Always in bloom, a visit really makes one’s day’: Your favourite garden centres
News.content:
Bryan, 86, from the South East, has been a customer of Henry Street Garden Centre in Arborfield, Berkshire for decades: “My wife and I often used to browse and purchase plants and garden furniture.”

But his favourite memory was watching his wife’s “delight at their incredible Christmas displays of decorations. Lights, live reindeer even and the wonderful family atmosphere all around you,” he describes. “It’s still a magical place for me where I can get close to her memory.”

For Mary, 79, from the South East, “a garden centre is special if the plants are in season and healthy and there is great choice of both plants and compost”. She nominates family-run Grovewell Garden Centres at Swingfield near Folkestone, which has three other branches based in Kent.

Not only are their plants “always beautifully displayed”, she explains, they have “an amazing choice of garden supplies, cards and gifts, as well as a nice little coffee shop”. Her favourite memory, however, was at Christmas time a few years ago. “They have a couple of beautiful, nodding and interacting reindeer with a sofa in front of them. We were admiring them and an older guy on the staff asked if we wanted a photo taken, which was so sweet of him.”

“He took my husband’s phone and got a really happy little snap of us and the reindeer, which our girls thought was hilarious,” she says. “Service with a smile.”

Community spirit

News.title: Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe
News.content:
Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.

News.title: How to choose a sports bra, with advice from a netball player, bra fitter and scientist
News.content:
How do you tell if a sports bra is the wrong size?

One of the biggest mistakes shoppers make is assuming that if a sports bra feels tight, that’s enough. In reality, support comes from the right fit rather than simply compressing your chest.

Cardwell advises thoroughly testing a sports bra by moving in it in the same way as you will during the sport you will be doing. “Your breasts don’t just move up and down,” she says. “They move all around – circles, up, down, left, right. We want to try and restrict that as much as possible, but not to the extreme where you’re not able to breathe.”

What is a high impact sports bra?

High-impact sports bras are designed for activities where your breasts experience the greatest movement, such as running, HIIT, tennis and netball. Their job is to minimise breast movement in every direction, helping reduce discomfort while allowing you to move more efficiently.

To measure how high-impact a sports bra is, Wakefield-Scurr asks women to run in a laboratory, both without a bra and while wearing different sports bras. “For a bra to be classed as high support, it has to reduce breast movement above certain thresholds,” she says. “If your breasts move 10 centimetres without a bra and five centimetres in a sports bra, that bra has reduced breast movement by 50 per cent.”

In the lab, Wakefield-Scurr and her team found that “if you run in low support compared with high support, you reduce your stride length by four centimetres. Four centimetres might not sound like a lot, but over the course of a marathon, those four centimetres add up to around a mile.” This proves that wearing a high-support bra doesn’t just keep you comfortable, but it can improve your athletic performance.

Cardwell, who wears a double G cup, says high-impact support has improved dramatically in recent years. “There has been a lot more research into high-impact sports bras, especially for larger-chested women.” She also warns against assuming that every sports bra offers the same level of support. “If it’s the same material as a smaller cup size, it’s probably not going to be sufficient for someone like me with double Gs.”

How often should you replace your sports bra?

There’s no set rule for replacing a sports bra, according to Wakefield-Scurr. This is because its lifespan depends more on how you care for it than how often you wear it. “The lifespan of a sports bra is affected more by how you wash and dry it than by how often you wear it,” she says. In one of her team’s studies, support dropped by around a third after 25 washes. “Always follow the washing instructions,” she advises. “You’d be surprised how many sports bras should be hand washed or washed at a lower temperature.”

Looking after your sports bra properly will help it last longer, but no bra lasts forever. Once the underband loses its elasticity or the support noticeably decreases, it’s time to replace it to ensure you have the right level of support.

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal retirement date ‘revealed’ as fans may not get chance to see him in UK again
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO’s retirement date from football has reportedly been revealed.

The five-time Ballon d’Or winner made his name in the UK during an six-year spell with Manchester United.



Ronaldo, 41, left United in 2009 for Real Madrid in what was a then-record transfer fee worth £80million.

He has since gone on to play for Juventus and Al-Nassr either side of his brief return to Old Trafford.



The forward featured in his SIXTH World Cup finals tournament but failed to win the elusive trophy.

He is Portugal‘s record goalscorer with 146 goals in 233 appearances – three of which came in the World Cup just gone.



Ronaldo is set to continue his playing career but reports have claimed that he will call time on his international duties.

Speculation after Portugal’s exit to eventual winners Spain suggested that he could try to soldier on to the Euros in 2028 or even a home World Cup in 2030.

But it seems that will not be the case, with his last dance on the international stage coming a lot sooner.

According to journalist Mohammed Awaad, Ronaldo will play one more time for his country.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

That outing will come in their next fixture against Wales in the Nations League on September 24.

The match will suitably be played at the home of Ronaldo in the Jose Alvalade – the stadium of his boyhood club Sporting Lisbon.

If this is the case, then it means Ronaldo is very unlikely to play in front of UK crowds again in his career.

He currently plays for Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia, who do not come up against British teams in regular tournaments.



The only chance for Ronaldo to play in a British stadium again would most likely be in a pre-season friendly.

Ronaldo has played against the Welsh once before in his career with the fixture coming in Euro 2016.

He scored a header and assisted team-mate Nani for the 2-0 victory at the Groupama Stadium in Lyon, France.



The star made his Portugal bow in 2003 during a 1-0 win over Kazakhstan as he replaced Luis Figo off the bench.

His record of 233 caps makes him the record holder for men’s international appearances – Lionel Messi is second with 207 for Argentina.

USA Women’s legend Kristine Lilly however boasts 354 international caps between August 1987 and November 2010.



Ronaldo has helped Portugal fill their trophy cabinet despite the lack of success in the World Cup.

Sports.title: Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni pleads with adoring fans to let him visit dentist after being TRAPPED in house all week
Sports.content:
LIONEL SCALONI appealed to Argentina fans who bombarded his home as he attempted to make his dentist appointment on time.

It’s eight days on from the World Cup final and La Albiceleste supporters are still camped out on their boss’ lawn in Pujato, outside Rosario.



In the viral footage, Scaloni, 48, can be spotted amongst a horde of fans with security ushering him towards a car.

On a crowded path, people of all ages held their arms out as they tried to get their moment with the Argentina boss.



Scaloni is heard excusing himself, saying: “I have a dentist appointment. I will be back soon.”

With the masses gathered outside his house, it is a wonder what the property would have looked like had Argentina won.

The Argentine has reportedly been coming out morning and afternoon to greet people, sign autographs, and pose for selfies.

Eager fans rushed online to comment on the swarm of supporters showing their affection to Scaloni.



One X user wrote: “It’s as though they won the World Cup. Massive love.”

Another said on Reddit: “Best manager in their history.”

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But someone else acknowledged: “Nice guy for doing all that for the fans.

“It seems overwhelming though, to have so many people surrounding him all the time.”



A fourth agreed: “Bro literally can’t go home without being hounded. That’s gotta feel insane.”

Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the game to hand the World Cup trophy to Spain as they claimed their second title.

Post-match, scattered melees broke out on the pitch while skipper Lionel Messi sobbed on the sidelines.

On Monday, Scaloni posted a statement on Instagram following the final disappointment.

The statement read: “After an intense week where sadness intertwined with joy, tears with smiles, anguish with tranquillity, and nerves with calm, I can finally sit down to write a few words.



“Although you know I’m not big on social media, it might be the best way to get this message to you.

“All I can say is I’m sorry I couldn’t bring home another trophy and give you a new reason to celebrate – something that, even if only for a few days, might have made you forget life’s hardships.

“But I want you to focus on what we tried to show you through this group of players – my warriors, as I called them when speaking about them to my wife.



“The effort, the drive, the desire, the “I can do it” attitude, refusing to give up (even when the odds are stacked against you).

“Giving your all (even when you have nothing left), weathering the cold showers of criticism (FROM PEOPLE WHO DON’T KNOW US), maintaining composure.

“And finding the will to stay on your feet when your legs no longer obey your brain…

“That is the true trophy.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I am eternally grateful to my coaching staff, the players, the AFA staff – those who work quietly behind the scenes to ensure our comfort – and to each and every one of you for the affection you’ve shown us.



“P.S. Whoever has an Argentine friend has a treasure.”

Sports.title: Will Morgan Rogers play for Chelsea on their pre-season tour of Australia and Asia?
Sports.content:
MORGAN Rogers will play for Chelsea next season, after completing a club record switch to the Blues.

The 23-year-old switched from Aston Villa to the Blues for a fee of £117million, a British record transfer fee.



Xabi Alonso is set to take charge of his first Chelsea games since becoming manager on a pre-season tour in Australia and Asia.

Will Morgan Rogers play for Chelsea on their pre-season tour?

Chelsea will tour Australia and Asia as part of their pre-season preparations.

Sports.title: ‘Absolute tinpot garbage’ – Ian Holloway unleashes instant classic rant after defeat before calling squad ‘imposters’
Sports.content:
SWINDON TOWN’S flops were on the receiving end of an explosive tirade from boss Ian Holloway after their preparations for the new season went from bad to worse.

The Robins suffered a 3-1 defeat to Championship side Bristol City on Saturday.



It came after also losing to Crystal Palace and non-league minnows Chippenham Town in friendlies.

And Holloway, 63, threatened to put members of his Swindon squad up for sale during a furious post-match rant.



The legendary chief launched a scathing attack over the Robins’ defending and warned huge improvements need to be made with the new campaign edging closer.

Holloway, whose side had their clash with Swindon Supermarine suspended following a horror injury earlier this month, said: “Pre-season’s a joke – always has been, always will be. Imposters wandering around.

“If you have a brilliant pre-season, you win every game, you can start the season like a bunch of idiots.

“What we’re trying to do is get people who understand it’s nice if you win, it’s nice if you get rewarded for your good stuff, but they’ve just showed me what I’ve got to look at.

“How can you take a throw-in here and not make them go back towards their goal and let you let a goal in?

“Absolute garbage. Terrible backline, awful midfield. The backline should be talking to the midfield. So, I’ve got some wonderful coaching points.

“Great goal by them, but that’s what we should have stopped. If that’s in a war, we’re dead.

“The truth about it – absolute tinpot garbage. That is in the Swindon area. That is right on our doorstep. That’s got to be headed out.

“I will look at that and if anybody continues to do it then I’ll have to get rid of them. If anybody didn’t do their job, we’ll have to show them.

“Hopefully, they’ll do it better, or we’ll have to get rid of them – because we’ve got to move forward.”



Swindon are set to face Leyton Orient and Forest Green Rovers before getting their season underway with a trip to Cardiff City in the first round of the Carabao Cup next week.

Sports.title: Jermain Defoe threatens legal action over 'untrue' Woking claims since leaving job
Sports.content:
Jermain Defoe threatens legal action over 'untrue' Woking claims since leaving job

Jermain Defoe left his role as Woking manager after four months but a bitter row has broken out over his exit from the National League side

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe's representatives have hit out over a statement issued by Woking chief Jody Brown. (Image: PA)

Former England striker Jermain Defoe intends to take legal action after a statement from Woking director of football Jody Brown. The National League side parted ways with the Premier League icon less than two weeks before the beginning of the season after Defoe admitted it was 'impossible to continue'.

‌



A bitter row has broken out between the 43-year-old and Cards chief after he defended the club's transfer policy in light of Defoe's departure.

‌



Brown thanked and praised the former Tottenham Hotspur, Sunderland and Rangers striker for his work during his four months in charge. But while the Woking chief was reluctant to divulge details, he accused Defoe of not turning up to a meeting with the directors, head of operations and the management team.

‌



The 4 transfers Arsenal must complete for Mikel Arteta to win another Premier League title READ MORE :

Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits READ MORE :

As a result of the statement, Surrey Live contacted the former striker's representatives, who replied: “The statement issued by Jody Brown is highly detrimental to Jermain’s reputation, and amounts to a serious defamation of character.

"The statement also suggests that Jermain was making unreasonable demands, which is simply untrue.

“Jermain is therefore taking immediate legal advice and intends to pursue appropriate legal action in relation to the statements made.”

‌



Defoe's departure on the eve of the new campaign sparked concerns and questions among the wider community. It prompted criticism towards the Woking hierarchy, leading Brown to launch a defence on social media platform X.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Brown said in a statement published online: “Jermain’s feedback was always positive, and he regularly expressed his enthusiasm and excitement for the season, both publicly and privately. I can therefore appreciate the surprise and subsequent speculation surrounding his sudden departure.

‌



“However, in recent weeks there had been feedback from across the club, including players, staff and other departments, regarding growing concerns. To better understand the situation, I asked Jermain and Paul for a brief report outlining the squad’s current depth, recruitment targets and any operational challenges, so we could provide the support required and accelerate preparations for the season.

"That report was requested on more than one occasion but was never received. A meeting was subsequently scheduled involving the directors, manager, assistant manager and Head of Operations to review preparations for the season. Neither Jermain nor his assistant attended that meeting or that day’s training session.

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe pictured alongside Jody Brown after being unveiled as Woking head coach. (Image: PA)

‌



"Throughout his tenure, Jermain had never communicated any serious concerns directly to me, so I am not going to speculate on his reasons. Every football club faces challenges. Players want more game time, improved contracts or transfers. The media team might want better equipment, the medical department more interns, the strength and conditioning staff larger gym space. and the car park attendants may want more coffee.

"But people do not just fail to turn up. The experience has highlighted lessons for both myself and the club, particularly around communication with Jermain and his representatives throughout the four months and six matches he was with us. Throughout that period, the club’s objective remained the same: to support the players and staff and give the project every opportunity to succeed."

Woking began their league campaign at home to Sutton United on August 8. Craig Ross and Jake Hyde has been instructed to take charge of the Cards on an interim basis.

Ross and Hyde were installed on a temporary basis four months ago after Ardley's tenure came to an end on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Marine in the FA Trophy quarter-final.

Sports.title: Bryson DeChambeau confronts his own behaviour as marmite LIV Golf star speaks out
Sports.content:
Bryson DeChambeau confronts his own behaviour as marmite LIV Golf star speaks out

Bryson DeChambeau has opened up about his behaviour, which has made him a divisive star on tour

View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau in action for LIV Golf (Image: Jason Butler, Getty Images)

Bryson DeChambeau has spoken candidly about his commitment to engaging with fans and signing autographs, revealing that his modest upbringing shaped his determination to make golf more accessible to people from all walks of life.

‌



The 32-year-old has built a profile that extends well beyond the fairways, cultivating a YouTube channel with more than 2.7 million subscribers and welcoming some of sport's biggest names — among them NBA icon Stephen Curry — onto his platform. Yet despite his considerable fame, DeChambeau remains one of the most approachable figures in professional golf, rarely declining an autograph and always willing to stop for a photograph.

‌



While he has had run-ins with Rory McIlroy and rubbed some up the wrong way, DeChambeau always has time for his fans. Despite his considerable fame, DeChambeau remains one of the most approachable figures in professional golf, rarely declining an autograph and always willing to stop for a photograph.

‌



Speaking to Mirror US Sport at the US Open, DeChambeau was open about the roots of that attitude. Growing up in Clovis, California, in a household where money was tight, the prospect of travelling to compete in tournaments felt out of reach.

"As time has gone on out here at LIV, you're playing around the globe quite a bit," said DeChambeau. "You're feeling and experiencing different grasses and learning how to compete under those conditions.

"I feel like, if anything, it's made me a more well-rounded golfer and given me the ability to learn in different situations because I wasn't fortunate to have that as a kid. I played in my area, and that's it. I didn't have the ability to go travel nor the money to go travel."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

"I mean, it's an honour. It's a crazy honour," DeChambeau added, referring to the popularity and attention he's gained throughout his career.

"I can't believe a kid from Clovis, California, that struggled to get into tournaments, because we didn't have any money growing up. Not too much. I mean, we had a mom who made a good salary, and my dad made an okay salary, but we really didn't have much."

‌



View 2 Images Bryson DeChambeau says he is growing in the game (Image: Getty)

The Ryder Cup star has endured a difficult major season, yet his 2026 LIV Golf record includes two victories as the Saudi-backed tour faces a potential collapse amid funding cuts.

Despite failing to make the cut at the first three majors, DeChambeau insisted his LIV Golf campaign has been hugely impressive.

‌



"It's funny, I feel like I've had my best year out here this year, and for whatever reason, I feel like I've left a lot out there, which is quite interesting to me, but very grateful for having a great year out here," said DeChambeau.

"I don't really know what to say. I feel like this year I was ready to go. I felt ready to go this year. It didn't work out that way in the majors. I feel really comfortable with my game, as comfortable as I felt in a long time."

DeChambeau's future remains uncertain as LIV Golf continues its search for fresh investment to safeguard the tour's survival beyond 2026.

Sports.title: PSG tell Liverpool outrageous Bradley Barcola transfer price as Chelsea cause problems
Sports.content:
PSG tell Liverpool outrageous Bradley Barcola transfer price as Chelsea cause problems

Liverpool's pursuit of PSG star Bradley Barcola this summer has been complicated by Chelsea

View 2 Images Liverpool have been told to pay £140m for Bradley Barcola (Image: Getty Images)

Liverpool's hunt for a Mohamed Salah successor appears to have led them to the door of French attacker, Bradley Barcola. The winger, who impressed at this summer's World Cup, will not come cheap, however, with Chelsea inadvertently causing the Reds a major headache.

‌



The 23-year-old's club, Paris Saint-Germain, are reportedly demanding that any of Barcola's potential suitors cough up a stunning £145 million for his services. Their reasoning for such a steep fee is in response to the astonishing amounts Chelsea paid for Aston Villa's Morgan Rogers and Manchester City dished out for Nottingham Forest's Elliot Anderson this summer.

‌



According to French outlet Mercato, Barcola has indicated he wants to leave the reigning European champions. However, as the winger still has two years left on his contract, PSG believe that £140m is a fair reflection of his valuation, given his profile and the current market.

‌



Rogers recently joined Stamford Bridge outfit Chelsea for £117m, a British record, while his England team-mate, Anderson, has moved to the Etihad Stadium for £116m. The French publication adds that talks between Barcola and PSG over a new deal have now ceased, and there are no further discussions between the two parties.

PSG's price for Barcola would make him the third most expensive transfer in history. It would put him behind Neymar's move from Barcelona to PSG in 2017 for £200m and Kylian Mbappe's switch from Monaco to the Parisian giants in the same year for £165m.

‌

Should Liverpool shell out such a sum, it would eclipse the £125m they paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak last summer. The Reds, now under Andoni Iraola, have made just one signing so far this transfer window.

Spanish World Cup winner Victor Munoz arrived from Osasuna for £34.5m, but he remains their sole addition so far. Speaking at his first press conference as Liverpool’s new head coach, Iraola admitted that his side needed more players.

He said: "Obviously we've signed two players already but we need more players – we know this. The club is working on this.

‌



"Me as a coach, selfishly, you want the players here [on] day one, ready to train from the pre-season, but we understand that football doesn't work like this. I know the club is working hard to get those signings and I'm trying obviously to help also."

View 2 Images Bradley Barcola's price tag has been set by PSG (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Former Liverpool striker Emile Heskey believes Barcola could prove a season-defining acquisition for the Reds. Heskey told BOYLE Sports: "Signing Bradley Barcola would be an amazing coup for Liverpool because he provides the pace and directness we've been missing on the left wing. We've been spoiled with Sadio Mané and Luis Díaz, and now we need Barcola to get the fans off their seats again."

‌



Former Man United and French forward Louis Saha believes Barcola possesses the qualities required to reach the pinnacle of the game.

Saha told Live Football Tickets: "Bradley Barcola is a terrific player. He has already won two Champions Leagues, and he could even win the World Cup over the next few weeks, his achievements for such a young player are staggering.

"He has enormous potential, and I'm not surprised Liverpool are looking at him. They need a replacement for Mohamed Salah, and Cody Gakpo has looked uncomfortable at times for them out wide. Barcola could easily fill either of those positions."

Sports.title: The 4 transfers Arsenal must complete for Mikel Arteta to win another Premier League title
Sports.content:
Arsenal ended an arduous 22-year wait for Premier League glory last term by winning the title under Mikel Arteta — and now they are hungry for continued domestic dominance.

The Gunners will be out to retain the title this year but know they cannot afford to stand still as their rivals strengthen across the board. Manchester City and Liverpool both have new managers who will want to make a strong impression, while Chelsea have already made some serious moves in the market.

Arsenal have made three signings so far (Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier and Piero Hincapie on a permanent) but are expected to push through far bigger deals before the transfer deadline.

The most eye-catching signing is likely to be the one that fills the left wing berth; Vinicius Junior is the latest player to be linked with Morgan Rogers now out of the equation and, with Arsenal wanting a real ceiling-raiser to level up their attack, the Real Madrid star certainly fits the bill in that respect. Whether or not a deal can be done in the next few weeks is another matter, particularly as it has been claimed Jose Mourinho wants to keep the Brazil international at the Bernabeu since news of Arsena's interest first emerged.

‌



Tzolis has already been signed from Club Brugge to replace the popular Leandro Trossard. As impressive as the Greece international's output was last season, he alone does not improve Arsenal's attack. That means they simply have to sign another left forward if they are to progress further this year — even if it means having to budge from their valuation of targets.

Arsenal have been left without a choice as Mikel Arteta's transfer frustrations clear READ MORE :

Bradley Barcola is another player who has been touted as a potential target but it seems as though Liverpool are pushing harder on that front right now. Yan Diomande, the other elite winger likely to move for big bucks this summer, seems to be Real Madrid bound. Arsenal reportedly enquired about Diomande last week. His prospective move to Real Madrid could, however, boost their chances of landing Vinicius Jr. So watch this space...

Central midfield is another area which is likely to see movement and Arsenal's pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes is in danger of becoming a bit of a saga. Arsenal want the Brazilian and he wants Arsenal. Unfortunately, Newcastle want their talismanic captain to stay put and are playing spoiler when it comes to a transfer.

As it transpired with Rogers, a move for Guimaraes will all come down to price; Newcastle will want a monster fee to sanction an exit and Arsenal will not want to pay what they deem silly money for a player who, although top-class, will turn 29 later this year. Suggestions last week were that Arsenal were ready to bid £70m for him. Subsequently, it was claimed Newcastle would reject that out of hand.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal's pursuit of Bruno Guimaraes is in danger of becoming a saga (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

If Guimaraes does prove to be unattainable, Arsenal are likely to turn their focus elsewhere. Alex Scott is well liked but again, Bournemouth don't want to sell and could demand in excess of £80m given the inflated transfer fees currently distorting the market. Ayyoub Bouaddi, one of the World Cup's breakout stars, is another player Arsenal have been linked with, although Manchester City are heavily courting the teenager amid speculation over Rodri's future.

With William Saliba out for the foreseeable future, Arsenal are also expected to add a centre-back. They have already set their sights on Ezri Konsa but, just as with Rogers prior to his Chelsea switch, their valuation of the player differs to that of Aston Villa. At 28 and coming off the back of a stellar World Cup with England, Konsa boasts Premier League pedigree and is versatile, too.

If Arsenal decide against pushing the boat out for Konsa, then his England team-mate, John Stones, is available on a free transfer and has the scope to be one of the bargains of the summer. Chelsea are also interested in the former Manchester City man, who has been doing his best to prevent Arsenal from winning the title in previous years. If the stars align before September 1, there's every chance he could be doing his bit to help them win it this time around.

‌



View 3 Images Arsenal are also avid admirers of Julian Alvarez (Image: Carl Recine, Getty Images)

If Arsenal do strengthen in those three positions, and depending on what sort of budget they have left available, there may be a chance they seek an elite centre-forward. That's despite spending significant money on Viktor Gyokeres last year.

Julian Alvarez is a player Arsenal have been linked with all the summer. He would command an absolutely seismic transfer fee, though, which would likely well eclipse the £125m that Liverpool parted with to sign Alexander Isak last year. He would represent an upgrade on Gyokeres, though, and it's even been suggested that Arsenal could offer the Swede as a makeweight to sweeten any prospective deal given Atletico Madrid do not want to sell Alvarez.

During his final season at Manchester City, Alvarez accumulated 21 goal contributions (11 goals, 10 assists) and is proven at Premier League level. A return to England may be unlikely, though, given Barcelona is thought to be the Argentina star's preferred destination.

Sports.title: Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits
Sports.content:
Man Utd announce goalkeeper transfer as Michael Carrick greenlights two exits

Manchester United have signed 19-year-old former Swansea City goalkeeper Kit Margetson and are looking to sell two other keepers in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Kit Margetson has joined Manchester United (Image: Poppy Townson/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have announced the signing of Kit Margetson as part of their overhaul of the goalkeeping department.

‌



Margetson, a Wales under-21 international, left Swansea City earlier this month when his contract expired. However, Swansea will receive a compensation fee for the young goalkeeper, having developed him since under-15 level under the eye of his father Martyn, who was until recently the Championship's side head of goalkeeping.

‌



He spent last season on loan at Connah's Quay Nomads where he made 34 appearances and kept 10 clean sheets. Margetson made his debut for Wales under-21s against Belarus in March.

‌



The club, who haven't announced the length of his contract, said in a statement: "Everyone at United would like to welcome Kit to the club and wish him the very best of luck for the future."

Free agent XI including Man Utd flop, Liverpool legend and current England star READ MORE :

Margetson's arrival is the latest in a succession of moves in the goalkeeping department at Old Trafford. United signed Wales international Karl Darlow from Leeds on a free transfer to provide back-up to Senne Lammens, who himself only arrival last year.

‌



Previous No.1 Andre Onana has been loaned back to Turkish side Trabzonspor, while Altay Bayindir and Radek Vitek are also set to depart in the coming weeks.

View 2 Images Radek Vitek could leave Manchester United this summer (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has greenlighted their departures to create space in the first-team squad. Bayindir has struggled to make an impact over the past few season and is seeking a permanent move, having not returned to United following the World Cup.

‌



Vitek spent last season on loan with Bristol City in the Championship and made a real impression. United are understood to value the the 22-year-old at £10million and have received plenty of interest in his services.

He started United's 5-0 pre-season win over Rosenborg on the weekend but will be allowed to leave, with Lammens and Darlow installed as the first and second-choice keepers and his value high after his Bristol City stint.

Sports.title: Arsenal will not be able to offer Vinicius Jr one thing he wants as huge update emerges
Sports.content:
Arsenal will not be able to offer Vinicius Jr one thing he wants as huge update emerges

Vinicius Jr will be forced into a change should he join Arsenal from Real Madrid in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr is of interest to Arsenal this summer (Image: Michael Regan - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Vinicius Jr would be denied his dream number at Arsenal if the Gunners were to clinch an extraordinary deal for the Real Madrid superstar. The 26-year-old emerged as a target for the Premier League side this past weekend.

‌



The Brazilian has spent eight years with the La Liga giants and with just 12 months left on his contract, rumours have circulated on whether his time at Madrid will come to an end. According to Diario AS, Vinicius hopes to continue at Madrid and optimism remains that a contract extension can be reached.

‌



However, if the winger does make the move to north London, he'll have to do without his favoured No. 7, having worn the number for the last three seasons in Spain. The jersey is currently occupied by Bukayo Saka, with Vinicius having to look elsewhere.

‌



Prior to receiving the storied jersey in 2023 upon the departure of Eden Hazard, the Brazilian had worn the No. 20 for three years, which is also unavailable at the Emirates Stadium, with Noni Madueke sporting the number.

Vinicius could revert back to the first two numbers he wore at Madrid - No. 28 and No. 25. Both jerseys are available in Mikel Arteta's squad, as well as No. 15 and No. 19 - the latter being vacated by Leandro Trossard's move to Besiktas.

Vinicius Junior transfer: Arsenal ready to break salary record to sign Real Madrid star READ MORE :

Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move READ MORE :

While Vinicius won't be able to continue sporting No. 7 on the club stage if a move to Arsenal materialises, he will be able to call himself the most paid player in the club's history, according to reports.

‌



The Telegraph states that his staggering salary of £400,000 per week wouldn't stop the deal from happening. It further claims that club executives would aim to improve his wages to further convince the Brazilian to sign.

View 2 Images Vinicius Jr has 12 months left on his contract at Real Madrid (Image: Photo by Alex Pantling - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Article continues below

Vinicius' potential wages would easily usurp those of Arsenal's current highest-paid player, Saka. The England star inked a £365,000-a-week contract in February, which is set to rise each season.

The Brazil international is coming off his second-best goalscoring season in La Liga, with 16 goals scored. But he failed to win a major honour for a second season in a row at Madrid.

Sports.title: Arsenal and Newcastle agreement ‘days away’ as Bruno Guimaraes transfer talks accelerated
Sports.content:
Arsenal and Newcastle agreement ‘days away’ as Bruno Guimaraes transfer talks accelerated

Arsenal are pushing for a move for Newcastle United captain, Bruno Guimaraes, and plan to complete a deal with the Magpies in the coming days

View 2 Images Arsenal are eager to sign Bruno Guimaraes (Image: NurPhoto, NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Arsenal are preparing to intensify talks with Newcastle United over Bruno Guimaraes, as they look to finally secure the Brazilian midfielder. It's been a lengthy saga between the two clubs this summer, with the Gunners keen on welcoming reinforcements to their engine room.

‌



That's despite the Magpies ultimately telling all interested parties that their captain is not for sale for any price. A shining light last season at St James' Park, Guimaraes has seen a wealth of attention in the current window.

‌



However, having already lost Sandro Tonali to Tottenham Hotspur and Anthony Gordon to Barcelona, Newcastle are eager to retain at least a portion of their foundation. Arsenal, however, have other ideas.

‌



Arsenal's two conditions for Bruno Guimaraes transfer as Gunners set to make next move READ MORE :

Bruno Guimaraes agent takes to social media as Arsenal prepare £70m bid for Newcastle star READ MORE :

It is understood that while no official discussions have begun, talkSPORT claim that Guimaraes has already reached an agreement on personal terms with the Gunners.

Andrea Berta's board are also reportedly prepared to offer at least £70million for the 28-year-old in the coming weeks, with sources additionally informing the publication that three verbal proposals have already been submitted by the North London club.

That's despite senior figures on Tyneside insisting that no official approach has been lodged as yet. Under contract until 2028, Newcastle are in no hurry to part with their captain, meaning they can essentially command whatever fee they desire to permit his departure.

‌



While Eddie Howe is determined to keep Guimaraes at the club ahead of the new campaign, the manager has conceded that the final decision ultimately lies beyond his control.

View 2 Images It looks to be a tough summer for Eddie Howe (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Speaking at the weekend, he said: "I've spoken to him as I would do. Bruno, normally, is just a fantastic person.

‌



"We've had some really good conversations, both before the World Cup, during the World Cup and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private.

"He's just a great player and a great person. Look, I don't know what's going to happen with Bruno's future.

"That's for other people to, one, speculate about, but also conversations that I'm not part of. We don't want to lose our best players.

‌



"That's an obvious statement to make. Losing those big two [Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali] is painful for us and difficult. For me, it's been another challenging summer so far."

Sports.title: 'Pressure is on Antonelli' - Norris not ruling out title fightback
Sports.content:
Lando Norris has not ruled out mounting a title fightback and says all the pressure is on Formula 1 championship leader Kimi Antonelli.

Norris claimed McLaren's first Grand Prix win of the season on Sunday with an impressive performance at the Hungarian Grand Prix and sits fifth in the Drivers' Championship, 91 points behind Antonelli with 11 rounds remaining.

Last year, Max Verstappen was 104 points off the championship lead with 10 events to go and fell just two points short of the title, which was won by Norris.

"The pressure is on him [Antonelli] for sure. There's no pressure on me. I've been feeling very confident," Norris told Sky Sports F1.

"They [Mercedes] have made more mistakes as a team and we have made less and we have come strong but I expect them to still win races and expect us to win more races. We just need to be perfect from here on now for the whole year.

"We need to improve the car still. We were certainly the quickest in Hungary from qualifying to the race. Not every race is going to be this simple, and we are going to be as quick, so we need to work hard to try to get the car to be this good to get the car to be this good everywhere. If we can, maybe that's a genuine question."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the 2026 Hungarian Grand Prix

McLaren brought a major upgrade packaged to Hungary, including a new floor, which has given them a big chunk of pace, having been able to fight at the front for most of the season.

Team principal Andrea Stella expects everyone to continue to bring new parts after the summer break, so McLaren must continue to improve too.

"Like it's always been in this 2026 season, it's a matter of a race of upgrades. The good news is that McLaren is now back in this race of upgrades, while fighting for the lead," he said.

"But I expect that the car that will be the best car at the end of the season will keep adding tenths of a second in the next 11 races, probably as much as half a second. So definitely a lot of work ahead of everyone, not only McLaren."

Image: The F1 Drivers' Championship with 11 rounds remaining

Norris defends pit priority call in Hungary

Norris lost out to Piastri on the opening lap of Sunday's race and was stuck behind his team-mate, despite clearly having more pace in hand.

He eventually used that speed advantage around the second pit stop phase by running longer than Piastri and overcutting the Australian. Prior to that moment, Norris wanted to pit first and had stated on the radio he was "miles faster".

"I just want to win the race. There are certain rules we have as a team, and we can't harm each other's race by being overly aggressive and wanting to win," said Norris in the press conference.

"But I want to win, and I certainly had much better pace than him. We had a much better chance of winning the race, let's say.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Oscar Piastri take the lead from Lando Norris as George Russell has a race start to forget at Hungaroring in Budapest

"When I was stuck behind Oscar, Max was three or four seconds behind, and at that point he's still a threat. Ahead, there's no threat, and we have a lot more of a guarantee that we'll win as a team anyway.

"So, I wanted to box and undercut because my pace would have been so good, I could have pulled away a whole pit-stop window, I think, on him and boxed again if I needed to. Or I get him to box early. I think we were on the fine line between boxing too early and harming both of our races.

"So, it was just in the best interests of the team, which they rightly have to say back against me. But I want to do whatever I can to try and win a race, of course."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

Norris has generally had the upper hand over Piastri in recent races and many feel the British driver is performing just as well as last year when he became world champion.

The McLaren driver is unsure why his pace advantage was so significant in Hungary but hopes he continues to have the same feelings in the car after the summer break.

"The cars are identical, and I've just been feeling very strong lately. I've worked on many areas from last year," he said.

"I feel much more confident lately with how to extract performance, and I've worked a lot with my engineers to understand this car because it's certainly not an easy car to understand and figure out how to drive on the limit consistently.

"So, why? Just hard work. Hard work from my engineers and from myself to improve me as a driver and improve my driving. That is the answer."

Sports.title: What does Arsenal interest and Real's Diomande pursuit mean for Vini Jr?
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior's Real Madrid future has been the subject of recent speculation, with Arsenal exploring a deal for the forward, but what could happen next?

What is the latest on this situation?

Brazil star Vinicius Jr, 26, is entering the final year of his contract at Real Madrid.

Negotiations over an extension have dragged on without a breakthrough, and it has caused increasing speculation over his future at the club.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Vinicius Jr's five best Real Madrid goals in LaLiga last season

That intensified last week when it emerged that Arsenal are interested in signing him this summer if he cannot agree a new deal at Real.

Meanwhile, Real Madrid have made a significant move for another winger - the exciting Ivory Coast international Yan Diomande at RB Leipzig.

It means doubts around Vinicius' future at the Bernabeu have grown over the past few days.

How serious is Arsenal's interest and can they afford him?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Could we see Vinicius Jr and Yan Diomande line up for Real Madrid next season, or is the Brazilian set for a move to the Premier League champions Arsenal?

Arsenal's interest is real but in the early stages and conditional on a number of factors, not least the cost - which would be significant should the door open for Vinicius to leave Real.

There have been no club-to-club talks, and there is no guarantee it progresses to a formal bid.

Arsenal, as newly-crowned Premier League champions, are looking to add another top-class forward despite signing Christos Tzolis. He was brought in to replace Leandro Trossard and there is doubt around the future of Gabriel Martinelli.

Last year they were keen on Vinicius's Real Madrid team-mate Rodrygo, while this summer Sky Sports News has reported their interest in Julian Alvarez and Morgan Rogers, who has since joined Chelsea from Aston Villa.

With one year left on his contract, the financial side of purchasing Vinicius would not be as severe as it previously has been - but it is worth remembering the sheer scale of an offer for the player two years ago from the Saudi Pro League.

Image: Vinicius Jr's stats from last season at Real Madrid

They were ready to pay him €1bn over five years and a transfer fee to Real Madrid of more than £300m (around €350m), which would have made him the most expensive transfer in history.

It would not cost anywhere near that much this time, but it gives a sense of what both Real and Vinicius were willing to forego in 2024.

Although the real figure is confidential, Vinicius is believed to earn around €15m to €17m net per year. That's around £247,000 to £279,000 per week after tax. To earn that amount in the UK, Arsenal would need to pay him somewhere between £450,000 and £500,000 per week.

That would make him far and away Arsenal's highest paid player. Bukayo Saka is widely believed to be the current highest paid on more than £300,000 per week.

A report in the Telegraph this morning claims Arsenal would be willing to go to £400,000. But that would still not equal Vinicius' current salary. Widespread reports in Spain claim part of the current impasse with Real is over his increased salary demands.

So is it just a dispute over a new contract?

Image: Vinicius Junior celebrates after scoring for Real Madrid in last season's Champions League clash with Manchester City at the Etihad

The situation has some of the classic hallmarks of a new contract dispute; reports of an impasse over salary demands, emerging Arsenal interest, further talks to come.

But there is no strong public evidence yet that Vinicius wants to leave Real Madrid for any reason, sporting or otherwise; no quotes, no interviews, no suggestive social media posts.

Real Madrid and - most importantly - new manager Jose Mourinho want him to stay and agree new terms. Sky Sports News reported on Monday morning that there will be further talks this week between Real and Vinicius' representatives, with Arsenal monitoring things closely.

Image: Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr is one of the most sought-after players in world football

Club president Florentino Perez is personally involved and has publicly expressed a desire for Vinicius to stay long term. Reports in Spain have long claimed that both parties have indicated a preference for him to remain at the club. Real Madrid do not want him to run down the deal into a free agent situation either.

Vinicius is more than just an outstanding left winger. He is a global superstar - and a Galactico in every sense. In that way he embodies everything about Real Madrid and fits right in.

Can the same be said about Arsenal? Signing such an icon has not been part of Mikel Arteta's Arsenal project so far, however exciting it might be to go in that direction.

Does Real Madrid's pursuit of Yan Diomande affect things?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande addressed speculation surrounding his future when he ws on World Cup duty - but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger

Sky Sports News has been told Real's proposed deal for Diomande has no real bearing on the Vinicius situation. It says nothing about their desire to keep Vinicius or not, and only suggests they see a front-three with both of these players in the team.

Diomande can play from the right wing too, and he only strengthens the attacking options of the biggest club in the world.

According to Spanish newspaper AS, the players whose futures would be affected by Diomande's arrival are more likely to be striker Goncalo Garcia - who is wanted by Fulham - and winger Brahim Diaz. Rodrygo is still recovering from a long-term injury, so Diomande has space to come into the team quickly, even at only 19 years old.

What is the most likely outcome?

At this stage, all signs still point to Vinicius signing a new deal with Real Madrid. The fact that they will all meet again this week to discuss this suggests this is the direction of travel.

It will most likely come down to how closely Vinicius' earnings can get to that of Mbappe and satisfy his Galactico status in the squad. Normally, you do not say no to Real Madrid.

Real would not want to go into the new season with his contract running down, and the resulting intensification of speculation in the media.

Arsenal's interest is only likely to become more concrete if the renewal fully fails - so this week is a crucial one.

Sports.title: The story of the 'non-League Wrexham' now chasing the EFL dream
Sports.content:
Having sold 40 per cent of influencer marketing agency, Goat, in 2021, Harry Hugo had made his fortune at 26 - and he realised that, by the age of 30, he would have the rare luxury of not needing to work again.

So, by his own admission, he chased moments of "instant gratification". But he also knew he needed to find a purpose.

One day, he and his friends - who had worked with him since he started his first business aged 16 - visited a Ferrari garage. He had his eyes on a 458 Spyder in black.

"My mate asked me why I was considering buying it," he tells Sky Sports.

Image: Farnham Town have earned three promotions in four seasons since Harry Hugo became chairman (Image: LJP Photos)

"My only answer was that it would be fun. That wasn't a good enough answer, so I challenged my mates to come up with something that would provide as much fun for the money.

"The first suggestion was, why don't we buy a football club - and I thought that was quite a good idea!"

The group built a matrix to rank the non-League clubs within a 50-mile radius of his home. Leatherhead came out on top, so Hugo followed the Tanners - then in the Isthmian Premier Division, one below the National League South - for six months.

Image: Hugo sold 40 per cent of influencer marketing agency Goat in 2021 and the remainder two years later (Image: LJP Photos)

When he met the board, there was scepticism, he says. "I get that as, one, it's unusual for a young guy wanting to go and spend loads of money on a football club and, two, there have been a lot of negative stories in non-League, where people have put loads of money in then walked away."

Hugo was left deflated when a deal to take over did not materialise, yet he soon realised he had not fallen in love with Leatherhead, but non-League in general and "the raw emotion, the old-school nature of football in its purest form."

Town takeover leads to back-to-back-to-back

Number two on the matrix was Farnham Town. Hugo had grown up in local area attended school in the town - which is around 11 miles from Guildford, Surrey - so there was a tie-in. The only downside? They were another two tiers down the pyramid.

But the board were instantly receptive and a deal was completed within five weeks.

Soon, the reality of what he had inherited caught up with him.

"When we walked in, it cannot be understated how s*** it was here," he says, overlooking the pitch at The Memorial Ground, which is looking in excellent condition, despite the intense recent heatwaves.

"It was the clubhouse, a stand behind the goal… and that was it. A concrete block wall around the side of the pitch and a fence across the top. I was embarrassed to bring my wife down here!"

Today, it is almost hard to believe it is the same stadium. But more on that shortly as, to understand why that is the case, one must look at Farnham's incredible rise, led on the pitch by manager Paul Johnson.

In 2022/23 - Hugo's first season - Farnham finished sixth in the Combined Counties Premier Division South.

In 2023/24, they won that same division with 108 points.

In 2024/25, they won the Isthmian South Central Division with 102 points.

Image: Paul Johnson has been in charge of Farnham Town since November 2022 (Image: LJP Photos)

And in 2025/26, they finished second to Walton & Hersham in the Southern League Premier Division South, before beating Gloucester City 5-1 in the play-off final to reach the National League South.

Before Hugo's arrival, the club had never played above the ninth tier of English football. In 2026/27, they will play in the sixth.

Do Farnham have any recognisble faces? Sam Hutchinson: Five Premier League games for Chelsea, 207 games for Sheffield Wednesday in all competitions

Brandon Mason: Two Premier League games for Watford, 36 League One games for Coventry City

Rakish Bingham: 64 Scottish Premiership games for Hamilton Academical

Billy Clifford: 31 League One games for Colchester United and Walsall, 43 League two games for Crawley Town

Aaron Kuhl: Six Championship games for Reading, five Scottish Premiership games for Dundee United

Wrexham links and the value of socials

Naturally, there have been comparisons to Wrexham, who are the most high-profile example of a club achieving back-to-back-to-back promotions, from the National League to the Sky Bet Championship.

"I'm OK with that!" says Hugo, with a laugh.

"Like them, we also care about media, brand, image, experience and the biggest thing is they brought people up; they made more National League and EFL teams look at themselves and think they could be doing it.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Reynolds and Rob Mac reflect on their five years as Wrexham owners.

"We're having the same impact on teams at step three, four, five and wondering, if they did it, why can't we?"

While the Red Dragons have their Disney+ series 'Welcome to Wrexham', Farnham produce 'Non-League Diaries', which is released weekly on YouTube.

Hugo harnessed his connections to get social media collective The Sidemen to sponsor the team in his first season, while last September, the club went viral after former Liverpool and England striker Peter Crouch walked out as a mascot as a forfeit for losing his Fantasy Football League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Due to a forfeit, Peter Crouch agreed to become Farnham Town's mascot - and drew a record attendance for the non-League side!

From 2023 until earlier this summer, Love Island runner-up Harry Cooksley was a key member of the squad and, on TikTok, they boast over 150,000 followers.

"Social media is huge commercially, from a fan engagement and brand-awareness point of view. It's weird the amount of people that know about Farnham Town," Hugo adds.

Image: Harry Cooksley (left) of Love Island fame played a key role in Farnham's rise (Image: LJP Photos)

"They might not have ever come, but they know Crouchy walked out in a full kit as a mascot or we won the play-off final 5-1 or we hold the British record for the most wins in a row in a league campaign. Other clubs have done things like it, but they can't get the message out; they can't tell the story.

"We've done a really good job of doing that and it's been a major focus because it's my background. It's the perfect distribution channel that allows us to tell that story."

Rapid rise forces need for rapid growth

Online, some accuse him of just throwing money at it. He accepts that was "a legitimate point" in his second year as getting out of the ninth tier became imperative.

"People who keep the lights on do an amazing job and make sure these non-League football clubs exist, then there's the people who are trying to push it forward. That's good for everybody," he says.

"Farnham doing things for the first time and being as successful as we have been on and off the pitch drives everybody to be better. People have gone from hating us to admiring us because they've seen someone who is genuinely invested in this and wants to do it sustainably for the long-term.

"I don't hide in a corporate box and I genuinely love football. I'm Farnham's number one fan, and the chairman second. I've never been an anxious person, but I hate the 90 minutes because it means so much to me, which is why I do commentary. It's like therapy to me because I'm so nervous!"

Farnham's rise on the pitch has put strain - a welcome one at that - on Hugo and those off the pitch. Each promotion has brought a nine-month deadline for the club to bring their stadium up to the requirements for that level. The official capacity is currently 2,300, but by March 31 2027, it needs to be 3,000.

But they have not focused solely on that this summer. There are impressive new stands, but the whole club has received a makeover of the highest order. The transformation is striking.

"It's constant money, but also planning. I love that, but I think it's really important for people to understand it's not just about winning on the pitch," Hugo says.

"There's so much you have to think about off the pitch if you're as successful as we've been. It's not just about throwing money at it; it's about being strategic.

"The nice thing is we're going to have brought a fanbase through that take nothing for granted because they've seen where we've come from. Hopefully everyone comes down to support the football club because we're going to need to put a lot of cash back in the coffers with the work we've done."

Speaking of cash, Hugo is incredibly transparent on social media with the financial side of things. He often posts details on X, highlighting the importance of the spend-per-head metric. Why?

"Because moving the dial from an average attendance of 1,000 to 1,500 is disproportionately harder than getting someone to spend £18, not £15, inside the ground. Once you get someone in and you give them opportunities to spend, that is way easier than trying to get someone brand new in.

"That's not necessarily about putting prices up, more giving them opportunities to spend on better things.

"That metric has improved massively since we've been involved, without the ticket prices going up much at all. We are a cheap day out."

The EFL is no longer just a pipe dream

Farnham's rise has been so quick that it is hard to believe they are only two promotions from Sky Bet League Two. The ambition to get there is significant - and growing.

"The biggest thing that drives me is that Surrey doesn't have an EFL team. That's ridiculous," says Hugo. "How doesn't one of the most affluent counties, so close to London, not have one of the 92 EFL teams?!

Surrey's top non-League teams National League: Sutton United, Woking

National League South: Dorking Wanderers, Farnham Town, Walton & Hersham

"Woking and Sutton are in the league above us and when we started, Sutton were in the EFL and we were in step five. Now there's one league between us. Who's to say Farnham can't get in ahead of all the others? Three years ago, I didn't even consider that.

"We know how to get promotions. I know it takes everything, so much stuff that people don't see, but we can actually stand up and say we think we can get to the EFL and we've proven we know how to do it, though we know it's going to get harder.

"We are obviously going to try and get promoted again this season because that's in our nature, but would it be the end of the world if we didn't? Absolutely not. But we've only ever been promoted, so it's going to be a weird feeling if we get to the end of the season and we don't have a pitch invasion!

One to keep an eye on? Local lad Owen Dean came through Farnham Town's youth ranks and has since become the club's prized asset.

The 23-year-old has played 202 games for the club since the 2021/22 season, scoring 87 goals and providing 39 assists.

"Some clubs will go through a chairman's lifetime and never have one - we've had four in four years. I'm OK with our pitch not being invaded this year! It means we'd have time to figure out our facility, get it ready, so it would be National League, EFL ready."

A long journey undoubtedly lies ahead, but it would take a brave person to bet against Hugo and Farnham, who have already changed perceptions of what a modern non-League club can be.

Several years on from that day in the Ferrari garage, it is certainly fair to say Farnham's young chairman has found the purpose he was seeking.

Sports.title: Real to hold further talks over Vinicius Jr's future this week
Sports.content:
Real Madrid will hold further talks with Vincius Junior's representatives about his future this week.

Those discussions will centre on finding an agreement over a new long-term contract.

Arsenal, who are aiming to strengthen their left-wing options this summer, are interested in Vinicius and are monitoring the situation closely.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Vinicius Jr's five best Real Madrid goals in LaLiga last season

Manager Jose Mourinho wants to keep the Brazil international and the club want him to sign new terms.

However, he has has entered the final year of his contract and if an agreement cannot be found on a new deal, Real could be open to selling, rather than lose him for free next summer.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at all of the reasons why Yan Diomande is high on the radar of clubs from across the world.

Sky Sports News has been told Real Madrid's proposed deal to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig has no bearing on Vinicius's situation.

Madrid are increasingly confident of completing a deal for Diomande this week after Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the race on Sunday.

Sky Sports News has reported for several months that the Premier League clubs interested in Diomande are Liverpool, Arsenal and Manchester City.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Yan Diomande says he is fully focused on the World Cup despite transfer speculation, but Sky Sports' Jay Bothroyd is not convinced by the Ivorian winger.

But he now looks destined for the Bernabeu, and Sky Sports News understands PSG are to resume their pursuit of Monaco's Maghnes Akliouche next.

Last week, Sky Sports News exclusively revealed that Liverpool had made an approach to Monaco for Akliouche, whom PSG will only bid for at the right price.

Liverpool are also interested in PSG winger Bradley Barcola, along with Arsenal, in what is an intensive and wide-ranging market for wingers this summer.

Sports.title: Doyle: Scandinavia can emulate Kyprios with Goodwood Cup win
Sports.content:
Our ambassador is previewing all five days of the Goodwood, beginning with an enthralling opening day on Tuesday, featuring the Goodwood Cup.

Scandinavia poised to retain cup crown

The eagerly anticipated re-match between SCANDINAVIA and Trawlerman in the Al Shaqab Goodwood Cup (3.35) on the opening day of the Qatar Goodwood Festival is one race I'm particularly excited about in what promises to be an amazing week on the Sussex Downs.

Aidan O'Brien's reigning champion got the better of a protracted duel with Godolphin's admirable veteran in the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and can confirm his superiority in the Group 1 showpiece which once again looks like being a two-horse battle.

Four years younger and arguably even better this year, he can emulate Aidan's Kyprios by winning the race twice and giving the master of Ballydoyle his fourth Goodwood Cup in five years.

Roger Varian's Yorkshire Cup winner Rahiebb makes more appeal than the rest but is up against it. He simply didn't stay the marathon trip in the Gold Cup but I can't see him laying a glove on the market leaders, even though he's dropping back half a mile.

Rejuvenated Qirat may be hard to peg back

If QIRAT gets out on the lead in the HKJC World Pool Lennox Stakes (3.00) at Goodwood I really don't see any of his rivals drawing him back.

Ralph Beckett's five-year-old, who sprung that massive surprise in last year's Sussex Stakes, impressed me from the front in the Group 3 Criterion Stakes at York last time when he wore a tongue tie for the first time.

Image: Qirat stunned Goodwood with success in the Sussex Stakes last term

He could be open to more improvement in a race that might not take a lot of winning this year and gets my vote ahead of Andrew Balding's Marvelman.

He ran a smashing race in the Chipchase at Newcastle last month on his return from a lengthy break and should be sharper this time. A Group 2 winner already, he needs to take a step forward but looks a serious danger while Witness Stand, who won this race for me last year, is better than he was able to show at Chester and can hopefully make another bold bid.

Amo colt can break his maiden in vintage

I nominated PIKACHU as a horse to follow after his big run at Newmarket so I'm not forsaking him on his re-appearance in the Coral Vintage Stakes (2.25) at Goodwood.

Charlie Johnston's Amo Racing colt galloped through the line strongly in the Superlative Stakes after hitting a flat spot and can break his maiden at the fourth time of asking over this seven furlong trip.

The likely favourite Al Hudaiba is highly talented as he showed when beating Pikachu in that Group 2 but is complicated, too, and it's interesting that Charlie Appleby reaches for the blinkers in an attempt to concentrate his mind.

A more reliable proposition may be Aidan O'Brien's Haffner, a promising son of Justify who built on his Curragh debut with a maiden win at Newmarket earlier this month. This is much tougher but he represents Team Ballydoyle for a good reason.

More to come from Burke's course winner

LIBERTY LANE, a Listed winner at Goodwood, has dropped to a tempting mark which makes him a danger to all in the opening Coral Chesterfield Cup Handicap (1.50) at Goodwood.

Karl Burke's 2024 Cambridgeshire winner hasn't raced off this mark in nearly two years and is well drawn under Clifford Lee in stall four. He hinted at a return to form at Sandown last time in first-time cheekpieces, which are retained for this assignment.

My husband Tom's (Marquand) mount Yabher is also capable of a bold show after bolting up over this course and distance in May but was disappointing at York last time so has something to prove in such a competitive handicap.

Lexington can Blitz them in sprint Handicap

The Coral Rewards Shaker Handicap (4.10) at Goodwood will be fast and furious and can go to the rapid LEXINGTON BLITZ, who ran a huge race in the Epsom Dash last month.

A course and distance winner, Robert Cowell's four-year-old looks well enough treated to win this off just a 1lb higher mark but don't under-estimate Richard Spencer's pair Run Boy Run and Twilight Calls.

Richard has a knack of winning big sprint handicaps and has enlisted the services of Ryan Moore's son Toby who claims an invaluable 7lb off Run Boy Run. He's well drawn in stall 17 for a race like this while Newmarket winner Twilight Calls remains well handicapped of a mark of 90 with the in-form Saffie Osborne in the saddle.

I'll be back with my thoughts on Wednesday's action at Goodwood, featuring the Group 1 Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes and the big juvenile sprint, the Group 3 Molecomb Stakes.

Hollie Doyle was speaking to Sky Sports Racing's Simon Mapletoft.
