Sports.title: Why Tottenham Women have provided distraction from the gloom of watching men’s team | Mark Burton
Sports.content:
The exciting football played by Tottenham’s women last season provided a much-needed antidote to the dreadful men’s team, who not only flirted with relegation but took it out on a dinner date, looked deep into its eyes and started to plan a future together.

Fortunately, that relationship fizzled out and fans were able to “celebrate” at the end of the season as Premier League status was secured. Meanwhile, Spurs achieved their highest points tally in the Women’s Super League. Highlights included a 7-2 goal-fest against Aston Villa, a mind-bending FA Cup penalty shootout win against London City Lionesses (where the first 17 penalties were successfully slotted home) and a stream of wonder goals including a 40-yard screamer from Cathinka Tandberg.

As the men crumbled and the prospect of Lincoln visiting the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium loomed, my Spurs men’s WhatsApp group of season-ticket holders and members went into meltdown. “Spurs crisis hotline,” I’d answer, before being unable to provide answers to pressing questions: are all those passes around the penalty area really necessary? Why aren’t Spurs signing players to plug the injury gaps?

Thankfully, there was a distraction from the gloom because three years ago my wife, son and I became Tottenham Women season-ticket holders. This move was inspired by England’s Lionesses reaching the World Cup final in 2023. We were visiting family in Australia and when England beat Colombia 2-1 in the quarter-finals, several of Colombia fans made detours to shake our hands in the Brisbane fan zone. There were about 2,000 of them and approximately 20 England fans. This, I thought, is the sort of football experience I want my son to enjoy.

That positive vibe has continued as we’ve followed Tottenham. So what explains their recent improvements? The first factor was Martin Ho’s appointment as the head coach last year. Before joining he had been an assistant at Manchester United and the head coach of the Norwegian side Brann. Behind-the-scenes chatter suggests players like and respect him.

View image in fullscreen Martin Ho’s arrival as Tottenham head coach ahead of last season transformed the team’s fortunes. Photograph: Ben Whitley/PA

He has connected with supporters by wandering occasionally through the “Legends Lounge” at Leyton Orient (where Spurs play most of their women’s home games) for pre-match chats. But the most important part is that Ho has Spurs playing attacking and organised football. The players look certain of their roles and clear on how they can support each other.

Another factor has been the players who joined. The midfielder Olivia Holdt was Spurs’ top scorer last season and Toko Koga has been a stalwart in central defence. Then came the squad augmentation in January with the arrival of Signe Gaupset, who loves to charge through the midfield with the ball.

The way Ho worked with the existing players has also been key. In 2024-25 the team significantly underperformed, finishing one place above relegation, which led to the departure of then-head coach Robert Vilahamn. Last season Spurs won five of their first six games. It is unknown what Ho said to encourage established players back to their best, but it was likely not an Igor Tudor-like speech where he told them they couldn’t attack, couldn’t defend and couldn’t run.

View image in fullscreen Cathinka Tandberg (right) scored one of the goals of last season against Everton. Photograph: Ryan Browne/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

Tottenham were good at attacking, defending and running all season, and it was a pleasure to watch Eveliina Summanen, Amanda Nildén, Lize Kop, Drew Spence and Clare Hunt.

There were a couple of games where they were thumped by Manchester City, but City have Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw, who has a better goals-per-game ratio than Erling Haaland. They also won the league ahead of Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester United. These four clubs dominate the WSL and Spurs finished fifth behind these heavyweights. Breaking into the top four seems a real possibility in the next year or two.

Within days of last season ending, Spurs signed the highly-rated Netherlands international Caitlin Dijkstra from Wolfsburg to bolster the defence and Germany’s Shekiera Martinez, who impressed as a clinical striker at a mediocre West Ham. Other proven players have followed, including Kirsty Hanson from Aston Villa and Alice Sombath from OL Lyonnes.

It has been sad to say goodbye to Bethany England and lAshleigh Neville. Neville’s desire to move closer to home by transferring to Leicester was understandable but it is perplexing that England, Spurs’ record goalscorer, wasn’t given at least a one-year extension.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The side at the start of the season will look very different from the one we began supporting three years ago but what remains constant is the friendship and passion of our fellow season-ticket holders.

View image in fullscreen Bethany England’s departure from Tottenham at the end of last season was an emotional affair. Photograph: Javier García/Tottenham Hotspur FC/Shutterstock

Their knowledge of football is extraordinarily deep. Many have been Spurs men and women fans for years, writing blogs, recording podcasts and punishing themselves by going to West Ham to stand in the rain and wind. These fans have loved Spurs women from the days when a smattering of them watched Broxbourne Ladies, as the club were then, working their way up the leagues.

Another bonus of watching the women’s game is the atmosphere. Fans will vent their frustration and respectfully inquire whether the referee has recently attended a well-known high street opticians, but the swearing and anger often exhibited at the men’s games is largely absent.

Before each game fans decorate the stands with banners of Spurs players adorned with the Progress Pride flag. This visualisation of LGBTQIA+ identity shows that everyone is welcome. I hadn’t paid much attention to this until starting to support Spurs Women and it has made me much more aware of football’s potential as a positive agent for change.

Women’s football may be fractionally slower than the men’s but the games are fast-moving and VAR-less. This results in the occasional refereeing howler but it is preferable to waiting in the stands for five minutes wondering what is going on.

This season, hopefully there will be even more people going to matches and enjoying the experience of supporting the women’s game. It is difficult to recommend coming to Spurs more highly, but other women’s football teams are available.

Mark Burton is a Tottenham Women season-ticket holder

Sports.title: Fifa president Gianni Infantino accuses critics of spreading hate at World Cup
Sports.content:
The Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, has hit back at critics of the World Cup, accusing them of spreading hate and false narratives while defending the tournament ⁠as a success that celebrated ⁠unity, safety and inclusion.

In ​an open letter published on Monday, Infantino said detractors had overlooked the joy and togetherness experienced by millions of fans around the world who witnessed the tournament, ⁠won by Spain and staged in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

“You were so consumed by hate and criticism that you missed it all,” said the 56-year-old. “To those behind their pens and papers, behind ⁠their screens spreading hate and false rumours, I want to say that while you are sitting behind, we at Fifa are ​on the front lines organising, working hard, and delivering ‌the best show in the ‌world. We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100% safety and security, only joy and happiness.”

Fifa faced criticism about a number of issues ‌during the World Cup, including US visa restrictions affecting supporters and officials from several countries and concerns for teams from conflict-hit regions. Infantino’s letter followed scrutiny of Fifa’s suspension of an automatic one-match ban imposed on the US striker Folarin Balogun after the intervention of Donald Trump. Officiating decisions in Argentina’s last-16 victory over Egypt also received criticism, most strongly from the Egypt manager, Hossam Hassan.

“Potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent ​decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues worldwide,” Infantino said in his letter. “It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.“

The Somali referee, Omar Artan, was barred from entering the US despite having a valid visa while the Iran team and staff were subject to difficult travel restrictions imposed on them by the US government as a consequence of the war between the two countries.

“Iran ​entered the United States without ‌incident or conflict. The ​Iranian team received visas ​to enter because football is about peace. It’s not about politics,” said Infantino. “Countries facing serious health issues or other challenges were granted visas.”

Infantino’s letter is likely to lead to further criticism and ridicule of the man who on the eve of the previous World Cup in Qatar declared: “Today I feel Qatari. Today I feel Arabic. Today I feel African. Today I feel gay. Today I feel disabled. Today I feel a migrant worker.”

Sports.title: Andrea Pirlo out of running for Italy job but defends deal with Russian betting firm
Sports.content:
Andrea Pirlo has confirmed he is no longer in line to coach Italy, with his sponsorship deal with a Russian betting firm believed to behind the development. Several Italian politicians have raised concerns about Pirlo’s role as an ambassador for Fonbet, saying the national team coach should not have conflicting views on Italy’s support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

Writing on Instagram on Monday, Pirlo said he “heard last night that I’m no longer the candidate for the Italy national team job”. The former Azzurri midfielder had previously insisted the Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is “exclusively for commercial and sports purposes”, adding: “Attributing a political significance to that collaboration means attributing beliefs to me that I have never expressed and don’t belong to me.”

Pirlo added: “Over the past few days, I have watched with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of head coach of the Italian national team. Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always carried out my work in full compliance with the laws of the countries where I have worked and with the contracts I have ‌signed.“

Despite Pirlo having the backing of the new Italian football federation technical director, ‌Paolo Maldini, the controversy has created significant friction among politicians. “After yet another defeat and another missed World Cup qualification, Italian football desperately needed a cultural, ethical and managerial revolution. The choice of Andrea Pirlo goes in the exact opposite direction,” said Pina Picierno, a vice-president of the European parliament, on social media.

Ignazio La Russa, the head of the Senate and a member of the prime minister Giorgia Meloni’s party, expressed doubts over Pirlo’s possible appointment. On Saturday, La Russa said: “Of course ​I am an Italy fan ​and Pirlo was a great champion, but as a coach, it is a leap in the dark.”

Carlo Calenda, the leader of the Azione party, was even more direct in his criticism. “Anyone who is or has been promoting Russia after 2022 should not hold national office,” he said.

The FIGC turned to Pirlo – who had been prepared to leave his job as coach of Dubai United – after failing to land Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti in their search for a successor to Gennaro Gattuso, who left his post by mutual consent in April after Italy failed to qualify for a third World Cup in succession.

The former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are now being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Arsenal and Liverpool battle it out for Bradley Barcola?
Sports.content:
Like baggy trousers, small sunglasses and leopard print, transfer rumours are back in a big way. And there can be no doubting the transfer ambition of the Premier League champions, Arsenal, who are eyeing up either Vinícius Júnior or Bradley Barcola as a deluxe Leandro Trossard replacement.

One sticking point for the Gunners is the former’s apparent desire to stay put at Real Madrid, while Liverpool appear to be favourites for Barcola if they can muster the £145m Paris Saint-Germain are demanding for their fourth-best forward. The path may become clear for Vinícius to leave the Bernabéu, however, with the club closing in on a deal for the Ivorian World Cup sensation Yan Diomande. Perennial prospect Endrick has also been touted for a move away from Madrid this summer.

Staying with wingers, Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye is coveted by the Saudi Pro League’s Al-Hilal, while a potential fight for the signature of Pedro Neto could be upon us, with a few Saudi clubs in the mix with Liverpool and Manchester City. Why on earth Chelsea would want to sell such a talent is a good question, but balancing the books at Stamford Bridge is imperative after the £117m splurge on Morgan Rogers. Forgotten City wide man Savinho could be heading to Tottenham to make room for any new arrival at the Etihad.

Manchester United are staying out of the scramble for wide guys and instead concentrating their efforts on centre-forwards. If Joshua Zirzkee leaves this summer – with Juventus targeting the Dutchman – Ollie Watkins, 31 before the year is out, a possible replacement. United could ship out their young left-back Harry Amass to Coventry, either permanently or on loan, which has got some fans very excited about the possible arrival of Lewis Hall.

João Palhinha’s future has been the subject of some speculation. Bayern Munich’s sporting director, Christoph Freund, has made no bones about trimming their squad, paving the way for the Portuguese to join Aston Villa, but the midfielder would prefer to stay put. Mind you, he previously said he wanted to extend his loan stay at Spurs. Marco Silva – a former manager of the midfielder at Fulham – wants him at Benfica on loan.

Remember Mohamed Salah? Well the Egyptian King is still without a club after leaving Liverpool and enjoying some holiday after the World Cup. His next stop could well be Besiktas, with a stunning Darwin Núñez reunion on the cards if the Uruguayan also joins the Turkish club from Al-Hilal. Plenty of Saudi clubs are still on the Salah case and even Sporting Kansas from MLS have been linked.

Sports.title: Real Madrid ready to seal deal for Yan Diomande after PSG pull out of move
Sports.content:
Real Madrid look to have won the race for RB Leipzig’s coveted winger, Yan Diomande, after Paris Saint-Germain withdrew from the bidding war.

The Ivory Coast international has been the subject of an intense transfer saga this summer, following a breakout season in the Bundesliga and an impressive World Cup campaign.

The 19-year-old was linked with a move with Liverpool early in the window, before the player’s camp revealed he would instead prioritise a switch to Paris. However, with Real now moving ahead of PSG, Diomande looks set for the Bernabéu with the reported fee “well in excess” of €100m (£85m).

The breakthrough comes just days after Leipzig rejected Madrid’s opening proposal of €90m plus €10m in add-ons. Diomande, who has reportedly already agreed personal terms with Real, is now expected to fly to the Spanish capital for a medical.

The deal will come as a blow for PSG, who looked to be the frontrunners, with many reports suggesting they were his first choice if he did leave Germany. However, the European champions were unable to agree a fee and issued a statement on Sunday insisting they will not break their “principles”.

The statement read: “Paris Saint-Germain has this evening formally withdrawn its interest in and bids for Yan Diomande. PSG will not break its principles of rational financial management and squad balance.”

Meanwhile, Liverpool have turned their attention to PSG’s Bradley Barcola as they continue to search for wingers.

Sports.title: Chiesa wants ‘new chapter’ with Iraola after frustrating time under Slot at Liverpool
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa has said he wants “a new chapter” at Liverpool with Andoni Iraola following a frustrating time under Arne Slot and claimed the club were lucky to qualify for the Champions League last season.

The Liverpool forward has been linked with a return to Italy this summer having struggled for minutes during his two years at Anfield. Chiesa made 36 appearances for Slot last season, a healthy return on paper, but only five were starts.

He started one Premier League game last season despite the problems Liverpool had in attack because of injuries to Alexander Isak and Hugo Ekitiké, and his last start came in the FA Cup fourth-round win against Brighton on 14 February. A change of head coach, Chiesa hopes, will herald a change in fortune as a Liverpool player.

“It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year,” said the 28-year-old, who produced a fine finish in Liverpool’s 4-2 friendly defeat of Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. “Maybe there have been too many fresh starts [for him]. But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager.

“Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best. Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach whether he wanted me to play or not. Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer had his gameplans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football. This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.”

Chiesa admits he has not discussed his future with Iraola since the Basque coach succeeded Slot in June. “The only conversations I had were about pressing and tactics,” he said. “He put me striker against Sunderland and he wants me there.”

But the Italy international, who has two years remaining on his Liverpool contract, claimed his priority is to prove himself to the head coach rather than seek a return to Serie A. Como and former club Juventus have been linked with a move for the forward.

“Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool,” said Chiesa. “I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see. At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.”

View image in fullscreen Federico Chiesa scored for Liverpool against Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday. Photograph: George Walker IV/AP

Liverpool secured Champions League qualification on the final day of a troubled season in May in what proved to be Slot’s final game in charge. Chiesa insists that was no cause for celebration at a club of Liverpool’s stature and there must be improvement next term.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The forward said: “Liverpool deserves more. Two years ago, we were Premier League champions. Last year, we almost went out of the Champions League spots. We were battling for fifth, which was enough at the time but as we know usually only four go in. We were lucky.

“It was a tough season last year and this season we need to do better, in the Champions League as well. We went out to PSG. We want to go further in that competition and then we want to do even better in the Premier League as well.”

Chiesa also hopes to reclaim his place in the national team next season, having missed out on several squads recently. Italy are now searching for a new head coach, having failed to qualify for the World Cup under Gennaro Gattuso.

Chiesa said: “The situation is that I spoke to the manager a few times, Gattuso, and I was not ready physically at the time. When I got back in March, unfortunately I got injured. But I am looking forward to playing for the national team. I have won with the national team [the European Championship]. It is always nice to play and win for your national team.”

Sports.title: Teamwork, tactics and data: behind the scenes at Wigan’s pre-season training
Sports.content:
“This is the only rule I’m going to have for yous all season: ‘team first’,” says Gary Caldwell. The Wigan head coach’s Scottish accent booms over the gentle hum of a projector in a darkened classroom at the club’s Christopher Park training ground. “That is the one thing that we cannot ever go against,” he says, pointing to a slide on screen. “The team is the most important aspect of everything we do.”

Three rows of professional athletes listen intently, keen to learn not only what the day holds, but about the 10 months ahead.

Some shall see it through to next May, others may leave before the 2026-27 League One campaign begins on 14 August, and new faces will be added.

It is pre-season and before the interminable football carousel begins spinning, there is much work ahead.

View image in fullscreen Gary Caldwell talks tactics with his squad. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

The meeting is short, just long enough for Caldwell to zip through a handful of tactical points. As he speaks, the head of performance analysis, Lauren Jones, plays clips from their “best practice bank”.

Because she, Caldwell, and the first-team coach, David Perkins, joined from Exeter only in February (the physio, Michael McBride, and goalkeeping coach, Kevin Miller, followed this summer), the bank is small, but growing.

There are myriad general football clips that Caldwell could use, but he values “the lads seeing players in Wigan shirts doing what we’re asking of them”.

Perkins relays the day’s plan – a 1.5km time trial, several drills, some out-of-possession shape work and an afternoon weights session – before the class is dismissed and told to reassemble on the grass 45 minutes later.

There is no idling, though, the entire squad soon beginning self‑led pre-activation (in old money, warming up).

Bodies are strewn across the in-house gym with bands, benches and foam rollers used as aids to contort muscles and limbs.

Wigan’s facility is, by modern standards, modest but functional. A printed sign sets out the simple rules: £50 fines for anyone with a phone, wearing sliders or sulking.

When the centre-back James Carragher discovers the Guardian will be joining the morning’s run, a sanction of double that amount is declared should anyone not beat the guest journalist. At 10.55am, the strength and conditioning lead, Matthew Barrow, explains that the run consists of 15 pitch lengths with 14 turns. “Your choice lads – boots or trainers, but I recommend boots so you don’t lose time on the turn.”

“I’m glad I’m not doing it,” Caldwell says, laughing. “It’s a maximal test and anything like that involves people pushing themselves.”

Could you survive a professional football pre-season fitness test? – video

It is not the squad’s first testing of pre-season. Their first day back involved a series of body and strength tests “designed to provide us with a benchmark”, Caldwell says. “If they get injured, we know where we need to get them back to.”

But the days of players reporting back overweight are long gone, with only a small number a smidge above their optimum numbers during body composition testing. “That will all have been gone with the first week or so,” Caldwell says.

Running for running’s sake is also past practice. Instead, Barrow and the sports scientist Jack Craigie will use the run data to get each individual’s maximum aerobic speed. “From that, we individualise all the running they’ll do,” Craigie says. “For example, if we have a volume session planned, rather than giving a generic number of lengths, we set individual distances based on their results. That way they all get the same stimulus.”

By 11am, the players are jogging through a warm-up lap. According to the sign-in sheet outside the staff offices, some arrived on site three hours ago. The physio hub just off the gym has had a steady stream of visitors, a mix of prevention and cure. Breakfast was enjoyed in a canteen acting as a social space for staff and players.

It marks a leisurely start when measured against some mornings. With no tour plans, Caldwell is finding alternative ways to avoid monotony. Several 6am meets precede 3.5km runs to a partner gym for intense, Hyrox-style workouts. With players working in trios, staff are as interested in attitude and demeanour as fitness.

View image in fullscreen The players take part in various training drills. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

“We’re taking the group out of their comfort zone to see how they react under a bit of pressure,” Caldwell says. “We can look at the energy someone brings at 6am when others are tired. That will help us know who is going to pick the group up when we’re a little fatigued.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Those sessions also promote Caldwell’s “team first” ethos. “When you’re ‘off’ you still have a role to play,” he says. “Are you helping your pal get in and out of the straps on the rower more quickly? We want to see how they react in that situation. Come November, when it is cold and we’re struggling in a game, we can remind them of these sessions.”

A late-morning run feels tame by comparison, albeit after several pitch lengths that naive notion is dispelled. No one loses £100 to the club kitty.

Soon the footballs are out and the group is split into two groups for a series of drills. The energy is impressive, with Max Power, who recently rejoined Wigan for a third spell, among the tone setters.

In one exercise he encourages a junior teammate to make a pass, only for a defender to block the space. Rather than get frustrated or dish out abuse, Power immediately finds another opportunity to tee up a similar ball and praises a successful outcome. “The better the player, the less stick they give people, I find,” says one staff member. “They want everyone to improve.”

The staff’s challenge is to manage the intensity, building towards a peak. Caldwell avoids directly asking players to hold back, but with a drone monitoring everything and GPS data available in real time, sessions can be adjusted accordingly. Sometimes it is as simple as moving cones in a few yards.

For one drill, tape on the grass creates a dozen boxes, within which three banks of four must work to create and find gaps. “Football is sometimes about the chaos,” Caldwell says, grinning. “If we give them more space, they will use it.”

View image in fullscreen Wigan use the in-house gym during a break from the action on the pitch. Photograph: Dom Maltby/The Guardian

Building towards a peak is also Wigan’s aim. Supporters want a return to the relatively recent success, which is natural after eight seasons as an established Premier League side. That ended in 2013 – the year they lifted the FA Cup at Wembley with Caldwell in the squad.

Four Championship relegations and three League One promotions have followed, including in Caldwell’s first full season in management. That was 2015-16 and the third-tier title was claimed.

Caldwell’s immediate challenge last season was avoiding relegation from League One, and patience is required for the next step.

After lunch, the day concludes in the gym with a short, sharp, upper body strength session. In one corner, pull-ups, in another perfectly formed jackknives.

“Once the season begins, training loads are consistent around games,” Barrow says. “But with the time in here now we can really chase that hypertrophy.”

Pre-season was once, in effect, punishment for a summer well enjoyed, but in 2026 is a meticulous, data-driven, foundation-building exercise.

The payoff will become known only next May.

Sports.title: Régis Le Bris says Chelsea’s pursuit of Sunderland captain Xhaka is ‘closed’
Sports.content:
Régis Le Bris has declared Chelsea’s pursuit of Granit Xhaka “closed” and insisted there is no prospect of Sunderland selling their influential captain this summer.

Xhaka played a major role in Sunderland qualifying for the Europa League on their return to the Premier League last season, prompting Chelsea to make an £8m bid for the 33-year-old this month. Xabi Alonso, the new Chelsea manager, is keen to be reunited with his former midfielder at Bayer Leverkusen.

Sunderland, however, immediately rejected Chelsea’s bid and their head coach has emphatically denied that a deal could be revisited before the end of the transfer window.

“No, this topic is closed,” said Le Bris after Sunderland’s 4-2 pre-season friendly defeat by Liverpool in Nashville on Saturday. “He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland. He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. Great leader.”

Despite the added demands of European football next season Sunderland have been quiet in the transfer market, signing only the experienced Belgium defender Thomas Meunier on a free from Lille so far. Le Bris anticipates further additions but admits this summer will be nothing like the rebuilding work before Sunderland’s return to the top flight 12 months ago.

The Sunderland head coach added: “It’s going to be quiet. Under the radar, right? I won’t give you information. Because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it’s really important to be quiet because otherwise it’s a mess. And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. It won’t be the case this year. We’ll see what will happen.”

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi labelled world’s second best player in position despite one World Cup appearance
Sports.content:
Martin Zubimendi labelled world’s second best player in position despite one World Cup appearance

Spain boss Luis de La Fuente heralded Martin Zubimendi as the 'second best' midfielder on the planet.

Speaking to Spanish broadcaster RTVE, De la Fuente made the bold claim during a passionate defence of Rodri.

3 Zubimendi was lavished with praise by De la Fuente despite his reduced World Cup role Credit: Getty

"With all due respect, and I don’t mean to offend anyone, I said that doubting Rodri was an insult to football intelligence, obviously," De la Fuente said.

"He’s the best player in the world in his position, knowing that we have Martin Zubimendi behind him, who is also another great player, surely the second best in the world.

"But we knew we had to follow a process and the deadlines we had set.

"He improved game by game, and the fact is that Rodri, even at 50 per cent, is better than many other players."

How much did Zubimendi play at the World Cup?

Despite anointing Zubimendi with such an accolade, De la Fuente only let the midfielder loose on just one occasion at the World Cup.

That came in the form of a 21-minute appearance off the bench in the final against Argentina, which La Roja won 1-0 courtesy of Ferran Torres' strike in extra time.

But for every other match, Zubimendi remained an unused substitute.

Instead, De la Fuente's midfield triumvirate featured a combination of Rodri, Fabian Ruiz, Pedri and Dani Olmo.

Zubimendi's Arsenal teammate Mikel Merino was the only one outside of the regular midfield quartet to have made a start, which came in Spain's 1-0 win over Uruguay to round out the group stage.

De la Fuente's midfield selections were vindicated in the best way possible though as Spain reclaimed the World Cup for the first time in 16 years.

3 Zubimendi won the World Cup alongside Arsenal teammates Merino and David Raya Credit: Getty

Pivotal to La Roja's charge was Rodri, who was awarded the Golden Ball as the best player of the tournament.

Ruiz, who only started four of Spain's eight matches, also caught the eye, with his performances rocketing him into contention for the Ballon d'Or.

De la Fuente drops major hint over future as Spain boss

But most of the praise belonged to De la Fuente, who has now led Spain to three major titles in his tenure thanks to their Nations League triumph in 2023 and Euro 2024 success over England.

And the 65-year-old, who has only lost just three of his 49 matches in charge of the national team, admitted he could be willing to stick around for the 2030 World Cup, which Spain will co-host alongside Portugal and Morocco, with games also to be held in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay.

"A while ago, a journalist asked me this question, 'Luis, would you like to be at the World Cup in Spain,'" De la Fuente said.

"Don't put it in the headline, but if you ask me., how could I not like it?

3 The 65-year-old has been in charge of Spain since December 2022 Credit: AFP

"It's the greatest honour a coach can have, to be the manager of your country, to lead the Spanish national team. How could I not like it?

"I'm also very short-term thinking, and I'm focused on the matches we have in September and October. The next World Cup seems a long way off."

De la Fuente's side return to action following their World Cup triumph against England in a Nations League clash at Wembley on September 26.

Sports.title: York City appoint sacked League Two boss hours after axing Stuart Maynard
Sports.content:
York City have appointed Scott Lindsey as their new head coach.

The announcement comes less than 24 hours after the club sensationally axed Stuart Maynard just over a week before the new season.

4 Lindsey is back in the dugout - months after being axed by Crawley Credit: Rex

York's statement on Lindsey's appointment

"Lindsey joins the Minstermen ahead of our return to League Two, bringing with him a vast wealth of experience working across the EFL," a York City statement read.

"An experienced League Two manager, Lindsey has previously taken spells at Swindon Town as well as taking charge of Crawley Town, where he guided the club to promotion from League Two via the play-offs.

"He has also held a role at Milton Keynes Dons at this level. His coaching career began with a caretaker spell at Lincoln City before enjoying non-league success with Chatham Town.

"In his playing days, Lindsey spent time across the EFL and non-league pyramid, including a spell at local sides Goole Town and Bridlington Town.

"Lindsey will be assisted by assistant manager Joao Alves and first-team coach Gary Elphick, and will take charge of his first game against his former club Crawley Town on Monday, 3rd August."

The 54-year-old's appointment marks his fourth different managerial role since September 2023, with his last stop coming at Crawley who axed him last March after he oversaw their relegation from League One to League Two.

Lindsey has large shoes to follow considering predecessor Maynard guided York back into the EFL after a record-breaking 108-point season culminated in the National League title.

Maynard, who only took charge in August 2025, ended the Minstermen’s decade-long hiatus from the division at the first time of asking.

York have now confirmed that a ‘difference in vision’ between Maynard and the board has seen him leave his role as head coach.

York City part ways with manager

A statement read: "York City Football Club can confirm that Stuart Maynard will be leaving his role as first team manager, with immediate effect.

4 York City confirmed manager Maynard's departure on Sunday Credit: Getty

"This has not been an easy decision, and it is not one the board has taken lightly. Ultimately, it comes down to a difference in direction and vision for the football club.

"We recognise that, from the outside, this may look like a strange or difficult decision to understand. But we believe that in the long term, the football club will be in a stronger position because of it, another step towards the vision we, as custodians of this club, believe will deliver sustained success.

"Like every one of you, we love this football club, and we would never make a decision we didn’t believe was in its best long-term interests.

"We hope our track record of improving year on year has earned us a degree of trust, and we understand that not everyone will agree with, or fully understand, this decision right away.

"We would like to thank Stuart for his contribution to York City FC and wish him well for the future."

York's announcement came just two days after a 2-2 draw against Steven Gerrard's former Saudi Arabian side, Al-Ettifaq.

4 York earned promotion to the fourth tier in the most dramatic of final-day shootouts Credit: Getty

The Minstermen have just one more pre-season friendly scheduled, a home clash with League One Peterborough United, on Tuesday.

York then get their season underway in a Carabao Cup preliminary round tie with Crawley Town on Monday, August 3.

The Yorkshire outfit are one of four clubs involved in the extra round of the EFL competition - owing to the fact that nine Premier League teams will compete in Europe this season.

Their League Two campaign then kicks off 12 days later on Saturday, August 15 at home to Bristol Rovers.

York were only recently told that their 8,500-capacity stadium, which is shared with rugby league team York Knights, is too small to match the club's ambitions.

Under Maynard, York secured promotion back to the EFL in one of the most dramatic final days of the season ever.

4 Maynard led York City to the National League title in April and has left three months later Credit: Getty

Just one point separated York and rivals Rochdale ahead of the two sides facing each other for a winner-takes-all title showdown.

Rochdale scored what they thought was the decisive goal in the fifth minute of stoppage time, only for their rivals to grab an equaliser eight minutes later through Josh Stones to send them straight up.

The Dale went on to secure promotion as well through the playoffs, coming from two down to beat Boreham Wood on penalties.

Sports.title: ‘Topic is closed’ – Chelsea issued final hands-off warning following rejected bid
Sports.content:
Chelsea have been told by Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris that club captain Granit Xhaka is categorically not for sale.

talkSPORT understands Xhaka was the subject of an £8million opening bid from Chelsea in June, with new boss Xabi Alonso keen to reunite with a key figure from his Bayer Leverkusen reign.



4 Xhaka proved pivotal in Sunderland securing a Europa League spot last season

However, this offer was immediately rejected, which was said to have been deemed 'unacceptable' by the Black Cats.

It was also suggested Sunderland wouldn't entertain any further offers for their skipper, with the club under no pressure to sell.

Chelsea are yet to submit an improved offer for Xhaka, who has drawn interest after playing a major role in his team's qualification for the Europa League last season.



The Swiss captain returned to the Premier League with Sunderland last summer after two years at Leverkusen under Alonso.

Staying put

It now appears that Xhaka's future lies at the Stadium of Light, with manager Le Bris reiterating the Black Cats' not for sale stance.



Speaking after his side's 4-2 friendly defeat to Liverpool, Le Bris said: “No, this topic is closed.

“He has been really clear about his future. He loves Sunderland, he wants to stay in Sunderland.



"He wants to make the future of Sunderland. He is a good captain. Great leader.”

New Chelsea boss Alonso had keen on a reunion with ex-Arsenal star Xhaka, who starred in Leverkusen's unbeaten Bundesliga glory under him in 2024.

But with the 33-year-old now looking set to stay on Wearside, his demands will be greater in the upcoming season as he prepares to lead his side in Europe.

4 Alonso has been keen to reunite with Xhaka Premier League after previous success together in Germany Credit: AFP



4 Xhaka was immediately made captain after joining Sunderland last summer Credit: Getty

Xhaka played 34 league games for Sunderland in the 2025/26 campaign after joining the club, instantly making a huge impact on and off the pitch as they remarkably went on to finish in seventh spot.

And despite the added strain of Europa League football next term, Le Bris insisted his side won't be strengthening as heavily in this transfer window as they did last summer.

Ahead of their return to the Premier League last term, the Black Cats recruited heavily, signing 15 new players.



But they have been quiet so far this summer, with only Belgium defender Thomas Meunier arriving on a free following his Lille release, and Le Bris admitted fans won't see a huge rebuild in the coming weeks.

The Sunderland head coach added: “It’s going to be quiet. Under the radar, right?

"I won’t give you information, because I think we are working hard behind the scenes, and it’s really important to be quiet because otherwise it’s a mess.

4 Alonso has overseen over £200m in summer signings in his first summer at Chelsea Credit: Getty



"And we are looking at probably a different transfer window if you compare with last season. We had to sign 14 new players. It won’t be the case this year. We’ll see what will happen.”

Busy Blues

With Chelsea seemingly out of the race to sign Xhaka, they have already set about pursuing other midfield targets.

talkSPORT recently revealed that the Blues had seen a £64m bid for Alex Scott rejected by Bournemouth, with Arsenal and Manchester United also keen on the young Englishman.

The west London side have shown they mean business so far this summer as they prepare for a new era under Alonso.



Morgan Rogers arrived from Aston Villa in a £117m deal to add to their wealth of attacking midfield options, which also features Cole Palmer, while they are also keen to keep hold of Enzo Fernandez.

Winger Geovany Quenda has officially joined from Sporting Lisbon - along with striker Emmanuel Emegha from Strasbourg - with Chelsea also forking out £45m on Italian right-back Marco Palestra from Atalanta.

Sports.title: ‘Great bitterness’ – Andrea Pirlo denied new manager’s job due to Russian betting company links
Sports.content:
Italy football legend Andrea Pirlo has confirmed he is no longer in the running to take charge of his national team.

The 47-year-old, who was part of the last Azzurri side to lift the World Cup as a player in 2006, left the Italian federation unhappy over his commercial ties to a Russian betting company.



6 Pirlo has been removed from the running due to commercial ties with Russia Credit: Fonbet

Pirlo had emerged as the leading candidate to succeed Gattuso after former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola turned down the post.

The AC Milan icon had strong support from newly-appointed FIGC technical director Paolo Maldini and his adviser Leonardo.

However, the fallout from Pirlo's role as a global ambassador for Russia's largest bookmaker, Fonbet, led to political resistance.



Pirlo will not be Italy's new head coach

“Out of respect for the institutions, the federation and everybody involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now,” Pirlo wrote in a statement on his Instagram story.

“However, after learning last night that I am no longer a candidate for the Italy national team head coach position, I feel it is necessary to clarify a few points.



“Over the past few days, I have watched with great bitterness as the debate regarding my name and the possibility of my taking on the role of Italy national team head coach unfolded.

“Throughout my career, first as a player and then as a coach, I have always performed my duties with full respect of the laws of the countries I have worked in and the contracts I signed.



“The professional collaboration that is the subject of recent controversy came about as part of my working experience in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature. Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing convictions to me that I have never expressed and that I do not hold.

“I wish to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the respect and faith that they showed in me. I know their competence, their seriousness, and the love that they have always dedicated to Italian football.

“However, it is regrettable that a decision based on sporting grounds was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing motives and intentions to my name that never existed. My love for Italy does not depend on a job. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.”

6 Former Italy captain Pirlo made over 100 appearances for his country Credit: AFP



Why did Guardiola reject Italy?

Guardiola was the first-choice candidate to succeed Gattuso, who left his post in March after Italy failed to qualify for a third successive World Cup.

Italian football expert Daniele Fisichella explained on the latest talkSPORT episode of Danny Kelly's Trans Euro Express podcast: “The name of Guardiola has been invented, has been named since May.

“Basically, the Italian FA, with the newly appointed Paolo Maldini, the former player, as a managing director, and Leonardo [Araujo], the Brazilian, as an adviser, they tried to get the best manager available on the market, which is Pep Guardiola, they met in Barcelona last Saturday, hours before the World Cup final, to explain the proposal and the idea of him managing not only the first team, but also be in charge of the restructuring of the Italian football.

“Of course, a fascinating proposal, albeit for the fact that there is quite a lot of work to do in the Italian FA and in the Italian national team.



“Guardiola was honoured; he said, but very politely replied, thanks, but no thanks, for different reasons.

“Also because he wants to take a step down for a bit from football, for personal reasons, for family reasons,” Fisichella continued.

6 Pep Guardiola bid farewell to Manchester City in May after a decade at the club Credit: Getty

“So even the idea of living in Barcelona and almost working remotely and then going to Italy to manage the team every three or four months didn't quite appeal to him.”



Who did Italy try to hire next?

Fisichella continued: “So then the Italian FA tried to convince Carlo Ancelotti, via Paolo Maldini, of course, his former teammate and former player at AC Milan. But Carlo Ancelotti had already committed to stay at Brazil.

“So the first choice, really the only viable choice, remained Andrea Pirlo, who, by the way, is a great friend of Paolo Maldini, having played together at AC Milan.

“And Paolo Maldini has always been a big sponsor of Andrea Pirlo. Why?

"Because Andrea Pirlo is considered almost somebody who has also got this aura.



“He was a fantastic player, but he's considered somebody who is destined to be a great manager.

6 It's back to the drawing board for Leonardo and Paolo Maldini in their search for a new manager Credit: Getty

“Unfortunately, his CV and his career doesn't quite tell the same story. His first ever coaching experience was at Juventus in 2021, and he didn't do really well there. They finished second; they won the cup.

“But that team never really convinced and was never able to impose themselves, despite still having Cristiano Ronaldo in very good form as well.



“Then he went to manage Sampdoria in the second division, got sacked after a year and a half, then went to Turkey and managed to finish fourth with a team outside of the top three anyway.

“And last year was managing in Dubai's second division, which, by the way, he won the championship there. So at least he got United FC promoted to the first division.”

6 Pirlo was named a global brand ambassador for Fonbet in October 2025 Credit: Getty

Pirlo's ties to Russian betting company

Regardless of his less-than-glittering managerial CV, Pirlo looked set to become 'the new Italian manager on a very cheap contract'.



“Only 1.5 million euros [£1.2m], compared, for example, to [Jurgen] Klopp, who earns 7-8m at Germany,” Fisichella added on talkSPORT on Sunday evening. “So he's obviously much, much cheaper.

“However, it has emerged that Pirlo earlier this year in May flew to Russia to participate in a testimonial game and to do some sponsorship for a betting company, which, of course, has been frowned upon.

“Now, a big crisis has started in the last few hours.

“Even politicians got involved in Italy, saying that whoever represents Russia or helps Russia should never, never be appointed into public office. So you can imagine the things have unravelled.

6 Pirlo was accused of being a ‘moral bankrupt’ by the Ukrainian skeleton athlete Vladyslav Heraskevych (not pictured) Credit: Getty



“And Paolo Maldini, who's been in the job less than three weeks, might resign if Pirlo, his friend, is not appointed.

“I mean, there's never a boring moment in Italian football. Let's face it.”

Sports.title: Wrexham set to make Crystal Palace defender first summer signing in £5million deal
Sports.content:
Wrexham are closing in on Crystal Palace defender Danny Imray, talkSPORT understands.

It is understood Imray won't be a part of Palace's squad for the Como Cup ahead of the deal being completed.

3 Imray joined Palace as an academy player in 2021 but has never made a senior appearance Credit: Getty

Imray is set to cost Wrexham approximately £5million and will become their first signing of the summer.

News of the 23-year-old's imminent arrival follows Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson revealing live on talkSPORT he anticipated the club landing a new face this week.

"You bring the players in different stages of pre-season," Parkinson told Majestic and Alan Pardew on The Final Word.

"Some deals take longer than others, people moving into the area and it took us a while to find our feet in the division and also, I had players adapting to that.

"But I feel we've got a better, stronger squad this pre-season and it's been great to work with the group so far, which we put together last season.

"However, I don't feel we're there yet in terms of the squad. We're not resting on our laurels and thinking we're seventh and we're just going to naturally progress above that."

Who has Danny Imray previously played for?

Imray will join Wrexham following two consecutive seasons out on loan.

The defender linked up with Bromley for the 2024/25 League Two campaign following the club's promotion from the National League.

Imray made 43 appearances in total for the Ravens, registering two goals and seven assists in all competitions as they finished 11th in the fourth tier.

He then made the step up to League One at the start of the 2025/26 season, joining Blackpool on loan.

3 The 23-year-old has impressed at right-back on a number of loan spells Credit: Getty

But the stint with the Tangerines only lasted 16 games as Imray was recalled by Palace in January, only to be loaned out again to Championship side West Bromwich Albion.

Imray handled yet another step up in competition as he featured 17 times to help the Baggies avoid relegation from the second tier, even with the club copping a points deduction late in the season.

He'll soon be tasked with helping Wrexham's bid for promotion to the Premier League.

How EFL's radical change will boost Wrexham's promotion hopes

The Welsh side agonisingly missed out on the play-offs last term as they finished two points off of Hull, who came sixth and went on to win the play-off final.

More will be expected from Parkinson's side this term though, especially with the Championship play-offs being expanded from four teams to six.

Previously, teams who finished from third to sixth would qualify for the season-ending chaos.

3 Parkinson has been in charge at Wrexham since July 2021 Credit: Getty

But the EFL announced in March the format would now include the teams who finish seventh and eighth, giving more teams a chance to enjoy the riches that come with being a Premier League club.

The 2026/27 season will mark the first campaign with the new play-off rules.

Wrexham will continue their pre-season preparations with a friendly against Liverpool at Yankee Stadium in New York.

The match is scheduled to commence at 12:30am BST on Thursday.

Sports.title: Federico Chiesa desperate for Liverpool stay as he teases new position under Andoni Iraola
Sports.content:
Federico Chiesa desperate for Liverpool stay as he teases new position under Andoni Iraola

Federico Chiesa insists he is 'doing the best I can' to revive his fortunes at Liverpool following two rough years under Arne Slot.

Chiesa was Slot's first signing after he replaced Jurgen Klopp as Liverpool boss, joining from Juventus in a deal worth up to £12.5million.



3 Chiesa featured in just 318 minutes of Premier League action for Liverpool last season Credit: Getty

However, Chiesa's switch to Merseyside has not gone to plan.

Of his 50 appearances for the Reds over the last two seasons, just nine of those have been starts.

Despite his lack of playing time, Chiesa was blocked from departing the Reds in January due to Alexander Isak's injury and Mohamed Salah's participation in the Africa Cup of Nations with Egypt.

But with Slot now gone and Andoni Iraola in the Anfield hot seat, Chiesa is hopeful of a change in fortunes.



Chiesa: I 'love everything' about Liverpool

“The only conversations I had were about pressing and tactics,” Chiesa said following Liverpool's 4-2 win over Sunderland in a pre-season friendly, a match in which he scored.

“So I don’t know, it is difficult to say. It is always a fresh start at the beginning of the year. Maybe there have been too many fresh starts.



“But I don’t care, I am trying to do my best for this new manager. Last season under Arne Slot, I was trying to do my best.

“Right now, at the moment, I am happy here at Liverpool. I love the club, I love the fans, I love everything. I am doing the best I can to have a chance here. And then we will see.



"At the minute, the only thing I am thinking about is Liverpool.”

Intriguingly, Chiesa could be set for a new role under Iraola.

3 Chiesa scored Liverpool's third goal against Sunderland Credit: Getty

A winger by trade, Chiesa came off the bench to play up top in the Reds' friendly against Sunderland.

Liverpool are light on bodies in the striker department, with Hugo Ekitike continuing to recover from a ruptured Achilles and Isak needing to be managed following his fibula fracture last term.

It's why the duo's fitness woes could be the perfect tonic to help Chiesa turn a new page in his Anfield career, especially given Iraola 'wants' him to play as a striker.



New man up top?

Chiesa remarked: “Last year I felt ready for a bigger role, then it depended on the coach, whether he wanted me to play or not.

“Of course I wanted to play more but it is what it is. The gaffer decided to do so, he had his game plans, he took his decisions, I have nothing to say about that. It is football.

"This year, let us say it is a new chapter. There is a new manager and I have to focus on that.

3 Iraola joined the Reds after three years with Bournemouth Credit: Getty



“He put me striker today and he wants me there. I have played my whole career as a winger, but I am happy to play striker as well.

“Pre-season is always hard, no? We didn’t just start, we have been training two weeks now with a new coach.

"We have seen what he wants. He wants high intensity, one versus one all over the pitch, that’s what we wanted to show today. Of course it is hard, it is pre-season.”

Chiesa will look to impress Slot yet again when the Reds face Wrexham in their next pre-season contest.



The match will take place at Yankee Stadium in New York, with kick-off scheduled at 12:30am BST on Thursday.

It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Read all about it as Forest eye £21m deal

Nottingham Forest are continuing negotiations with Feyenoord over a £21million deal for Givairo Read.

The Netherlands U21 international right back has agreed a five-year contract with Forest but they have still to finalise terms with his club after improving their offer on Sunday.

Feyenoord ideally want to keep the right-back for another season but he is keen on the move to the Premier League and what would be a hefty increase in salary.

Ortega in talks over Greece move

Former Nottingham Forest and Manchester City goalkeeper Stefan Ortega is in advanced talks with Olympiacos.

The 33-year-old left Forest in June after the expiry of his short-term contract.

The Greek club are also owned by Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis and are selling Konstantinos Tzolakis to Hull City.

Stefan Ortega left Forest this summer after his short-term contract ended

Manchester United sign new keeper

Manchester United have confirmed the signing of goalkeeper Kit Margetson from Swansea.

The 20-year-old was on loan at Welsh Premier League side Connah’s Quay Nomads last season, where he kept 10 clean sheets in 34 appearances.

The Wales youth keeper, the son of former Manchester City keeper Martyn Margetson, made his debut for Wales U21s against Belarus in March.

Margetson will move to Old Trafford subject to registration, after the two clubs agreed a compensation deal.

Kit Margetson is the son of former Manchester City keeper Martyn and also plays in goal

Ipswich land giant keeper Kjell

Ipswich Town have agreed a fee of around £11million for 6ft 9in Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen.

Scherpen had his medical today ahead of becoming their sixth new signing of the summer.

The fee agreed with his club Union Saint-Gilloise is £8.5m plus a further £2.5m in add-ons.

Brighton also had a 40 percent sell-on clause from USG as part of the deal.

Kjell Scherpen spent four years as a Brighton player from 2021 but spent most of his time out on loan

Villa's Kosta eyed by Osasuna

Aston Villa defender Kosta Nedeljkovic is wanted on loan by Osasuna.

The 20-year-old Serbia international right-back has been on loan at RB Leipzig but has not had a great deal of game time owing to niggly back and knee injuries.

He returned to full fitness in March and played for Serbia against World Cup winners Spain and was back in Villa's team for the pre-season friendly win over Walsall last week.

Fiorentina also made enquiries for Nedeljkovic earlier this year but Villa are ready to send him out for what they hope will be a more beneficial season on loan and La Liga side Osasuna want him to join them.

Villa have been trying to add another right-back and held talks with Flamengo for former Spurs defender Emerson Royal.

They are still to receive another approach from Arsenal for Ezri Konsa but the offer of a new contract is on the table and they do not need to sell following the £117m departure of Morgan Rogers.

Leicester eye Spurs defender Hardy

Tottenham defensive prospect Malachi Hardy has emerged as a potential loan target for Leicester City.

The League One side are exploring a move for the England U18 international who has impressed Roberto de Zerbi on pre-season so far with his composure and ability.

Following the 2-0 win over Auckland, De Zerbi said simply of the central defender, 'Malachi is another good player for the future of the club.'

The 18-year-old was given a contract extension earlier this year after impressing staff enough to step up to train with the first team and 'improving his aggression'.

Everton's Ndiaye a target for Al-Hilal

Al-Hilal are targeting Everton winger Iliman Ndiaye.

The Senegal international, 26, has three years left on his contract and Everton have been trying to tie him down to an improved deal which he has so far rejected.

The club’s stance has been he is not for sale amid interest from Premier League rivals but Al Hilal’s presence and financial power may bring greater concern.

Much will depend on what offer they put on the table, but they have yet to submit a bid.

Al Hilal, who have former Bournemouth technical director Simon Francis now on their staff, signed Crysencio Summerville from West Ham last week.

Iliman Ndiaye still has three years on his Everton contract and has resisted an improved deal

Imray's set for £5m Wrexham deal

Wrexham are set to sign full back Danny Imray from Crystal Palace in a £5m deal.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport yesterday the 22-year-old, who had loan spells with Blackpool and West Bromwich Albion last season, was wanted back by Albion while Stoke City also posted interest.

Wrexham, though, have got their man as they look to bolster their bid for promotion from the Championship to the Premier League.

Wycombe made a £750k bid in January 2025, which Palace decided to rebuff. Now they are set to land a fee seven-times higher 18 months later.
