Sports.title: Part-time sprinter - and UEFA employee who worked at Tottenham - stuns Glasgow by winning 100m Commonwealths heat
Sports.content:
Part-time sprinter - and UEFA employee who worked at Tottenham - stuns Glasgow by winning 100m Commonwealths heat

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

A part-time sprinter who works for UEFA sprung a surprise in Glasgow after winning his heat in the 100metres.

Elliot Jones, 28, was called in as a late replacement for England after Louis Hinchcliffe pulled out of the competition last week.

The top seven sprinters were given a bye through round one, with Jones registering the third fastest time across 10 heats with a time of 10.07 seconds.

Back in March, Jones was working in the matchday operations team for Tottenham’s Champions League match against Atletico Madrid.

‘There’s not a footballer who could touch me on the track!’ said Jones, who comes from Wigan.

Elliot Jones crosses the line first in a time on 10.07s - and goes again in the semis on Tuesday night

‘I work part time for UEFA. I’m a local assistant at matches for the venue operations team. They send in a team of managers to do broadcast, media, hospitality and matchday operations. I work as an assistant doing jobs like accreditation, signage around the ground, bits of access stuff. This year I was at Nottingham Forest and Spurs.’

Jones scrambled to get ready to compete, having originally planned to feature solely in this weekend’s relay.

‘I was only supposed to be travelling up on Tuesday,’ he said. ‘After Louis Hinchcliffe pulled out, I got a call from the sprints manager on Thursday night asking how I would feel about running the individual.

'I was like, “Let me think about that… yes!” I had to get the bus at 9am the next morning, quickly pack and restructure my training plan but it’s fine, we’re always ready. It was supposed to take us six hours but it took us seven hours with the traffic.

‘I’m just trying to enjoy it. I came here wanting to run sub-10. That’s my target. I’m going to use this as a platform and you’re going to see me here for the next few years. Every athlete’s dream is to go to the Olympics so touch wood I’ll be there in 2028.’

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty admits his future 'won't be filled with glory' in emotional Instagram post as he breaks silence on bronze medal and tearful Commonwealth Games interview
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty admits his future 'won't be filled with glory' in emotional Instagram post as he breaks silence on bronze medal and tearful Commonwealth Games interview

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Adam Ramsay-Peaty has admitted his future 'won't be filled with glory' after being forced to settle for bronze in the 100metres breaststroke final at the Commonwealth Games on Saturday, labelling sport as 'cruel' in an emotional statement on Instagram.

The British swimmer, 31, broke down in tears immediately after finishing third, having held the world record since 2015. He has one more shot at gold over 50m in Glasgow on Monday night, having qualified second in his semi-final yesterday.

But Ramsay-Peaty has accepted that golds will no longer come as regularly as they once did, admitting that his 'story won't be filled with glory, victory and gold' from now on.

The legendary swimmer – who is married to the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay, Holly – declared that his career is worth more than gold in a lengthy statement on social media, insisting he is 'not finished' despite his dwindling form in the pool.

Family and fatherhood has shifted Ramsay-Peaty's priorities of late, with the swimmer and Holly expecting their first child together, but he has urged he has no plans to retire before the next Olympics.

'A proud moment for me after a monumental effort to climb back from the Olympics two years ago,' Ramsay-Peaty said in a statement on Monday, referencing his bronze medal in the 100m breaststroke.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty has admitted his future 'won't be filled with glory' after Saturday's bronze

Ramsay-Peaty, pictured with wife Holly, also labelled sport 'cruel' in an emotional statement

'But as we know, sport is cruel, it’s the same reason that it’s beautiful. But why do it? I still love standing on the blocks, hearing the roar of the crowd, fighting inch by inch in every stroke, putting myself on the line, and, because I’m not finished. Ultimately, I know these are the stories I will be telling my children and their children.

'Bronze in the 100m was a bittersweet moment, I must put it into the perspective that it’s my first championship since Paris 2024. But with that, I know in my soul that I am capable of much more, as all athletes, I push myself to the extremity in training for better results. The race just didn’t come together unfortunately and I am building my race skills back together.

'The canvas is set and I know this story won’t be filled with glory, victory and gold. However I’ll keep fighting, learning, adapting and striving for excellence until I can no longer give anymore. Sport isn’t a fairytale if your happiness and self-worth are only validated by medals. But it can be, if you find value in the hardship, the struggle and the tough times which might ultimately lead you to what you seek.'

Ramsay-Peaty continued with a message to the next generation, adding: 'To the younger athletes, never be discouraged by a performance you’re not happy with, do not be afraid to be vulnerable in knowing that your training deserved more and use the pain to keep fighting. Enjoy every second because this journey goes much faster than you think.

'To the people out there who want to hurt me and my family with comments, I have seen this story thousand times with other athletes from many sports. We are athletes, doing something we love and that is our deepest passion. As it’s said, be the change you want to see in the world, and, I want a better world for the next generation of athletes. Love always wins.

'I am thankful for the opportunity to be able to race again at this level. Thankful for my wife, my friends, my team, and the people in the stands who cheer my name. Racing with my countries’ flag on my cap is the greatest honour. Tonight, I go again.'

After finishing third on Saturday, Ramsay-Peaty immediately joined Holly in the stands and kissed his wife's stomach before returning poolside to deliver an emotional post-race interview.

Breaking down in tears, he said on Saturday: 'It’s hard because I know how hard I work. I know the s*** I’ve been through, which is no fault of my own, but it does take its toll.

'I’m not crying because it’s bronze instead of gold. I’m crying because I know I am better than that. I feel like I couldn’t have put any more in and that’s where it hurts, because I’m like "what’s the point of all the metres every day, what’s the point of being exhausted all the time? What’s the point of having to say no to family events because you can’t go to training"?

Ramsay-Peaty spoke of the importance of fatherhood as he and Holly expect their first child

The legendary British swimmer took to social media with a lengthy statement on Monday

'It has to mean something and for me it has to be human excellence and that is not excellence for me. So that’s the emotion that is unfortunately coming out.'

Ramsay-Peaty, who also has a son George with his ex-girlfriend Eirianedd Munro, added: 'There’s obviously a lot of unanswered questions, which is about right, because we haven’t yet had time to debrief. But that is sport. It can break you. It can make you. You can have highs to highs and lows to lows.

'My wife is always going to be proud of me. As a father, it doesn’t matter if you come home with a gold – as long as you come home with a teddy, which I did. The emotion is something I’m always going to carry. I’m never going to be afraid to show weakness.'

Sports.title: Sorry Morgan Rogers, you're wrong. Here's the definitive proof that Arsenal are the BIGGEST team in London as James Sharpe gives Chelsea's record signing a history lesson
Sports.content:
Sorry Morgan Rogers, you're wrong. Here's the definitive proof that Arsenal are the BIGGEST team in London as James Sharpe gives Chelsea's record signing a history lesson

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Thanks a bunch, Morgan. Kick the hornets’ nest, why don’t you.

‘I am joining the biggest club in London,’ declared Morgan Rogers after completing his £117million British record transfer to Chelsea from Aston Villa. Perhaps he genuinely means it. Perhaps you’re contractually obliged to say it when your new club fork out quite so much for you.

Elliot Anderson did his bit after his £116m move to Manchester City, too. ‘For as long as I’ve known, Manchester City have been the Kings of Manchester,’ said the lad born in 2002.

Anyway, back to London. Rogers’ bold claim about a club that finished 33 points behind actual Premier League champions Arsenal last season stoked up all the old feelings and arguments. So, who are the biggest club in London?

Daily Mail Sport have donned a tin hat and bravely taken it upon ourselves to provide the definitive answer to the most divisive of questions…

Morgan Rogers boldly declared he had joined London's biggest club after completing a £117m move to Chelsea, but Arsenal will also stake their claim for that title

Trophies

What do the biggest clubs do? They win stuff. And the more you win, the more your reputation grows, as do your coffers, and your size.

But it also depends on what you win. A case full of League Cups and Community Shields is far less impressive than one of Premier League trophies and European Cups.

Arsenal have more than double the league titles of Chelsea, won over a far longer period of time, and almost twice as many FA Cups. Domestically, there is only one winner.

HONOURS Competition Arsenal Chelsea Premier League/First Division 14 6 Champions League/European Cup 0 2 FA Cup 14 8 League Cup 2 5 Europa League 0 2 UEFA Conference League 0 1 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup 1 2 Club World Cup 0 2 UEFA Super Cup 0 2 Full Members' Cup 0 2 Inter Cities' Fairs Cup 1 0 Community Shield 17 4

Only, isn’t being champions of Europe (or the world) bigger than being champions of England? Arsenal’s continental shortcoming is their glaring weak spot. The biggest clubs have won the European Cup. Arsenal haven’t.

A penalty shootout against Paris Saint-Germain away from glory, of course, but Tottenham have won a European trophy more recently, so have West Ham, so have Crystal Palace.

Chelsea have two Champions Leagues, two Europa Leagues, even a Conference League.

They boasted that they are the only club in history to win every major European trophy, which, more than anything, made you spare a thought for fans of the Inter Cities Fairs Cup.

As soon as Gabriel sent his penalty high into the stands, Chelsea posted an invitation to book a stadium tour at ‘London’s Home of Trophies’, with Big Ears front and centre.

They are two-time Club World Cup winners, too, which sounds cool but is only starting to feel important now that there’s £100m to win.

Verdict: Tie

Arsenal have more than double the league titles of Chelsea and almost twice as many FA Cups

Chelsea, however, have won the Champions League twice with Arsenal's contiential shortcomings their glaring weak spot

League position

Gravitas comes with a weight of history, too. That all but one of Chelsea’s league titles have been since 2005, with a Russian oligarch signing bigger cheques than anyone else, will tell you that time is on Arsenal’s side.

Since Arsenal joined the Football League in 1893, their average league position is 8.3. Across Chelsea’s history, theirs is 12.7. Tottenham’s is 11.7.

Across the 110 seasons in which both clubs have existed, Arsenal have finished higher in 77 of them.

Even in the Premier League era, when Chelsea stormed to power, the two clubs have split a higher finish 17 times apiece, though 16 of those for the Blues’ came across an 18-season period from 2004-05 to 2022-23.

However, Arsenal’s average position of 3.8 across the entire Premier League era still betters Chelsea’s of 5.

And even now Arsenal are current champions, after finishing second three times, during which time Chelsea finished 10th and 12th.

Verdict: Arsenal

Stadium and crowd

There’s simply no comparison between the Emirates Stadium, which Arsenal moved into in 2006, and Stamford Bridge. Bigger, better, fuller.

There was a brief five-year period before Arsenal’s move during which Chelsea boasted the marginally bigger crowds but, across history, the Gunners have had the greater attendances.

Chelsea’s average crowd even dropped below 13,000 in the early 1980s. Until Chelsea get an extension, or move, they cannot compete with Arsenal. Or Tottenham.

Yes, you can suggest, as the club’s supporters’ trust did during the malaise of Wenger’s final years, that Arsenal have not always been completely honest with their attendance figures — filled seats or tickets sold — but when the club’s fans come out they do so in force. Islington Council estimated more than a million people turned up for their Premier League title bus parade.

When Chelsea had theirs in 2015, official numbers were around 70,000. Around 200,000 turned up for their first under Jose Mourinho in 2005.

Verdict: Arsenal

There is no comparison between Arsenal's Emirates Stadium and Stamford Bridge

Over a million people reportedly attended Arsenal's Premier League title parade in May

Spending Power

The biggest clubs splash the biggest cash, right? Few spend it like Chelsea.

What began under Abramovich has continued into the BlueCo years. Chelsea’s net spend — that’s NET spend — over the past five years is more than £800m, nearly £150m more than any other Premier League side and £262m more than Arsenal.

Chelsea announced a Premier League-record pre-tax loss of £262.4m earlier this year for the 2024-25 season. They have spent well over a billion but not much of it well.

BIGGEST SIGNINGS Arsenal Fee Chelsea Fee Declan Rice £105m Morgan Rogers £117m Nicolas Pepe £72m Moises Caicedo £115m Eberechi Eze £67.5m Enzo Fernandez £106.8m Kai Havertz £65m Romelu Lukaku £97.5m Viktor Gyokeres £64m Mykhaylo Mudryk £88.5m Martin Zubimendi £60m Kai Havertz £75.8m Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang £55.4m Wesley Fofana £75m Noni Madueke £52m Kepa £71.6m

Kieran Maguire, the football finance expert, recently listed the biggest wage bills in Premier League history, adjusted for football inflation and the spending power clubs had at the time.

Chelsea made up eight of the top 10 with all their seasons from 2003-04 to 2010-11 at the height of their Abramovich era.

Arsenal’s first appearance on the list, their 2011-12 season, is in 51st place. Ahead of them are 16 different Chelsea seasons, 17 Manchester United seasons, 12 Manchester City seasons and five Liverpool seasons.

And yet over previous two sets of results, Arsenal have blown Chelsea out of the water in terms of their revenue: £691m to £491m.

Declan Rice is the only Arsenal signing of more than £100m.

Chelsea now have three: Rogers, Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez. Their top seven all come in higher than Arsenal’s second most expensive arrival in £72m Nicolas Pepe.

Verdict: Chelsea

Chelsea showed their financial power by signing Rogers from right under Arsenal nose

Rogers is one of three Chelsea players to cost over £100m, while Rice is Arsenal's only one

Star Power

Big spending brings big names and big managers. In the Premier League era, Arsenal have had Wenger, Unai Emery and Mikel Arteta in the dugout. Chelsea have had Mourinho (twice), Carlo Ancelotti, Rafa Benitez, Antonio Conte and Thomas Tuchel. The biggest names in the game. But then they have also had Graham Potter and Liam Rosenior.

On the pitch, few have ever had the aura of Thierry Henry, Dennis Bergkamp or Patrick Vieira. Bukayo Saka will be next. Chelsea will point to Didier Drogba and Eden Hazard. And Cole Palmer, perhaps?

Arsenal have taken a couple of Chelsea’s cast-offs in recent years, too, with Kai Havertz and Noni Madueke, and yet they are both now champions.

Arsenal lead the way, too, when it comes to producing England stars. Rice, Madueke, Saka and Eberechi Eze’s involvement in the World Cup quarter-final against Norway, took the club past 1,000 caps for Arsenal players.

Chelsea, the first club to field an all-foreign team, in 1999, stand at fewer than 750.

Verdict: Tie

Jose Mourinho is among a host of big name managers to have taken charge of Chelsea

Few can match the aura of former Arsenal stars Thierry Henry (pictured), Dennis Bergkamp and Patrick Vieira

Social Media

The true test of how big a club is in the modern era is, surely, how many followers they have on social media.

I would have staked everything on Arsenal winning this. Few supporter groups make their voices quite so piercingly heard than the Gunners’, and certainly when they feel, as they often do, that they have been wronged or robbed.

And, yet, Chelsea win on all counts. They have more followers on X, Instagram, TikTok, Facebook and YouTube, to the combined tune of more than 33 million.

Verdict: Chelsea

Insider’s view

It’s clear they both crave the title. Chelsea previously trademarked their ‘CFC LDN’ branding — what better way to prove you’re London’s big dogs? ‘There’s only one answer,’ replied one Arsenal source when posed the question.

‘The way Arsenal conduct themselves comes from a place of prestige,’ a prominent agent who has dealt with both clubs tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Chelsea have more of a big-club approach in the way they get things done. They are very much: if we want the player, we will do what it takes to get them. Put our cards on the table. That is a big-club mentality.

‘There’s definitely two different cultures, through which both see themselves as the biggest club in London but go about it in a different way. Arsenal are like your old money, slightly entitled aristocrat who can fall back on title and family history. Chelsea are the nouveau riche, super successful city worker who isn’t shy about showing off how much money they have and uses that to drive more success.’

Elon Musk might be the richest man in the world and Tesla the largest automobile company by market capitalisation, but good luck convincing anyone they are really bigger than Mercedes or Ferrari.

Verdict: Arsenal

Sorry Morgan, your new club may be big spenders but most metrics confirm the Gunners are the capital’s major players.

Overall verdict: Arsenal

Sports.title: Andrea Pirlo BLOCKED from becoming Italy manager after links to Russian betting firm spark 'political' concerns - as icon breaks silence on decision that has left Paolo Maldini furious
Sports.content:
Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after 'political' concerns were raised over the football legend's sponsorship deal with a Russian betting company.

Pirlo, 47, was backed by former team-mate and new Italian Football Federation (FIGC) technical director Paolo Maldini to land the role after legendary ex-Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola reportedly declined the opportunity.

The former AC Milan and Juventus star was on the brink of agreeing a deal with the crisis-hit football nation before several Italian politicians raised concerns about Pirlo's role as an ambassador for Russian betting firm Fonbet.

It was felt Pirlo, who had been prepared to leave his current job as coach of Dubai United, should not have conflicting views on Italy's support for Ukraine in the war with Russia.

Pirlo himself confirmed that he was no longer in the running in an Instagram post on Monday, urging that his Fonbet deal was linked to his job in the United Arab Emirates and is 'exclusively for commercial and sports' purposes.

His claim has been refuted by Dubai United owner Sergey Lomakin, who stated that Pirlo's involvement with the firm was not an involuntary aspect of his deal.

Andrea Pirlo is no longer in the running to become Italy's next manager after a dramatic twist

The Italy legend's appointment has been blocked after 'political' concerns were raised over his sponsorship deal with Russian betting company Fonbet in the United Arab Emirates

Pirlo said in a statement: 'In recent days, I have witnessed with great bitterness the debate that has developed around my name and the possibility of taking on the role of Head Coach of the Italian national team.

'Out of respect for the institutions, the Federation, and all those involved, I have chosen to remain silent until now.'

'However, I feel it is my duty to clarify certain aspects.

'Throughout my career, first as a player and now as a coach, I have always conducted my activities in full compliance with the laws of the countries in which I have worked and the contracts I have signed.

'The professional collaboration at the centre of the recent controversy arose as part of my career in the United Arab Emirates and is exclusively of a commercial and sporting nature.'

It is understood Maldini is furious by the decision made by FIGC president Giovanni Malago and may quit his role as technical director after Pirlo's appointment was blocked.

Adverts, endorsements and sponsorship deals pertaining to betting are strictly prohibited in Italy.

Pirlo added: 'Attributing political meaning to this collaboration means attributing to me beliefs I have never expressed and that are not mine.

'I would like to thank Maldini and Leonardo for the esteem and trust they have shown me. I know their expertise, their seriousness, and the love they have always dedicated to Italian football.

Paolo Maldini is reportedly furious at the decision and may walk from his role as a result

'I regret that a sporting decision was quickly dragged into a public debate that ended up attributing to me meanings and intentions that are not mine.

'My love for Italy does not depend on a position. It is part of my history, my identity, and will continue to accompany me, always.'

Pirlo was at best a third-choice after Carlo Ancelotti and Guardiola turned down offers to coach a team that has failed to qualify for three consecutive World Cups.

Now former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini and Antonio Conte are back being discussed for the job.

Sports.title: English WAG who supported Argentina at the World Cup reveals the gifts Lionel Messi gave EVERY team-mate including her Premier League boyfriend after finishing second
Sports.content:
English WAG who supported Argentina at the World Cup reveals the gifts Lionel Messi gave EVERY team-mate including her Premier League boyfriend after finishing second

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The English girlfriend of one of Argentina's World Cup stars has revealed the gifts that Lionel Messi gave to the entire squad after the tournament.

Kelci-Rose Bowers, 22, posted consistent updates on social media throughout the World Cup as she followed her boyfriend Marcos Senesi around.

Senesi and Bowers met while they were both playing for Bournemouth, though the former has since joined Tottenham on a free transfer.

And now Bowers has shared a video showing the personalised backpack, golden Stanley water bottle, and mate set that Messi gave her beau after their 1-0 defeat in the final by Spain.

Senesi's new bag has his name on it and has space for the ingredients and cup used to drink mate, a traditional South American caffeinated herbal drink.

It remains to be seen how long Messi has left with his Argentina team-mates. The legendary forward is now 39 and weighing up his international future.

Marcos Senesi's footballer girlfriend, Kelci-Rose Bowers, has showed off the gifts Lionel Messi got the Argentina squad after the World Cup

Bowers, who met Senesi while they were both at Bournemouth, followed him to the World Cup

Choosing to support Argentina over England proved to be a controversial decision

His team-mate Leandro Paredes indicated that the World Cup final may have been Messi's last game as he said: 'I think he had already decided that this would be his last game with the national team.'

Paredes himself – who clashed with Eric Garcia and Gavi after the final whistle - may step away from the international game, while Nicolas Otamendi already has in the wake of their lacklustre final performance.

Writing on Instagram after the loss, Messi said: 'The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal.

'But I also hold onto all the good things... the matches we turned around by giving it our all - moments that will remain in our memories forever - and the support of an entire country which, combined with this group's hard work and effort, brought us back among the world's elite once again.

'It is hard to fully appreciate our achievement right now, but this group reached two consecutive World Cup finals. Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.

'I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship.'

Messi is a gift who keeps on giving with regards to the global game. He actually first retired from Argentina duty in 2016 but soon returned, and it was definitely worth doing that; he's since won the 2022 World Cup and two Copa Americas.

His kind gesture towards his team-mates was certainly appreciated and Bowers, Senesi's girlfriend, has already racked up 300,000 views on her video about the gesture.

|Bowers filmed Senesi reacting to being handed a late call-up to Argentina's World Cup squad

Senesi, who has been on holiday in Ibiza, celebrated with his English footballer girlfriend

The duo had to cut short their holiday in Dubai when Senesi was handed a last-gasp call-up to Argentina's squad – and of course that made a social media hit as well.

An injury to Marseille defender Leonardo Balerdi freed up space in the squad and Argentina manager Lionel Scaloni decided that Senesi was the man to replace him.

Bowers shared a video of Senesi receiving news of his call-up, as she explained they had been about to go to dinner when he received a phone call from the Argentinean national team.

‘We just came back from Miami, where we had been on holiday, and came to Ibiza just to enjoy a bit and relax,' Bowers explained while Senesi was on the phone.

'But this whole time neither of us have switched off, we were both aware of the situation of a centre back getting injured.

'We have both the whole time not been able to fully enjoy, you know what I mean.

'And now Marcos has just been called up. He has been called up for the World Cup, are you joking.

'This is literally what both of us have been praying for, every day he has just been thinking about this.’

After Senesi put the phone down, both he and Bowers hugged and screamed in celebration.

The call-up was a reward for Senesi's fine season at Bournemouth, where he helped the Cherries to a sixth-place finish in the Premier League to secure Europa League qualification.

The defender, who had also been eligible to represent Italy, had made just three appearances for Argentina to date in his career.

He went on to make two outings at the World Cup, including as a late substitute in the final.

Sports.title: Levi Colwill admits he felt 'helpless' during Chelsea's struggles after missing last season and the World Cup through injury that 'killed everything'
Sports.content:
Levi Colwill is ready to prove he is one of the Premier League’s best centre backs after opening up on how his ACL ordeal left him feeling ‘helpless’ last season as Chelsea laboured to a 10th-placed finish.

The 23-year-old Englishman managed to return for the final few league fixtures of 2025-26, though his club missed out on qualifying for any form of European football. The last time Colwill played in a Chelsea victory came in the Club World Cup final against Paris Saint-Germain in July 2025.

‘I'm ready to go,’ Colwill told us in Sydney, Australia, where Chelsea have started their pre-season tour under new manager Xabi Alonso. ‘Having a tiny taste at the end of last season really gave me that extra motivation to come back for pre-season with that fire in my belly.

‘I want to take my game to the next level this year. I want to be regarded as one of the best centre-backs in the league this year, 100 per cent. I feel like we can challenge. I feel like the players we've got in our team are ready to do that. Having a manager of this quality now, when it all comes together, we’re definitely going to be able to challenge and push for the Premier League.’

While the focus has fallen on Alonso’s fondness for attacking football, he will be trusting Colwill to man his back line, most likely alongside Maxence Lacroix. The French central defender, 26, is set to sign from Crystal Palace for £52million.

Levi Colwill has admitted he felt 'helpless' during Chelsea's woeful season last campaign

Colwill has been working his way back after a lengthy injury kept him out of Chelsea's season

Discussing the devastating impact of his ACL injury, Colwill said: ‘It was the first day back of pre-season last year. You come off winning the Club World Cup feeling on top of the world, and then an injury like that happens. It kills everything. It was really tough to get my head around.

‘But I'm a strong believer that everything happens for a reason, so I just tried to take it in my stride. Seeing the boys on the pitch every day obviously hurt a lot, but I got over it, and I'm back now.

‘I feel like I'm a stronger person, mentally and physically. I had to find something to keep my head on and try to distract me when I could because it was very tough not doing what you love every single day. When you can't do anything to affect the game on the pitch, you feel helpless, and that's how I felt at times.’

Alonso has been heavily involved in training drills. Daily Mail Sport watched one session in Sydney on Sunday in which the 44-year-old Spaniard was playing passes to set up Estevao Willian and Chelsea’s other right-wing options for crosses.

‘We're really proud to play under him and, on the training pitch, when he shows the quality he still has, it shows that it never goes,’ Colwill added. ‘He's just spraying balls around for no reason and it's a perfect pass every time. Sometimes you can be a bit jealous, but he's an amazing manager to work under and he was obviously a crazy player, so to learn under him will be so good.

‘He's putting across his game plan and trying to make us play the football he wants us to play, which is really creative, attacking, free-flowing football, which I think we're doing really well.'

Chelsea face Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday with Colwill saying: ‘I really do believe the players we've got in the changing room are some of the best players in the world. When everything comes together, we can really be a strong force and push forward this season.’

Sports.content:
Spain's Dani Olmo accuses Argentina assistant who punched him in shameful World Cup scenes of LYING - and claims coach 'isn't sorry at all'

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Dani Olmo has accused the Argentina coach who punched him after Spain's World Cup final victory of lying in his attempt to downplay the incident.

Spain's 1-0 triumph was marred by shameful scenes of violence and thuggery as Argentina's players and coaching staff brawled with their opponents after the final whistle before refusing to watch them lift the trophy at MetLife Stadium in New York.

Olmo was one of four Spain players attacked by Argentina during the post-match melee, with coach Roberto Ayala appearing to throw a punch that caught the midfielder in the neck.

Ayala attempted to downplay the incident by stating it was 'more of a shove than a punch' and claimed he had reacted to 'some words' uttered by Olmo and his nearby team-mate Eric Garcia.

The Argentina assistant also issued a public apology and vowed to say sorry 'in person' if he ever sees Olmo again.

Speaking about the incident for the first time since Spain's World Cup final victory on July 19, Olmo refused to accept Ayala's apology and accused him of lying.

Dani Olmo has accused the Argentina coach who punched him at the World Cup of lying

Roberto Ayala clashed with Garcia before he appeared to strike Olmo after last Sunday's final

He told Spanish newspaper Diari de Terrassa: 'Someone who says they're sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, is surely not sorry.

'He is lying because I didn't say anything to him, so he doesn't need to apologise. What truly defines us is not the mistake, but the courage to acknowledge it with humility, honesty and dignity.

'When my children, my family and all those fans watch the game, I want them to be proud of how we competed, how we won and, above all, of our behaviour, because the importance of football means that us players are an example for children and the new generations, and that brings with it a huge responsibility.'

When questioned about the incident earlier this week, Ayala had said: 'Of course I'm sorry. Given my position, I cannot allow a feeling, or whatever I might receive from the other party, to affect my mood or my actions.

'For me, we need to draw a line and leave it at that. It was more of a shove than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be.

'It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person.'

FIFA have launched an investigation into the deplorable post-match scenes, which could see Argentina heavily fined for failing to control their players and staff.

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes could also face a lengthy ban for lashing out at Garcia before throwing Spain substitute Gavi to the floor after the final whistle.

Nahuel Molina, meanwhile, was caught on camera striking Rodri in his stomach as Spain's captain ran on to the pitch to celebrate with his team-mates.

Ayala tried to downplay his clash with Olmo by saying it was 'more of a shove than a punch'

Announcing their probe into what had gone on in the aftermath of last Sunday's game, FIFA said: 'Following an assessment of the relevant match reports for the FIFA World Cup final between Spain and Argentina, and in line with article 36 of the FIFA disciplinary code (FDC), the FIFA disciplinary committee has appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to investigate potential breaches of the FDC with regard to the post-match incidents.

'Further details will be communicated by the FIFA disciplinary committee once the prosecutor’s report has been completed.'

Sports.title: F1 news: Lewis Hamilton controversy as star lashes out an 'unacceptable' incident
Sports.content:
F1 news: Lewis Hamilton controversy as star lashes out an 'unacceptable' incident

Lewis Hamilton was involved in a controversial moment during the Hungarian GP as one F1 star made his feelings clear about an incident on the track

View 2 Images Lewis Hamilton was penalised during the Hungarian Grand Prix (Image: Beata Zawrzel/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

Lando Norris won the Hungarian Grand Prix on Sunday to claim his first victory of the campaign. The reigning world champion, who finished 15 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen, sits fifth in the drivers’ standings.

‌



Kimi Antonelli is currently leading the charge to take this year’s crown, having won six of 11 F1 races. Lewis Hamilton was denied the chance to shorten the Italian’s lead after receiving a controversial penalty for speeding in the pit lane.

‌



Meanwhile, Norris had battled his McLaren teammate Oscar Piastri for the lead during an early portion of the race. However, Piastri’s attempt to win was impacted by a collision with Carlos Sainz. Here is a round-up of some of the biggest F1 headlines following the Hungarian GP.

‌



Lewis Hamilton controversy

Sky Sports F1 pundit Anthony Davidson was left confused by Lewis Hamilton's penalty for pit lane speeding during the Hungarian Grand Prix. The incident occurred when Hamilton was travelling through the pit for his second change of tyres.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

Race stewards stated that Hamilton had driven at 80.1kph in the pit lane, where the limit is 80kph. Consequently, he received a five-second time penalty, which dropped him to fifth place, having originally finished fourth but only four seconds ahead of his Ferrari teammate Charles Leclerc. However, footage from above Hamilton's helmet appeared to show him pressing his pit limiter button at the right time.

‌



Kim Kardashian and Lewis Hamilton set to make first UK appearance at Ethnicity Awards READ MORE :

F1 news: Lewis Hamilton hit with new penalty as untelevised moment emerges READ MORE :

"I've looked at this so many times and I can't work out why he gets a penalty,” Davidson said during the Sky Sports broadcast. “For me, he slows down sufficiently well. We've got this marker board on the left-hand side that stipulates the 80kph speed limit. I don't see that [speeding].

"Let's have a look at the exit. Obviously knew he was under time pressure to get out in that race with [Kimi] Antonelli. Again, for me, it sounds like he releases the pit lane button on the line itself. This guy knows what he's doing when it comes to white lines and when to press the button.

"Maybe there was just an error when he was a bit too close to the line on the actual speed of the car and they were just pinged by that. Who knows? Strange that it only happened that one time. I don't have enough data here and I can only go by the sound of when he is pressing that button. For me, it looked totally fine on the way in and on the way out."

‌



View 2 Images McLaren driver Oscar Piastri spoke out after the Hungarian GP (Image: Clive Mason/Getty Images)

Oscar Piastri on ‘unacceptable’ incident

Oscar Piastri hit out at Carlos Sainz for colliding with him during the Hungarian GP. The McLaren driver was battling teammate Lando Norris for the lead when he approached Sainz and Fernando Alonso, who were both a lap down.

Sainz attempted to overtake Alonso but failed to complete the move before cutting across Piastri’s path, which led to a collision. Stewards deemed Sainz responsible for the crash on lap 39, with the Williams driver receiving a five-second penalty, while Piastri ultimately did not finish the race due to a gearbox failure.

Article continues below

"I couldn't believe what happened," Piastri said. "Getting crashed into by a lapped car is never one of the things you expect that can go wrong in your race. And today it was.

"I don't really care if he didn't see me and the fact that he didn't and no one told him, or there was a lack of complete awareness, is unacceptable."

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino’s rambling World Cup rant shows FIFA boss has gone ‘full Donald Trump’
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino’s rambling World Cup rant shows FIFA boss has gone ‘full Donald Trump’

The FIFA president has responded to his critics and has claimed that the 2026 World Cup was 'outstanding' but his assessment of the tournament is badly flawed

View 3 Images Gianni Infantino sounded like his good friend Donald Trump during a lengthy rant directed at World Cup critics (Image: Bradley Collyer/PA Wire)

Considering the amount of personal criticism he gets, Gianni Infantino is allowed the right to respond. Of course he is.

‌



And the FIFA president can respond in whatever manner he sees fit. Had he responded via a press conference at the end of the World Cup, it might have been better. But if he wants to do it in a 15-slide post on social media, that is fine.

‌



However, his declarations about the tournament are the ramblings of someone who has been made truly delusional by power. Having spent so much of the last couple of years on the shoulder of Donald Trump, why wouldn’t Infantino feel powerful?

‌



There are suggestions Trump wants Infantino as the next secretary-general of the United Nations, for goodness sake. But Infantino’s lengthy outburst against critics of some aspects of the 2026 World Cup reads like wilfully deceptive propaganda.

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

World Cup final referee Slavko Vincic quits football days later as statement released READ MORE :

“We experienced no violence, no incidents, 100 percent safety and security, only joy and happiness!” That is one of his declarations in his Instagram essay.

There was, indeed, a lot of joy and happiness, but four people died during World Cup celebrations in Mexico City following Mexico’s victory over Ecuador in the round-of-32. Fans from four competing countries - Iran, Haiti, Somalia and Ivory Coast - could not share the ‘joy and happiness’ because they were banned from entering the United States.

‌



In his post, Infantino says that “Iran entered the United States without incident or conflict.” Yet it was widely reported that only four of the 15 Iranian team staff members who were originally denied visas were later granted the right to travel into the country.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

And don’t forget, Omar Artan - regarded as African football’s best referee - was denied entrance to America on the eve of the tournament.

‌



“You mentioned the few people denied visas and overlooked the millions who were approved, from all parts of the world,” wrote Infantino. “Because football unites the world and it was demonstrated impressively this summer.”

So, is everyone supposed to just brush aside cases such as the Artan one? Yes, according to Infantino, it seems.

He says critics of the tournament should ‘meditate, pray or watch a football match’ in order ‘to find peace’. He says critics have been ‘spreading hate’.

‌



View 3 Images Top referee Omar Artan was sent back to Somalia after being refused entry into the United States for the 2026 World Cup (Image: SAID YUSUF WARSAME/EPA/Shutterstock)

But no-one is ‘spreading hate’ by denouncing FIFA for allowing football on the grandest stage to become a game of four quarters. Was there a pundit out there who likes the idea of compulsory hydration breaks?

And no-one was ‘spreading hate’ when denouncing FIFA for the suspension of Folarin Balogun’s automatic one-game ban after the United States’ 2-0 victory over Bosnia and Herzegovina in the first round of knockout games. Trump had phoned Infantino to ask him to review the Balogun ban. It was subsequently suspended, allowing the player to line up against Belgium in a round-of-16 tie.

‌



“Indeed, ‘arguable’ referees’ decisions or ‘strange’ disciplinary rulings such as for instance potentially mistaken red or yellow cards or subsequent decisions not to ban players in certain situations are routine and widely accepted in some of the biggest leagues in the world,” Infantino wrote. “It’s curious that the same countries employing these practices are the ones criticising.”

View 3 Images Folarin Balogun's one-game ban at the 2026 World Cup was controversially suspended by FIFA (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

There are rights of appeal in disciplinary processes in club leagues but the Balogun decision was a totally arbitrary one that has yet to be explained by anyone at FIFA. Clearly, it should, though, in the eyes of Infantino, be brushed under the carpet. We should all just chill out and admit the World Cup was great.

‌



“To the pens and papers, to all the screens, may you find love and peace where the people behind you couldn’t,” he went on. “May you find peace; we at FIFA have found ours and we deliver it, by delivering the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.”

As the final ended in scenes of post-match violent chaos, he really is delusional if he thought that was ‘the most outstanding FIFA World Cup.’ He has been hanging around with him so much, he has gone full Trump.

Sports.title: Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers
Sports.content:
Chelsea outline Pedro Neto stance as Man City and Liverpool consider offers

Chelsea winger Pedro Neto is being eyed up by some of the Blues' Premier League rivals - but they are determined not to sell the former Wolves star on the cheap

View 2 Images Pedro Neto is wanted by other Premier League clubs (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC)

Chelsea would look to ensure any transfer fee received for Pedro Neto would be proportionate to some of the mammoth figures being quoted for other wide attackers this summer amid growing interest in the former Wolves man.

‌



Liverpool and Manchester City have both been credited with an interest in Neto, who joined the Blues back in the summer of 2024. Chelsea shelled out £54million to bring the 26-year-old to Stamford Bridge, but the market has exploded in the last couple of years.

‌



And that means Chelsea will only sell Neto this summer if his suitors are willing to pay a premium price.

‌



The Mail report that Chelsea have noted some of the figures being placed upon in-demand wingers this summer, such as Bradley Barcola and Yan Diomande. Both players are valued in excess of £100m.

Jadon Sancho finally receives shock contract offer months after Man Utd exit READ MORE :

While it's noted that Neto would be unlikely to command such a transfer fee, Chelsea could still ask for a figure which is some way north of the amount they signed him for two years ago.

Interest from Premier League rivals is not thought to be a surprise to Chelsea; Enzo Maresca favoured Neto as his first-choice right winger while in charge at Stamford Bridge and is keen on working with him again at Manchester City.

‌



Liverpool are in the market for wide attackers as they revamp their squad following the departure of Mohamed Salah, while there is also interest in Neto from clubs in Saudi Arabia.

Neto is currently on holiday after featuring at the World Cup for Portugal.

View 2 Images Enzo Maresca would like to reunite with Neto at Manchester City (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Speaking back in October, just weeks before his explosive exit from Chelsea, Maresca lauded the winger for the improvements he had been showing.

"He’s top, he's very humble and working hard,’ Maresca said of Neto.

"He's a very important player for us, and we are very happy with Pedro. He's exactly the same as other players – he needs to be always 100 per cent, because in the moment that you drop a little bit, mentally or physically, in this league, it's complicated."

Sports.title: Luke Littler fronts new Netflix show where darts fans can win eye-watering £501k prize
Sports.content:
Luke Littler fronts new Netflix show where darts fans can win eye-watering £501k prize

Luke Littler is in a league of his own at the top of professional darts, yet plucky fans will be hoping to get the better of 'The Nuke' on a new Netflix show which offers a huge prize

View 2 Images Luke Littler won the World Matchplay trophy on Sunday (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Darts fans will be given the chance to take on Luke Littler in a new Netflix show which is offering £501,000 to anyone who can beat the world No.1.

‌



Littler may only be 19 years old but he is already well established as the best player in the world - and one of the best of all time. His victory over Gerwyn Price in the World Matchplay final on Sunday night saw him continue his utter dominance of the sport and set new records.

‌



Littler won 18-9, claimed £225,000 in prize money and broke Phil Taylor's long-standing records for the highest average across the tournament and in the final. He has now claimed £3,143,500 over the PDC's two-year order of merit - and now is ready to give an everyday player the chance to pocket some serious cash.

‌



The Nuke will step up to the oche and take on pub players, with Netflix putting up a gigantic prize to anyone who can achieve the impossible. 'Beat Luke Littler' will be aired live on the streaming giant on October 30 and will include regional heats in Manchester and London in September before 20 competitors take on Littler in a single leg.

"Everyone thinks they can beat me," Littler said. "Now they get a chance to prove it. Bring it on."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Alan Shearer's daughter marries England star in lavish wedding ceremony READ MORE :

Adam Peaty breaks down in tears and makes heartbreaking comment about family feud READ MORE :

A statement from Netflix read: “The rules are simple: one night, one chance, and one perfect leg of 501. If an amateur can defeat darts prodigy Luke Littler, they will walk away with a life-changing £501,000.

“Produced in partnership with the PDC, the governing body behind professional darts, the show will be rooted in the authentic world of competitive darts, bringing the sport’s electric atmosphere live on Netflix.

“To kick off the launch, Netflix has officially opened the nationwide recruitment search to find the 20 competitors brave enough to step up."

‌



View 2 Images Luke Littler is in ridiculous form right now (Image: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images)

Littler is operating on an entirely different level in darts, having won the World Championship, UK Open, Premier League and the Masters already in 2026. He's earned £2.13m more than world No.2 Luke Humphries in the current PDC cycle and believes there's still room for improvement.

“I can still get better,” he said in Blackpool after beating Price. “I can get a lot better. Through the matches, I was up to a 120 average at one point and I didn’t make it stick. Maybe in a few years’ time I will stick it and go up to a 120 average.

Article continues below

“At the minute I’m playing some of the best stuff and I’ve just got to keep it there… The main goal was to win every major once. I don’t know how many years are left in me. We’re still only two and a half years into my professional career. It’s far from done.”

Price, who averaged an impressive 104.97 in the final but was still way off Littler's standards, issued a warning to potential competitors. "Luke is one in a million, I threw everything at him," the Welshman said.

"He's fantastic for the sport. I wish he wasn't as good as he is - I would have won a couple more tournaments. I hope there's no-one else like him coming through because he's ridiculous!"

Sports.title: Former England rugby captain teams up with Strictly star for triathlon challenge
Sports.content:
Former England rugby captain teams up with Strictly star for triathlon challenge

Chris Robshaw and Julian Caillon were among those to take part in the London T100 Triathlon weekend.

View Image Former England rugby captain Chris Robshaw in action during the London T100 Triathlon.

Chris Robshaw swapped his rugby boots for his swimming cap, bike and running shoes as he completed his first ever triathlon at the London T100 Triathlon this weekend.

The former England rugby captain raced alongside his BBC Strictly Come Dancing co-star and professional dancer Julian Caillon at the ExCeL arena in a bid to raise money for the Kerslake-Robshaw Foundation. The charity funds projects across the UK that help young people facing barriers build confidence, improve wellbeing, find belonging and unlock their potential.

Robshaw and Caillon both took part in the Olympic distance triathlon, which included a 1.5km swim in Royal Victoria Dock, a 40km bike ride around the Docklands and then a 10km run around London’s ExCeL Centre. The 40-year-old was aiming to break the four-hour mark and subsequently smashed his expectations as he came home in a time of 3:14:59.

‌



“I was excited when I got here,” said Robshaw, who made 66 appearances for his county and finished 13th in last year’s series of Strictly. “But then I got in the water, and honestly, on my first lap, it’s like I forgot how to swim.”

“I couldn’t breathe, and it was so hard. That first lap was so hard. I thought I might not get back in. Then I got back in and the second lap was all right, and the bike and the run were actually the quickest I’ve done. To finish with 3:14:59, I’m really pleased with that, considering I wanted to do sub-four hours.”

“It’s been a great experience. The crowd’s been amazing. I’m still in one piece, which is important… and loved it.”

Australian Caillon, who has done multiple triathlons previously, finished in 2:38:38, while his fiancée Sofia Ochoa, also racing for the Kerslake-Robshaw team, finished in 2:39:01.

“This was actually my first Olympic distance triathlon. I’ve done a couple of other distances, but this was my first Olympic and my first T100 Triathlon event, and I was really, really excited for it,” said Caillon.

“Today was really good. I had a lot of fun. I went the wrong way on the swim [laughs] which happens to me every time. But, no, it was an awesome vibe. The weather was great. It was a lot of fun. I was a bit crampy on the run, but apart from that, yeah, awesome finish. Here in the ExCeL as well, finishing off and everyone cheering for you. Yeah, it was a really, really fun day.”

‌



“The Kerslake-Robshaw Foundation is obviously Chris and Camilla’s foundation, and they use sport and music to help young people and so we’re trying to raise money, raise awareness as well. It’s a great cause. They do a lot of great work with the community.

“I think triathlon can help everyone in so many different ways. I think the beauty of it is you’ve got three disciplines. So you’ve just got to hope that you’re somewhat good at one of them! But, to be honest, I think the community aspect is what’s drawn me into it.”

Robshaw and Caillon were the amateur ‘starter’ before the world’s best short distance triathletes competed in the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) London.

Australian Matthew Hauser won the elite men’s race while Frenchwoman Cassandre Beaugrand took the spoils in the women’s event. British stars Alex Yee, Georgia Taylor-Brown and Beth Potter all took part too, with Yee coming home in 14th while Taylor-Brown and Potter finished sixth and fourth respectively.

In total, 5,300 amateur triathletes will take part across the weekend, from experienced triathletes tackling the T100 distance on Sunday to first-time swim, bike and run participants taking on the shorter Super Sprint, Sprint and Olympic distance triathlons as well as Team Relays.

British stars, including Alex Yee, Beth Potter, Georgia Taylor-Brown, and Sophie Evans, competed at the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) London, with Olympic qualifying points on the line. For more information visit Triathlonlive.tv and TNT Sports in the UK.

Sports.title: Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl
Sports.content:
Spain star Dani Olmo accuses Argentina coach of lying after World Cup final brawl

The fallout from the unsavoury scenes after the full-time whistle in the World Cup final continues, with Spain midfielder Dani Olmo accusing Argentina coach Roberto Ayala of lying

View 2 Images Roberto Ayala clashed with Dani Olmo after the World Cup final

Spain star Dani Olmo has refused to accept an apology from Argentina coach Roberto Ayala and accused him of lying about what happened following the World Cup final.

‌



There were violent clashes on the pitch after the full-time whistle crowned Spain as champions in New Jersey. Ferran Torres' goal in extra-time was enough to seal a 1-0 win for Spain, but their winning moment was tarnished by what followed.

‌



Argentina's Leandro Paredes kicked and punched as he shoved Eric Garcia to the ground and grappled with Gavi, while Nahuel Molina appeared to have instigated the altercation by throwing a punch at Rodri.

‌



There was also a flashpoint involving Ayala and Olmo, with the Argentina assistant coach caught on camera putting his hand around the Barcelona midfielder's neck.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

FIFA are investigating the ugly scenes, which could prompt suspensions and fines. And the backlash against Argentina is continuing, with Olmo speaking out after Ayala said he reacted to something he had heard.

‌



Olmo told newspaper Diari de Terrassa: "Someone who says they're sorry, but justifies a punch by saying it was a response to a comment, is surely not sorry, because he is lying.

"I didn't say anything to him, so he doesn't need to apologise. What truly defines us is not the mistake, but the courage to acknowledge it with humility, honesty and dignity."

He added: "When my children, my family and all those fans watch the game, I want them to be proud of how we competed, how we won and, above all, of our behaviour, because the importance of football means that us players are an example for children and the new generations, and that brings with it a huge responsibility."

‌



View 2 Images Dani Olmo was able to celebrate the win after the incident (Image: Rob Newell/Getty Images)

Ayala had previously said: "Of course I'm sorry. Given my position, I cannot allow a feeling, or whatever I might receive from the other party, to affect my mood or my actions.

"For me, we need to draw a line and leave it at that. It was more of a shove than anything else, it wasn't a punch as they're making it out to be."

‌



He added: "It was a reaction to something he said, but that's it. If I see him, I'll obviously apologise to him in person."

FIFA have appointed a disciplinary and ethics prosecutor to assess the ugly scenes after the full-time whistle. It is likely to result in fines for Argentina failing to control their players and staff.

"There is no place or space for that," Alan Shearer said on the BBC at the time. "We know how much it means to them and we know how much it hurts to lose, but there is a way to lose. Too many times we have seen that from Argentina. The reaction after the final whistle is terrible."

Article continues below

Argentina's lack of discipline was obvious in the game, with Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez sent off after catching Pau Cubarsi with a high foot to receive his second yellow card, having been shown a first one for dissent.

Sports.title: Alex Yee denied dream homecoming as Olympic champion crashes bike in London T100
Sports.content:
Alex Yee denied dream homecoming as Olympic champion crashes bike in London T100

The Olympic champion loved racing in his home city but was unable to finish on the podium

View Image Alex Yee races through the run leg during the World Triathlon Championship Series event in London.

Alex Yee was unable to produce the podium finish he wanted on his return to World Triathlon Championship Series racing in London as he came home in 14th.

‌



The Olympic champion faced a difficult afternoon after struggling in the swim, before a crash during the bike stage left him well back heading into the final discipline. Despite the setbacks, Yee delivered the quickest run of any athlete (13:52) to fight his way back through the field and give the passionate British crowd something to shout about as he crossed the line.

‌



“It’s just not quite the swim delivery I wanted,” said Yee. “After about 100 metres of the swim, I just got very much caught up between two or three guys, just literally kind of shoulder-to-shoulder. From that point, it was very much trying to salvage my swim rather than try and be positive with it. I managed to move up well through the boys and then lose a little bit on the way back in.

‌



“I was able to ride fairly well. I was able to move up a little bit on the bike into that second group. At one point, I thought we were going to progress pretty well, but then they got working at the front. Maybe a little bit of motorbike assistance as well came into play.

“Unfortunately, I had a little bit of a crash on the way back into T2, but these things happen.”

Dylan Fletcher sees positives despite Team Emirates GBR suffering SailGP disappointment READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino slams FIFA critics in bizarre letter that glosses over World Cup issues READ MORE :

Matthew Hauser claimed the WTCS London victory after a strong all-round performance, with Vasco Vilaça finishing second and Csongor Lehmann third.

‌



The Australian’s win moved him to third in the overall standings while Max Stapley was the best-finishing Brit in 12th.

While the result was not what he had hoped for, Yee said being able to complete the race on home soil and test himself again was an important step forward after a difficult period.

“I was able to be inspired by the amazing crowd that came out here, that pushed me through that run,” he continued. “I’m proud to just be able to finish a race, to be honest, and be able to push myself to the limit, because there’s been a few reasons why I haven’t been able to do that before.”

‌



Yee also praised the return of WTCS racing to London, with the unique venue of the ExCeL allowing athletes to race close to the fans and create a memorable atmosphere.

He said: “I think massive kudos to World Triathlon that we were able to have a race back here. I hope it stays, and we can continue having this for many years to come. London 2012 is something which left an impact on me, and hopefully this can light a fire for someone else watching.”

Looking ahead, Yee remains focused on his long-term goals, including the challenge of qualifying for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics. But he knows there is still work to do, particularly in the swim, where he believes he is currently below his best level.

Article continues below

“I’d say pride, to be honest,” Yee said when asked about his emotions after the race. “I’m proud that I was able to give it 100%. You can’t be one per cent off in any of these disciplines, and I’m probably five per cent off where I need to be in the swim, or where I have been in the swim.”

British stars, including Alex Yee, Beth Potter, Georgia Taylor-Brown, and Sophie Evans, competed at the World Triathlon Championship Series (WTCS) London, with Olympic qualifying points on the line. For more information visit Triathlonlive.tv and TNT Sports in the UK.

Sports.title: Dylan Fletcher sees positives despite Team Emirates GBR suffering SailGP disappointment
Sports.content:
Dylan Fletcher sees positives despite Team Emirates GBR suffering SailGP disappointment

Dylan Fletcher believes Team Emirates GBR were unfortunate to miss the SailGP final in Portsmouth, with the reigning champions finishing bottom of their group despite flashes of promise on home waters.

View Image Team Emirates GBR driver Dylan Fletcher competes on the Solent during the SailGP event in Portsmouth.

Driver Dylan Fletcher felt Team Emirates GBR were unfortunate to finish bottom of Group B at their home SailGP race in front of a 20,000-strong crowd on the Solent.

‌



The British boat finished fifth and sixth in their two group fleet races, missing out on qualification for the final at the Emirates Great Britain Sail Grand Prix in Portsmouth by eight points, with the Swedish and Swiss boats progressing instead. Fletcher did see his crew storm off the line in the final race, only to be pipped to the first mark by the Swiss, resulting in a terminal loss of speed and falling off the foils.

‌



He said: “It was difficult. In the first race we just got boxed around a bit and didn't really have the opportunity very often to go where we wanted, and the second race was over after mark one for us. We know we chipped away and got back into the fleet a bit but ultimately we were miles behind after being off the foils.

‌



“Yesterday we didn't start well enough in two races and from there the level was higher in our fleet than the other fleet.

BONDS Flying Roos, the season championship leaders from Australia, were unable to progress too, instead ceding the top two positions to Canada’s NorthStar and Spain’s Los Gallos. And it was the Spanish who clinched their second consecutive victory and went clear of reigning SailGP champions Emirates GBR in second place, with USA SailGP Team and Sweden’s Artemis both leapfrogging the Brits in the championship too.

Fletcher said: “Especially yesterday, there weren't many overtaking lanes so it's very difficult for us to come back from those poor starts. It was different today - we managed to get on top of the starts and worked with the whole team to remedy that. That was nice to see, so as frustrating as it is, there are some little positives to take away from the weekend but it unravelled after that in both races.

‌



“It was a fairly slow bleed in the first race and I can't quite put my finger on what happened. Then in the second race, there was a fundamental mistake round mark one. I don't know exactly what it was but effectively, that was race over at that point.”

The previous race in Halifax saw teams split into two groups for the fleet racing, a format that SailGP is set to continue until the end of the season.

Fletcher said: “The longer group racing goes on, the fairer it becomes. You inevitably end up with a higher quality and lower quality fleet each weekend, and it can just be down to conditions and what goes on.

Article continues below

“I think the B fleet was the tougher fleet this time around, but next time around it might be different.

“I thought it was a fantastic course today with really interesting racing opportunities and great positioning in front of the crowd.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
