World.title: Resignation fails to shield Andrea Johnson from tough Madlanga questions
World.content:
PRETORIA - Despite submitting her resignation, which was accepted by President Cyril Ramaphosa, now-former Independent Directorate Against Corruption (IDAC) head Andrea Johnson continues to face tough questioning at the Madlanga Commission.

In a 17-point application to vacate office addressed to Ramaphosa and National Director of Public Prosecutions Andy Mothibi, Johnson wrote that “the recent five months or so have been challenging and the attacks on both my person and official capacity have been unprecedented.”

Her resignation, however, did not exempt her from further scrutiny before the Commission.

On Monday, Johnson entered the third day of her testimony, where evidence leader Mahlape Sello questioned her over whether certain documentation related to IDAC’s Crime Intelligence investigations has been handed over to the Commission.

LIVESTREAM | Andrea Johnson continues testimony

Johnson said MP Fadiel Adams provided four A1 statements to IDAC in relation to his complaints against Crime Intelligence officials.

Last week, Johnson admitted that parts of her earlier testimony before Parliament's ad hoc committee were incorrect.

She conceded IDAC had in fact solicited a Section 27 affidavit from MP Fadiel Adams that led to the arrest of Crime Intelligence boss Dumisani Khumalo, after previously denying that the directorate had ever received the document.

During the first part of her testimony on Monday, she conceded that the 6 February 2025 IDAC summons she signed may be problematic if there is no strong evidential basis to support alleged manipulation of security vetting processes.

The summons relates to investigations into alleged manipulation of security vetting processes and the unlawful granting of security vetting. She said she signed the summons after receiving a briefing from her investigators.

She added that police statements and referral affidavits form the foundation of investigations and, if they are incomplete or improperly compiled, the state risks losing its ability to prosecute those implicated

Sello asked: “What would your advice to the commissioners be regarding how they view the summons in circumstances where all the documents that you have listed, we have just discussed, do not factually or legally support this Section 28?"

Johnson answered:

“Then the investigation is problematic. Whatever follows is problematic.”

Asked about the legal validity of the investigation and any subsequent processes, Johnson said: “Short of a proper detailed explanation from the investigators, one that is accepted by the Commission, then that investigation falls away. It has to be a legitimate investigation that is supported by documentation. That is the basis on which IDAC has worked on all its other matters. This matter cannot be an exception.”

World.title: JSC advises Ramaphosa to suspend Selby Mbenenge
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Judicial Service Commission (JSC) has advised President Cyril Ramaphosa to suspend disgraced Eastern Cape Judge President Selby Mbenenge.

In January, the Judicial Conduct Tribunal, which investigated the sexual harassment complaint, found Mbenenge guilty of a degree of misconduct, but not gross misconduct. It found he breached the code of judicial conduct, which states a judge must always act honourably.

However, the JSC did not accept the findings of the tribunal and on 5 March, found that Mbenenge was guilty of gross misconduct. It then recommended that Mbenenge be suspended from office.

READ | Selby Mbenenge challenges JSC gross misconduct finding

Mbenenge is accused of making unwanted sexual advances towards junior employee, Andiswa Mengo, between 2021 and 2022.

In a statement on Monday, the JSC said it decided on 7 July after considering written submissions on whether Mbenenge should be suspended pending Parliament's consideration of the matter.

"At this meeting, the JSC resolved to advise the President to suspend Judge President Mbenenge from his duties pending the decision of the National Assembly as contemplated in section 77 of the Constitution," read the statement.

Mbenenge is challenging the findings by both the Commission and the Tribunal.

Pending the determination of his review, he also wants the court to interdict the President from suspending and removing him from office.

World.title: LIVESTREAM | Andrea Johnson continues testimony
World.content:
PRETORIA - Independent Directorate Against Corruption (Idac) Andrea Johnson returns to the Madlanga Commission to resume her testimony.

It comes after she admitted that parts of her evidence were incorrect, acknowledging key errors in her testimony to Parliament's ad hoc committee.

READ | Ramaphosa accepts Andrea Johnson resignation

Johnson conceded that IDAC had solicited a Section 27 affidavit for suspended Crime Intelligence Chief Dumisani Khumalo, after previously denying ever receiving the document.

Her appearance comes as a formal complaint has been lodged with the IDAC oversight judge.

It is calling for an investigation into her conduct and alleges abuse of prosecutorial authority.

World.title: 'Deliver or get out': Ramathuba tells underperforming councillors
World.content:
THOHOYANDOU - ANC Limpopo chairperson Phophi Ramathuba has issued a stern warning to underperforming councillors and mayors ahead of the 4 November local government elections.

Ramathuba has made it clear that poor performance will not be tolerated.

Addressing supporters at the ANC’s Mandela Legacy Rally at Makwarela Stadium in Thohoyandou, she said the governing party is prepared to recall deployees who fail to deliver, even if it means making changes on the eve of the elections.

The rally took place just a short distance from Thohoyandou Stadium, where the Economic Freedom Fighters (EFF) launched its local government election manifesto.

While the timing and proximity sparked speculation of political point-scoring, the ANC has dismissed claims that it deliberately staged the event to counter the EFF.

Instead, the party says the focus remains on strengthening governance and improving struggling municipalities across Limpopo.

READ | ANC banking on new faces to win back voters ahead of local elections

Ramathuba revealed that the ANC has already begun reconfiguring its provincial management teams, with several mayoral changes aimed at placing skilled and capable leaders in municipalities where performance has been lacking.

She stressed that accountability remains central to the party’s renewal efforts, saying the ANC cannot expect to win elections if it fails to hold its own deployees accountable.

According to Ramathuba, those who are unable to perform will be redeployed to positions better suited to their abilities, making way for leaders who can deliver.

ANC National Executive Committee member Enoch Godongwana echoed that message, saying effective leadership and reliable service delivery are critical to fixing local government.

READ | ANC set to announce mayoral candidates

Godongwana said municipalities need leaders who are equipped to meet the challenges facing communities and ensure that essential services are delivered where they matter most.

The rally also highlighted growing political tensions between the ANC and its long-time alliance partner, the South African Communist Party (SACP), following the SACP’s decision to contest the November local government elections independently.

Ramathuba acknowledged that the ANC had accepted the SACP’s decision, although it was not the party’s preferred outcome. She said the ANC remains focused on securing a decisive victory in Limpopo, adding that the SACP would have to contest the elections on its own.

Despite the political shifts, Ramathuba expressed confidence that the ANC will retain control of all 27 municipalities in Limpopo when voters head to the polls in November.

World.title: 'Deliver or get out,' Ramathuba says to underperforming councilors
World.content:
THOHOYANDOU - "Deliver or get out," Limpopo ANC Chairperson Dr Phophi Ramathuba told party supporters in Thohoyandou.

This was her warning to underperforming councillors in the province ahead of the 4 November local government elections.

Ramathuba said the party would not hesitate to recall underperformers, even on the eve of elections.

She said the party has reconfigured itself. That is why some municipalities have had mayors removed and new ones instated quickly in their place.

"We are strengthening our municipalities to bring relevant people with relevant skills," she said.

"If you don't have a strong ANC that holds its deployees accountable, you are not going to win," she told the crowd at the Makwarela Stadium in Thohoyandou.

National Executive Committee member Enoch Godongwana said fixing struggling municipalities requires good leadership and the provision of basic services.

Ramathuba said she is confident the ANC will hold onto all 27 municipalities in the province after the November polls.

World.title: DJ Warras murder case: Pre-trial proceedings resume
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Pre-trial proceedings in the murder case of DJ Warras resume on Monday in the High Court in Johannesburg.

The matter was postponed on Friday due to the absence of one of the accused.

Victor Majola, the alleged mastermind, failed to appear because of administrative confusion.

Co-accused Armando Pacula is charged with carrying out the shooting.

The court also heard that Majola is still waiting for some case documents, before proceedings can move forward.

World.title: Alonso says 'great signing' Rogers can rejuvenate Chelsea
World.content:
LONDON - New Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso on Monday said Morgan Rogers was "a great signing" who would make the club more competitive and expected the England midfielder to "link really well" with Cole Palmer.

The versatile Rogers was signed from Aston Villa last week for £117 million ($157 million), a record for a British player.

Alonso said he was "delighted" to lure the 23-year-old to Stamford Bridge ahead of his first match in charge, a pre-season friendly against Western Sydney Wanderers on Tuesday.

"It's a great signing. I think that in that position, we needed an important player, and I'm sure that there were not many more better options than Morgan," the Spaniard told reporters.

"So we are delighted. It means a lot for everyone."

The swoop is a significant statement of intent from Chelsea, who finished 10th in the Premier League last season and missed out on Europe.

Alonso will have to find a way to accommodate Rogers, Palmer, Pedro Neto, Estevao Willian and another close-season signing, Geovany Quenda, into his attacking midfield positions.

"I have a plan. I have an idea. I can see them linking really well," Alonso said on how Morgan could fit in alongside Palmer. The pair are close friends who have similar playing styles.

"You need to have a good mix, good stability players, and players that can play with more freedom," Alonso added.

"And if we get that balance right, and we get those special players in the right positions, with good control, I think that we will be more competitive with the ball and against the ball."

Chelsea had reportedly been chasing Rogers for two years and beat Arsenal to his signature after the Premier League champions refused to match the eye-watering fee demanded by Villa.

His transfer surpassed the previous record fee for a British player set by Manchester City when they signed England midfielder Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest for £116 million earlier this month.

"I think that one of his best qualities is that he's flexible," Alonso said of Rogers, who is not on their pre-season trip to Australia after helping England to finish third at the World Cup.

"I think that he can play in that pocket position, close to the striker, close to the turn, but he's played as well on the right. But I think more coming from the left.

"We (will) play him where he feels he is enjoying his game, that he feels his flow. I'm sure that he will have good connections with the other players that he can have around him.

"So if we get those connections right, those little associations between them that they look for each other and they connect well, I think that it will be a great step forward in the quality of our game."

Chelsea will also play fellow London club Tottenham Hotspur on Saturday in Sydney, before flying to Hong Kong for a match against Juventus on August 5.

World.title: 'We thought it was firewood': Officer tells court in murder of State House guard case
World.content:
Kenya's State House in Nairobi. [File, Standard]

A State House police officer on Monday gave a chilling account of the moment a man armed with a bow and arrows allegedly launched a deadly attack on security officers guarding State House, telling the High Court that the suspect appeared determined to target officers.

Testifying before the Kibera High Court, Kelvin Nyabuto, a presidential guard attached to State House, said he was on duty on the morning of October 13, 2025, when he noticed a man approaching Gate D carrying what initially appeared to be a piece of wood.

World.title: Ruto: Government will deal firmly with criminals
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto arrive for the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County on July 26, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has declared war on individuals who involve in violence, destruction of property and political intimidation.

He said people initially participated in anti-government demonstrations have "graduated from protesters to goons."

Speaking on Sunday during the consecration of Rev. Vitalis Job Ekuru as the fourth Bishop of the ACK Diocese of Katakwa in Busia County, the President said the government would no longer tolerate criminality disguised as peaceful protests.

"They have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere," Ruto said.

President Ruto maintained that safeguarding peace remains the government's top priority while ensuring all leaders have the freedom to campaign without fear of violence or intimidation.

He argued that Kenya had previously experienced a rise in criminal activities, but efforts to deal with those responsible had been complicated by differing opinions over how security agencies should respond.

"We had a small problem earlier when crime issues increased and we did not agree on how to tackle the crime as a nation because sometimes we used to defend those who were hurting people and destroying property. We could say that they should not be touched because they are our children," he said.

"But now we have seen the repercussions because they have now graduated from protesters to goons. They are bringing chaos everywhere."

Ruto said the government had resolved to restore law and order, insisting that criminal gangs would not be allowed to disrupt peace under the cover of political demonstrations.

"We have agreed to discipline all the goons, and no one will be allowed to propagate crime and disrupt peace in our country," he said.

The President also sought to reassure Kenyans that the country would remain peaceful as preparations begin for the 2027 General Election, saying his administration would do everything possible to safeguard stability before, during and after the polls.

"I agree that peace is not negotiable. All of us, irrespective of who we are, our persuasion, our political leaning and whatever it is that we believe in, we must have a peaceful nation," Ruto said.

"I want to assure you as the people of Kenya that we will have peaceful elections next year because elections come and go, but this nation must remain firm, united and stable. We shall do everything possible to ensure that this nation is stable."

At the same time, the Head of State emphasized that every political leader should be free to campaign and present their agenda without intimidation, provided they conduct their activities peacefully.

"Every leader should be given a chance to give their opinion. Those who have an agenda or plan should be given an opportunity to explain it to Kenyans. Even those who have nothing should be given a chance to speak, but all of us must ensure that we are peaceful," he said.

The President's remarks come against the backdrop of heightened political tensions and growing concerns over violent disruptions at political gatherings.

Recent incidents, including the Ol Kalou by-election in Nyandarua County, saw armed gangs disrupt voting and terrorize residents, prompting renewed debate over the role of criminal groups in Kenya's political landscape.

The government has faced criticism from sections of the opposition, who have accused state agencies of sponsoring the gangs.

However, Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has rejected the claims, instead alleging that the groups were mobilized by allies of former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua. Murkomen has pledged decisive action against those behind the violence, regardless of their political affiliation.

World.title: Ruiru 'Vampire' arrested after lodging incident with woman
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The suspect was arrested after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents. [Courtesy, X]

Police in Ruiru have arrested a 35-year-old man believed to be behind a series of bizarre and violent attacks in which residents were robbed and bitten, leaving several victims nursing serious injuries.

The suspect, identified as Githaiga from Mugutha, was arrested on Saturday afternoon after an angry mob cornered and assaulted him near the Powerstar area in Ruiru town following weeks of attacks that had spread fear among residents.

Ruiru Sub-County Police Commander Charles Kibathi confirmed the arrest, saying the suspect was heavily intoxicated at the time and had allegedly bitten a woman who was with him, tearing part of her lower lip.

"The suspect and the female victim were taken to hospital for treatment as investigations continue," Kibathi said.

He added that detectives are investigating whether the suspect is linked to the earlier attacks reported in Ruiru and neighbouring Gitothua Ward.

However, some residents defended the suspect, claiming the altercation that led to the woman being bitten stemmed from a disagreement after the two emerged from a room where they had spent the night.

Kibathi assured residents that police are pursuing all leads to establish whether other people may have been involved in the attacks and pledged to intensify security operations in the area.

The arrest follows weeks of panic after several residents reported being attacked by a man who allegedly robbed victims before violently biting them.

Among the latest victims was Daniel Ndegwa, who was attacked on July 11 at about 9 p.m. while walking to a nearby shopping centre. Ndegwa told police he was confronted by a man demanding his mobile phone before a struggle ensued. During the confrontation, the attacker bit his finger and injured his left hand. A friend who was accompanying him was also reportedly bitten.

Residents said the attacks had become increasingly frequent throughout July, forcing many people to avoid walking outside after dark.

In one of the most shocking incidents, another victim reportedly suffered severe facial injuries after the attacker allegedly bit off part of his cheek.

The incidents have disrupted normal life in Ruiru town and Gitothua Ward, with many residents opting to remain indoors in the evenings for fear of being attacked.

Residents, led by Severino Githinji, criticized the security situation, saying families have been living in constant fear and called for increased police patrols and swift action against those responsible.

Police said the first official report of the attacks was made on July 11, and investigations are ongoing to establish whether the arrested suspect is responsible for all the reported incidents.

Kibathi urged members of the public to continue cooperating with investigators as detectives work to unravel the full circumstances surrounding the attacks.

World.title: Murkomen: Police no longer rely on Gachagua's 'gossip'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen during the official launch of the Multi-biometric Identification System (MBIS) and handover ceremony of ANSI National Accreditation Board Certificate at DCI Headquarters on July 23, 2026. [NPS]

Interior Cabinet Secretary Kipchumba Murkomen has accused former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua of spreading falsehoods, saying technology-driven policing has replaced "gossip-based" investigations.

Speaking during the handover of the ANSI National Accreditation Board certification to the Forensic Evidence Management Unit and the launch of the Multi-Biometric Identification System at the Directorate of Criminal Investigations headquarters on Thursday, Murkomen said the country has shifted from outdated investigative methods to science-based policing.

"We are moving away from gossip-based collection of evidence to science. I saw an impeached former leader claiming he is well connected to police officers and receives gossip every day because he is not busy unlike the President," said Murkomen.

He said the biometric system will strengthen investigations through science and technology, making unofficial information unnecessary.

"That is an old style of collecting evidence. We now have a modern police service driven by science and technology. We do not need his gossip to run the National Police Service," he observed.

Murkomen claimed the technology would make it harder for unsuitable individuals to rise through public office.

"If these systems had been in place many years ago, people like Gachagua would not have survived the system as habitual offenders until he slipped through to become Deputy President. Such things will never happen again with this technological advancement," said Murkomen.

The Interior CS defended Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja, saying he has the government's confidence and has discharged his duties professionally.

"I have full support and faith in the leadership of the Inspector General. He has carried out his duties with dignity, honour and respect for the citizens of Kenya and his office," noted Murkomen.

Murkomen also rejected Gachagua's criticism of police leadership, arguing that Kenya is recording fewer cases of terrorism, banditry, robbery and other crimes.

"There has never been a period when Kenya has recorded fewer incidents of terrorism, banditry, robberies and other crimes. Our security agencies are working together and have improved security," he said.

He also criticised remarks attributed to Gachagua warning tourists against visiting Kenya, saying they damage the country's reputation.

"For anyone to stand out there and say Kenya is not safe and tourists should not come to our country is very embarrassing," explained Murkomen.

Murkomen dismissed claims that 68 women were raped by police officers during the Ol Kalou parliamentary by-election, urging anyone with evidence to report the matter to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority or the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights.

"If those incidents occurred, they should be reported so those responsible can be held accountable. If not, those making such reckless statements must also be held accountable," said Murkomen.

He accused Gachagua of making the allegations out of political desperation.

"I know why Gachagua speaks the way he does. It is because of desperation. Knowing that he cannot hold any office again in Kenya and can never be President of this republic, he wants to take the entire nation, including the economy, down the drain with himself. We will not allow that," he said.

Murkomen also urged media organisations to challenge politicians they host instead of allowing false claims to go unchecked.

"We should not feed Kenyans with lies. I want to tell media houses that when you invite such reckless human beings, please carry with you a lie detector. Otherwise you are going to mislead the people of Kenya and drive bad behaviour in our country," said Murkomen.

He maintained that intelligence gathering within the National Police Service follows lawful procedures and dismissed claims that private individuals receive confidential police briefings outside official channels

World.title: Gachagua: Why Ruto will not steal the 2027 General Election
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Righathi Gachagua during a live interview with KTN at his Karen home, Nairobi. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has claimed that President William Ruto will not be able to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 General Election, arguing that Kenyans have become more vigilant in protecting their votes.

Speaking during a live interview with KTN from his Karen residence, the former Deputy President said the recent Ol Kalou by-election had provided opposition supporters with a blueprint on safeguarding the electoral process.

"Voting is not enough; you vote and protect the vote. We now have a template from the Ol Kalou by-election," Gachagua said.

He urged Kenyans to remain vigilant during the next General Election, saying the alleged intimidation witnessed in Ol Kalou had failed to influence voters.

"They tried intimidating the people of Ol Kalou, but they did not succeed. We are celebrating what happened, and people from across the country are calling to benchmark on how it worked," he said.

Gachagua also questioned the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC)'s ability to conduct a free and fair election, accusing the electoral body of failing to condemn alleged voter suppression and bribery during the Ol Kalou by-election.

"IEBC has not even condemned the wrongs that happened during the by-election in Ol Kalou. We lost two people who were actually protecting our votes," he alleged.

The DCP leader further renewed his criticism of President Ruto, accusing him of betraying voters from the Mt Kenya region despite earlier warnings.

According to Gachagua, the outcome of the Ol Kalou by-election should serve as a warning to the Kenya Kwanza administration ahead of the 2027 General Election.

He maintained that the by-election demonstrated that Kenyans could no longer be intimidated by the State and described the result as a preview of what to expect in the next national polls.

Gachagua also revisited the Mbeere North by-election, alleging that DCP lost because of widespread voter bribery, intimidation of elderly voters and failure by the party to adequately protect its votes.

"We lost the Mbeere North by-election because we didn't protect our votes properly. There was also massive voter bribery, and those who participated were allegedly given the balance of their bribe after showing a photo of whom they had voted for," he claimed.

The former Deputy President further argued that DCP would have secured an even larger victory in Ol Kalou were it not for what he described as voter suppression and police intimidation.



More to follow...

World.title: Charles Owino appointed as Government Spokesperson
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

President William Ruto has promoted Government Spokesperson Isaac Mwaura in a fresh round of changes within the Executive, while also making nominations to key constitutional commissions and statutory bodies.

In an Executive Order issued on Tuesday, Chief of Staff and Head of Public Service Felix Koskei said the Public Service Commission had approved promotions and redeployments affecting senior government officials.

Under the changes, Mwaura was promoted and redesignated as the Head of the Office of Diversity, Inclusion and Disability Rights in the Executive Office of the President.

Charles Owino Wahong’o was redeployed from the Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy to the Executive Office of the President, where he will serve as Acting Head of Government Communications.

The former Police Spokesperson has been appointed the new Government Spokesperson, taking over from Mwaura.

At the same time, Ruto also nominated new office holders to key constitutional commissions and approved changes within the senior ranks of the Executive in a fresh round of appointments aimed at filling vacancies and strengthening government institutions.

Among the nominees is Dr. Duncan Ojwang Oburu, who has been picked to serve as the Chairperson of the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA).

Ruto also nominated Ms. Antonina Lentoijoni and former Kenya National Union of Teachers (KNUT) Secretary-General Wilson Sossion as members of the Teachers Service Commission (TSC).

Ms. Flora Mutua was nominated as a member of the Public Service Commission (PSC).

In the nominations, Ruto also named seven individuals to serve on the Intergovernmental Relations Technical Committee (IGRTC), subject to ratification by the National and County Government Co-ordinating Summit in accordance with the Intergovernmental Relations Act.

The nominees are Wilson Kuria Thuita (Murang'a), Silvya C. Apaa (Busia), Ahmed Kanyara Bishar (Wajir), Pascalyne Ntang'enoi Kimiriri (Laikipia), Ken Riaga (Migori), Evalyn Chepkirui Aruasa (Nakuru) and Mary Nanjala Kilobi (Nairobi).

World.title: Why public servants have less than a month to update pension records
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Public servants given until August 14 to update pension records [File]

Government has directed all public servants to update their records with the Public Service Superannuation Fund (PSSF) by August 14, 2026, in the latest step towards modernising pension administration.

In a circular signed by Principal Secretary for Public Service and Human Capital Development Dr Jane Imbunya, all PSSF members are expected to update their personal information and beneficiary details through the PSSF Member Self-Service Portal or the PSSF Mobile Application.

The circular was addressed to Ministries, State Departments, Constitutional Commissions, Independent Offices, County Public Service Boards and County Governments.

The exercise is expected to streamline pension administration and accelerate the processing of retirement benefits supported by a new Pension Administration System (PAS), a digital platform developed by PSSF to deliver faster, more transparent and more efficient pension services.

The registration exercise targets 529,635 members drawn from across the public service, including 332,950 teachers under the Teachers Service Commission (TSC), 120,084 officers in the disciplined services, 60,322 employees in Ministries, Departments, Constitutional Commissions and Agencies (MDCAs), and 16,279 county government employees.

PSSF Chief Executive Jonah Aiyabei said updating member records is critical to the success of the pension reforms and the delivery of efficient retirement services.

“By updating their records, public servants will enable quicker processing of retirement benefits, reduce administrative delays, improve data integrity, allow members to access pension services seamlessly through digital channels and ensure that the right benefits reach the right beneficiaries at the right time,” he said.

Under the new system, members can access their pension statements in real time, monitor contributions, view projected retirement benefits, update beneficiary nominations and personal details and initiate and track pension claims remotely.

The platform also features a Sponsor Portal that enables employer institutions to submit payroll information, contribution schedules and member data electronically, significantly improving efficiency and accountability in pension administration.

Dr Aiyabei said the Pension Administration System marks a significant milestone in the government’s efforts to digitise pension administration and restore dignity to retirees through faster, more accessible and transparent services.

“It will provide our members with real-time access to their pension information, enable seamless engagement with the Fund and support a fully digital, paperless pension administration process. Ultimately, our goal is to restore dignity in old age by ensuring every public servant receives timely and efficient pension services,” he said.

World.title: Egyptian, Tunisian FMs hail bilateral relations and regional coordination
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, Emigration, and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty and Tunisian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Migration, Mohamed Ali Nafti affirmed on Sunday, July 26, 2026, during a phone call that the special nature of bilateral relations and historic bonds uniting both nations.

The two ministers praised the development of ties and hailed the outcomes of the 18th Egyptian-Tunisian Joint Higher Committee held in Cairo last September, emphasizing the importance of following up on agreements to boost economic, commercial, and investment cooperation.

Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations across various fields.

Regionally, Abdelatty briefed his Tunisian counterpart on Egypt’s efforts and contacts with regional and international parties regarding rapid regional developments to de-escalate tension and support stability.

He underscored Egypt’s stance calling for an immediate halt to all military actions, prioritizing political solutions, and intensifying Arab coordination to safeguard regional security.

Regarding Libya, Abdelatty praised the results of the Tripartite Neighboring Countries mechanism ministerial meeting hosted by Cairo on May 21, stressing the need to maintain its regular meetings to support Libyan unity, sovereignty, and national institutions.

World.title: Electricity Minister presents renewable energy plans to ambassadors
World.content:
Minister of Electricity and Renewable Energy Mahmoud Esmat met on Sunday, July 26, 2026, with Egyptian ambassadors and heads of diplomatic missions to present investment opportunities in the country’s renewable energy sector and discuss plans to expand international cooperation.

During the meeting at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in the New Capital, Esmat reviewed Egypt’s strategy to increase investment in solar and wind energy, modernize the national power grid and accelerate the transition to smart grid technologies.

He said that Egypt offers many investment opportunities in renewable energy and electricity infrastructure, supported by an expanding network of international partnerships and government policies aimed at increasing private sector participation.

Esmat added that Egypt is working to strengthen its position as a regional energy hub through electricity interconnection projects with Sudan, Libya, Jordan and Saudi Arabia, as well as planned links with Greece and Italy, which will support cross-border trade in clean electricity.

He also noted that the updated national energy strategy targets increasing the share of renewable energy to 45% of total electricity generation by 2028, while continuing efforts to localize electrical equipment manufacturing and attract foreign investment.

Additionally, the minister reviewed the ongoing projects to improve grid efficiency, expand battery energy storage, upgrade electricity distribution networks and reduce reliance on conventional fuels.

World.title: Egypt, Bosnia discuss boosting tourism cooperation
World.content:
Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy discussed with Bosnia and Herzegovina’s Minister of Foreign Trade and Economic Relations Stasa Kosarac on Sunday, July 26, 2026, ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in tourism during a meeting at the Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM).

Fathy highlighted the strong ties between the two countries and their shared commitment to expanding cooperation, particularly in the fields of tourism and antiquities.

He also reviewed the outcome of his recent visit to Bosnia and Herzegovina, including talks on advancing bilateral tourism cooperation.

The discussions focused on increasing tourist flows between the two countries, promoting their tourism products and expanding air connectivity to support travel and tourism.

The two ministers also explored cooperation in tourism training and capacity building, as well as mechanisms for activating a memorandum of understanding on tourism cooperation signed during Fathy’s recent visit to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

They further discussed participation in Expo 2027 in Belgrade, describing the event as an opportunity to promote the tourism destinations of both countries and organize business-to-business (B2B) meetings between tourism stakeholders to explore new avenues of cooperation.

Following the meeting, Kosarac and his delegation toured the Grand Egyptian Museum and the Giza Pyramids, accompanied by Fathy.

World.title: FM asserts Egypt’s full solidarity with Kuwait
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Egyptian Expatriates Badr Abdelatty asserted Egypt’s full solidarity with Kuwait, its leadership, government and people.

He also asserted Egypt’s condemnation of all unjustified attacks targeting the country’s security, stability and sovereignty.

The remarks came during a phone call between Abdelatty and Kuwaiti Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah as part of ongoing consultations and coordination between the two brotherly countries on regional developments and efforts to de-escalate tensions and restore security and stability across the region.

During the call, Abdelatty conveyed the greetings of President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to Kuwaiti Emir Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah and Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Khaled Al-Hamad Al-Sabah.

The two ministers also discussed regional and international efforts aimed at reducing tensions.

Abdelatty stressed the importance of an immediate halt to all military actions and escalation, a return to negotiations and prioritizing political and diplomatic solutions to contain growing tensions and preserve regional security and stability.

He emphasized that the security and stability of the Gulf are an integral part of Arab national security, underscoring the importance of adhering to the principles of good neighborliness, respecting state sovereignty and refraining from interference in the internal affairs of other countries.

Abdelatty also briefed his Kuwaiti counterpart on Egypt’s intensive consultations with a number of regional and international partners to advance de-escalation efforts.

He stressed the importance of maintaining close coordination and consultation between Egypt and Kuwait in the coming period and continuing joint efforts to support initiatives aimed at restoring security and stability in the region.

For his part, the Kuwaiti foreign minister praised Egypt’s commitment to continuous consultation with Kuwait and commended Cairo’s firm stance condemning the attacks directed against Kuwait.

World.title: Egyptian MP proposes replacing ‘housewife’ on national ID with ‘generation maker’
World.content:
Egyptian Senator Sherine Sabry proposed replacing the term “housewife” with “Generation Maker,” in the job title in the national ID, asserting that this change better reflects the true role of women within the family and society.

Sabry explained that a woman who dedicates herself to raising her children performs a vital task, no less important than any other job, and contributes to building generations capable of developing the nation, Youm7 reported on Sunday.

The term “housewife” is no longer appropriate given the current era and the unprecedented focus the country is placing on women’s empowerment, she noted.

She noted that the political leadership has given Egyptian women significant attention, granting them numerous rights and opportunities in various fields.

The MP emphasized that women who choose to dedicate themselves to raising their families also perform a role worthy of respect and appreciation.

She explained that bestowing the title “Generation Maker” upon women would boost the morale of Egyptian women and enhance their sense of the value of their vital role in shaping future generations.

Appreciating the role of the mother in raising children is a real investment in the future of society, Sabry added, and that changing the title represents a moral message that reflects the status of women who shape the course of future generations.

World.title: Egypt welcomes Ireland’s ban on imports from Israeli settlements
World.content:
Egypt welcomed on Sunday Ireland’s passage of a law prohibiting the import of goods from Israeli settlements and the completion of the necessary constitutional and legislative procedures for its enactment.

An Egyptian Foreign Ministry statement explained that this important stance reflects a commitment to the provisions of international law and resolutions of international legitimacy.

It also affirms an utter rejection of illegal Israeli settlement activities that violate the rights of the Palestinian people and undermine chances of achieving a just and lasting peace.

Egypt reiterated its call to the European Union and the international community to take similar legal and practical measures to ensure that they do not contribute, directly or indirectly, to supporting or perpetuating illegal settlements.

Egypt also reaffirmed its unwavering support for the legitimate and inalienable rights of the Palestinian people, stressing that achieving security and stability in the Middle East requires ending the Israeli occupation and establishing an independent Palestinian state within the June 4, 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital.

World.title: Why Venezuela can’t access $4 billion in gold that could help with earthquake recovery
World.content:
It’s a fight for control over a stash of gold locked away in one of the world’s largest and most secure vaults, but this is no 18th century pirate novel or bank heist movie.

It’s the situation facing the Venezuelan government as it attempts to navigate its way through political upheaval and the aftermath of last month’s devastating twin earthquakes.

Caracas wants the Bank of England to return the 31 tons of gold bars it deposited there in 2008, saying it needs the money to pay for recovery efforts following the disaster that killed thousands of people and caused an economic hit equivalent to six percent of the country’s GDP, according to the United Nations Development Programme.

While it’s not unusual for the UK’s central bank to hold the gold reserves of other countries – with one of the world’s largest vaults it holds some 400,000 gold bars, including those of dozens of other nations – in this case, there’s a problem.

Nicolas Maduro, Venezuela’s former president, touches a stack of 12 Kilogram gold ingots during a news conference on the country’s cryptocurrency in Caracas on March 22, 2018. Carlos Becerra/Bloomberg/Getty Images

The fate of Venezuela’s gold bars – worth up to an estimated US$4 billion in today’s money – has been in limbo for years amid a years-long dispute involving the British government and Venezuela’s former President Nicolas Maduro.

The bank froze the gold after the UK – along with the US and numerous other countries – refused to recognize Maduro as the winner of Venezuela’s disputed 2018 presidential election.

It has been the subject of a long-running legal battle ever since, but with Maduro now in custody in New York following his capture by US forces in January, Caracas sees an opportunity to get its money back.

Since Maduro’s capture, his former deputy Delcy Rodríguez has been made acting president and has set about restoring diplomatic relations with the US – opening up her country’s oil sector to US investment, releasing some political prisoners and aligning her government with Washington’s regional projects.

Now she’s hoping for a similar thaw in the stand-off with the UK.

The Bank of England building in the City of London financial district on November 7, 2025. Toby Melville/Reuters

“That gold belongs to our people and should be used to address the terrible, tragic consequences of this double earthquake,” Rodríguez said on state television this month. “Venezuela has the resources to recover, to get back on its feet,” she added.

It’s hard to know what percentage of Venezuela’s total gold reserves the 31 bars represent. Around 20 years ago, the country was known to have some 300 tons of gold, but that figure is now thought to be much lower. The World Gold Council has more recently put the figure at 161 tons.

Rodríguez has even written to King Charles III, asking for the gold to be released for use in reconstruction efforts, though as a constitutional monarch he does not get involved in political disputes.

Whether the UK government itself will listen is, as yet, unclear. In the days following Maduro’s ouster, the UK’s then-Foreign Secretary Yvette Cooper said the UK still did not recognize the Venezuelan government.

When asked by a UK lawmaker specifically about the release of the gold, Cooper said, “the Bank of England must make decisions independently, but our principles focus on maintaining and promoting stability and the transition to democracy.”

Cooper, however, has since been replaced as foreign minister following the UK’s appointment this week of a new prime minister, Andy Burnham, and it’s too early to know what position her successor – Ed Miliband – will take on the issue.

Delcy Rodriguez, Venezuela’s acting president, at a press conference in Caracas on July 2 after the double earthquake that struck the country. Jesus Vargas/Getty Images

Still, Rodriguez has had some good news when it comes to winning over doubters, recently ending a seven-year freeze in relations with the International Monetary Fund. That move enabled Venezuela this month to secure $346 million from its own reserve resources to fund reconstruction efforts.

Whether she can have similar success with the Bank of England remains to be seen. At the time of publication, neither the Bank of England nor the Central Bank of Venezuela had responded to CNN’s enquiries on the state of the gold dispute.

At least for now, it seems, all that glitters … remains locked up overseas.

World.title: Ukraine sees highest civilian casualties since 2022
World.content:
Ukraine has seen the highest number of civilian casualties in the war with Russia this month for more than four years, according to government figures.

Russian attacks this month have killed at least 377 civilians and injured 2,129, making it the deadliest month of the war since April 2022.

The attacks this month have included a high number of ballistic missiles, which are difficult to intercept, and have targeted the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, on multiple occasions.

Russia has used nearly 1,700 drones, more than 1,630 guided aerial bombs, and more than 50 ballistic missiles in the last week, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“We must undercut Russia’s gamble on ballistic terror,” Zelensky said in a post on X Sunday.

“Every interceptor missile right now is literally helping save lives if it is here, in Ukrainian systems, not in our partners’ warehouses,” he added.

To underline Zelensky’s point, authorities said 10-year-old child and an adult were killed and three other people were injured in a Russian drone attack on a supermarket in Chernihiv on Sunday, according to local authorities.

Zelensky has frequently appealed for more Patriot and other air defense systems capable of intercepting ballistic missiles.

Ukraine has continued its drone and missile campaign against Russian energy infrastructure in the last week, with several refineries targeted. The campaign has led Russia to extend its ban on diesel exports until the end of the year.

Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said Saturday the government will consider lifting the ban on diesel exports “as the market recovers.”

“Many areas of Russia and occupied Ukraine continue to struggle with fuel shortages, though Russian officials are increasingly posturing that the economic situation and fuel crisis are stabilizing,” the Institute for the Study of War in Washington said Saturday.

Russia has retaliated by attacking fuel stations in northern Ukraine and has also stepped up its attacks on Ukrainian ports in the Black Sea and on the Danube river.

For the third consecutive day, the Romanian air force Sunday shot down a Russian drone over the Black Sea. The defence ministry said that the drone was shot down above Romanian territorial waters.

Romanian President Nicusor Dan said that it was “inadmissible and intolerable” for Russia to violate Romanian airspace.

The Russian ambassador in Bucharest was summoned to the Foreign Ministry Sunday.

World.title: Police Deny Cancelling Brian Mundubile’s Campaign Rallies
World.content:
The Zambia Police Service has dismissed claims that it cancelled campaign rallies for National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity (NRPUP) president Brian Mundubile on the Copperbelt, stating that all scheduled rallies have proceeded as planned.

Police Spokesperson Godfrey Chilabi said the confusion arose because the party allegedly conducted roadshows and processions without notifying the police after obtaining clearance for rallies.

Mr. Chilabi explained that while all approved rallies had taken place, police only intervened when supporters attempted to hold processions that had not been communicated in advance.

He noted that, unlike rallies held at fixed venues, roadshows require prior planning because they use public roads shared by motorists and other road users.

According to Mr. Chilabi, advance notice enables police to deploy officers, plan routes and inform the public where traffic may be affected during political processions.

He added that allowing unplanned roadshows could endanger both supporters and motorists, as drivers may unexpectedly encounter large crowds on public roads.

Mr. Chilabi also said police have a responsibility to safeguard businesses and members of the public, noting that large processions can sometimes create opportunities for criminal activity.

He reiterated that the Zambia Police Service remains committed to ensuring all political parties are able to campaign freely, provided organisers comply with established procedures designed to protect lives, property and public order.

World.title: Zambian Musician T-Sean Mourns Wife Sharai Mulenga
World.content:
Prominent Zambian musician, songwriter and producer Richard Mulenga, popularly known as T-Sean, has lost his wife, Sharai Mulonda Mulenga.

The sad news was announced by the Zambia Association of Musicians (ZAM), which said the music fraternity is mourning alongside the award-winning artist during this difficult time.

In a statement, ZAM Publicity Secretary Edmond Mbanga Miti said the association’s executive committee and entire membership were deeply saddened by the passing of Mrs. Mulenga.

Mr. Miti said the association’s thoughts and prayers are with T-Sean, as well as the Mulonda and Mulenga families, as they grieve the loss of their loved one.

ZAM has also called on fellow musicians, fans and members of the public to keep T-Sean and his family in their prayers and offer them comfort during this period of mourning.

The association said details regarding the funeral gathering and burial arrangements will be announced in due course.

World.title: Kalumbila holds annual KGS symposium
World.content:
Government has reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that every girl has access to quality education through the Keeping Girls in School and Beyond Initiative under the Girls’ Education and Women’s Empowerment and Livelihood for Human Capital (GEWEL II) Project.

Over K6.2 million has been disbursed in Kalumbila District since 2025 to support vulnerable girls’ access to secondary education.

Speaking when she officially opened the 2026 Keeping Girls in School Annual Case Management Academic Symposium in Kalumbila District of North-Western Province, District Commissioner, Brenda Sankisa, said empowering girls through education is key to national development.

Ms Sankisa said the government, with support from the World Bank and other cooperating partners, is implementing the GEWEL II Project across the country to increase girls’ access to secondary education through the provision of education grants, boarding support and other learner welfare interventions.

She said the initiative also provides reusable sanitary towels, psychosocial counselling, academic support and interventions aimed at preventing School-Related Gender-Based Violence in schools.

And District Education Board Secretary, Thompson Lungu, said the Keeping Girls in School Initiative continues to make a significant contribution towards improving school attendance and learner retention among vulnerable girls in the district.

Mr Lungu said Kalumbila District received K3.176 million in education grants in 2025, benefiting 3,970 girls, in addition to 880 reusable sanitary towels and 16 bicycles.

He added that the district has so far received K2.256 million for Term One and K834, 400 for Term Two education grant payments in 2026, as well as 3,650 reusable sanitary towels.

Meanwhile, Education Standards Officer for General Inspection, Bernard Kampolombo, urged girls to remain focused on their education and avoid early marriages, early pregnancies and other distractions.

District Planning Officer, Maseka Ella, called for strengthened efforts to eliminate School-Related Gender-Based Violence through increased awareness, stronger reporting systems and collective action by schools, parents and communities.

She reaffirmed the government’s commitment to creating safe, inclusive and supportive learning environments to ensure that every girl remains in school and reaches her full potential.

Held under the theme, “Empowering Girls – Creating Leaders for Tomorrow,” the symposium brought together government officials, education stakeholders, teachers, learners and community representatives to review progress made in supporting girls’ education.

World.title: Mundubile, Zulu walk to Chambishi rally after police blockade
World.content:
National Reconciliation Party for Unity and Prosperity presidential candidate Brian Mundubile and his running mate Makebi Zulu were yesterday forced to walk to a campaign rally in Chambishi after police allegedly attempted to block them from accessing the venue.

According to accounts of the incident, supporters resisted the police action and escorted the two leaders on foot to the rally venue while chanting slogans calling for change. The confrontation unfolded as the NRPUP duo sought to address supporters gathered for the campaign event.

Addressing the rally in Chambishi, and later a similar gathering in Mufulira, Mundubile promised to restore freedoms if elected, telling the crowd that Zambians had lived without peace and basic rights for the past five years.

“Firstly, I want to thank all of you. We know we are late because of Honourable Kambwili. The police tried to block us, but we were walking on foot. But do not worry, their time is up, all the lies they made in five years have been exposed,” Mundubile told supporters.

He said his team’s first priority upon taking office would be to work on restoring citizens’ rights. “You have stayed for five years without peace and rights. You have stayed like slaves because of the same laws that our friends introduced. So, the first thing we will do is bring back your rights. We want to bring back your freedom of expression, movement and freedom of worship,” he said.

Turning to the mining sector, Mundubile cautioned mining companies against involving themselves in Zambian politics, accusing certain mining houses of funding the ruling party to influence the outcome of the election.

“We have mining houses today that want to control the country’s democracy. There is one company, a mining house, that wants to select leadership. It is getting money and then paying the UPND. In return, the UPND are buying councillors and controlling democracy. Are you going to allow that? We want to send a very clear message to mining houses, come to Zambia, invest and stay away from politics. We will not sit idle and watch you fund politics, you want to change the democracy of this country. We are sending a warning to mining house. We will not sit idle and watch you alter the rights of our people,” he said.

Mundubile alleged that a specific mining house had been given favour by the Minister of Mines, saying it had saved almost one billion dollars out of an original obligation of nearly one billion dollars that Zambian leaders owed. He said this was part of a wider pattern of concessions extended to favoured investors at the expense of ordinary citizens.

“There is a certain mining house which was given favour by the Minister of Mines; we would debate in Parliament. It saved almost one billion dollars out of… it’s because of that one billion dollars that our leaders are going there,” said Mundubile.

He said the message he wanted to send to mining houses and their investors was straightforward. “This is where we see some candidates are given K20 million to withdraw. What is causing that is the money they have received from that mining house. It is giving them money so that they buy democracy. We will not accept that, we are independent,” he said.

Mundubile drew a broader link between mining sector concessions and the affordability crisis facing ordinary Zambians, arguing that reduced mineral wealth tax rates had come at the direct expense of citizens’ purchasing power.

“So, our friends, our investors, come into the country and work on what you are supposed to work for. Do not get involved in the issue of changing government. Your leaders failed to work for the people. In the past, they gave you tax waivers; they reduced mineral wealth tax from six percent to three percent. Because of that, you saved almost one billion dollars over the past three years. Now you are employing that money to try and destabilise the people’s choices. We will not accept that. It’s a warning to our friends, investors, come into the country and work on what you are supposed to work for. Do not get involved in the issue of changing government,” he said.

“It’s a warning to our friends to stay away from Zambian politics,” Mundubile added.

The rally in Chambishi and the subsequent event in Mufulira formed part of Mundubile’s continued campaign push across the Copperbelt, a province where mining sector policy and campaign financing allegations have increasingly featured in political messaging ahead of August general election.

World.title: Govt. commissions market shelter in Kaoma’s Luyanti Ward
World.content:
Government has commissioned a new market shelter in Luyanti Ward of Kaoma District in Western Province, aimed at providing safe, secure and dignified trading space for local entrepreneurs, with a special focus on women and youth.

Speaking during the event, Kaoma District Commissioner, Kashina Sheba, said the facility was constructed in response to the district’s growing demand for modern market infrastructure as commerce and economic activity expand.

“The facility we are commissioning has been constructed to respond to this growing demand by providing adequate trading space for our hard working entrepreneurs,” she said.

Mrs Sheba described the market shelter as a safe, secure and conducive environment for conducting business and reaffirmed the government’s commitment to empowering local entrepreneurs, particularly women and young people, who form the backbone of the local economy.

She revealed that government seeks to increase access to markets for local producers and traders, promoting entrepreneurship and creating opportunities for business growth.

The District Commissioner said through the market shelter, government supports skills development and economic empowerment initiatives, and contributes to the overall economic growth and sustainable development of the district.

She disclosed that the market shelter was constructed at a cost of K671, 000 using the Constituency Development Fund – CDF.

Ms Sheba further urged the community to take collective responsibility to maintain the infrastructure so that it continues to serve both present and future generations.

Speaking earlier, Development Committee Chairman, Ohlas Wina, indicated that marketeers had for years been appealing to previous governments to construct a market shelter but to no avail, until the UPND administration under President Hichilema came into power.

Mr Wina added that traders were previously operating from makeshift grass-thatched structures, but can now trade from a modern facility.

A trader, Lucy Mutelo, thanked government for the gesture, saying marketeers had been suffering selling in the sun after their makeshift market was blown off by winds.

Another trader, Charity Simasiku, said the new shelter will improve livelihoods as traders will now be selling in a conducive environment, unlike the crowded makeshift market they previously used.

The project is part of the government’s broader agenda under President Hakainde Hichilema to promote rural development, economic empowerment, and improved service delivery through CDF-funded projects.

World.title: Govt. commissions two dams in Luangeni constituency
World.content:
Government has commissioned two dams, Lunyike and Feni, in Luangeni Constituency of Chipata District, valued at over K33 Million.

Ministry of Water Development and Sanitation Permanent Secretary, Romas Kamanga, says the total value for Lunyike Dam is K16, 658, 555.12, while Feni Dam cpst K16, 990, 431. 26

The Permanent Secretary explained that Lunyike Dam was a special request from the late Paramount Chief Mpezeni to have it rehabilitated for the betterment of his subjects.

He further indicated that both dams will benefit a population of at least 35,300 people and 21,000 livestock.

“You may wish to note that the Lunyike Dam will directly benefit approximately 9,000 people, while the Feni Dam will directly benefit more than 34,400 people. In addition, the dams will provide reliable water for approximately 6,000 livestock at Lunyike and 15,000 livestock at Feni,” he mentioned.

Eastern Province Permanent Secretary, Paul Thole, who was represented by Eastern Province Director of Finance, Vincent Sampa, said government is putting up measures to ensure water is valued at all costs.

Mr Thole said projects like the ones just commissioned, ensure that members of the public are empowered.

He has urged benefiting communities to maximise the availability of the water bodies in their areas.

“Come up with gardens, water is here. The gardens will economically empower you,” he said.

And Chipata District Commissioner, Elidah Banda, who was represented by the District Administrative Officer, Kapambwe Sikazwe, also re-echoed the importance of safeguarding the facilities.

Meanwhile, the contractor of Lunyike dam, Construction of Africa Managing Director, Rodgers Mugala, said the dam had incorporated the local people throughout the rehabilitation period.

Meanwhile, Philimon Chirwa, who represented the beneficiary communities, expressed gratitude to the government for rehabilitating the dams, while calling for the rehabilitation of Msipazi Dam.

Sable Transport Limited Company was engaged for the rehabilitation of Feni Dam.

World.title: Kalaba Says Defections Do Not Reflect Instability in Citizens First
World.content:
Citizens First (CF) President Harry Kalaba has dismissed suggestions that recent defections from his party are a sign of internal instability, saying it is normal for political parties to gain and lose members over time.

Speaking through an interview, Mr. Kalaba was asked about the departure of several high-profile members, including his former running mate Moses Nawa and former ally Greyford Monde, who recently joined the ruling UPND Alliance.

The interviewer also referred to Mr. Kalaba’s earlier split from the Democratic Party, which led to the formation of Citizens First, noting that several prominent figures have since left his political camp.

In response, Mr. Kalaba compared Citizens First to a bus travelling from Lusaka to Kawambwa, saying some passengers may get off along the way, but the bus will still reach its intended destination.

He said the party remains focused on its long-term vision despite the recent defections, arguing that movement of members between political parties is a normal feature of democratic politics and should not be viewed as a sign of weakness.

Mr. Kalaba added that alliances are dynamic and that political partners sometimes part ways when they no longer share the same objectives. Quoting Amos 3:3, he said, “Two cannot walk together unless they agree.”

He further stated that those who choose to leave the party should be free to do so without resentment, while new members should be welcomed.

Mr. Kalaba also argued that the movement of people in and out of Citizens First demonstrates that the party remains active and politically relevant, adding that political parties receiving little public attention rarely experience the same level of membership movement.

The Citizens First leader is currently campaigning across the country ahead of the 13 August General Election, where he is seeking to become Zambia’s next President.

World.title: Namwala East Independent Candidate Responds to President’s Remarks, Alleges Campaign Intimidation
World.content:
Independent aspiring Member of Parliament for Namwala East, Silent Hapompwe, has responded to remarks made by President Hakainde Hichilema during a recent campaign rally in Namwala.

In a video statement, Mr. Hapompwe alleged that the President personally called him and urged him to withdraw his candidature in support of the UPND candidate.

Mr. Hapompwe said he declined the request, stating that the Constitution of Zambia gives him the right to contest the parliamentary seat. He added that the confidence and support shown by the people of Namwala East have strengthened his resolve to remain in the race.

The independent candidate further alleged that independent and opposition candidates in the constituency are facing intimidation during the campaign period.

He claimed that three vehicles with obscured registration plates have been seen in the area disrupting campaign meetings. According to Mr. Hapompwe, the matter has been reported to Niko Police Post and Namwala Police Station, but no action has been taken so far.

Mr. Hapompwe also said he is prepared to take election observers to the location of the vehicles so they can independently verify his claims.

The allegations have not been independently verified, and there has been no immediate response from State House or the Zambia Police Service.
