Tech.title: This Is Donald Trump’s AI Brain Trust
Tech.content:
As China’s open-weight AI models become increasingly powerful, the Trump administration is relying on a small group of officials to decide whether and what restrictions should be imposed.

The group is scattered across several departments and agencies in Washington—and they all have differing views on the best way to keep the US ahead in the race against China.

“It’s not an argument with two sides, it’s an argument with ten sides,” one senior White House official tells WIRED about the state of affairs.

With little interagency coordination in the administration, policy will almost certainly end up being set by the people with the most influence with the president. In an effort to map the forces at play, here’s a list of the current power brokers involved in the race to regulate AI.

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick

Photo-Illustration: Darrell Jackson; Getty Images

Howard Lutnick has increasingly emerged as an influential part of the intra-administration split over AI, in part because it oversees export controls through the Bureau of Industry and Security.

Lutnick, according to people familiar, has contemplated ways to create incentives for top US labs to create their own open-weight models to counterbalance China, and he has spoken with leaders at a number of AI labs.

On Thursday, Lutnick played down the capabilities of Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3 model, writing in an X post that his team found it performed worse than leading US frontier models in key benchmark tests.

Lutnick appears to be straddling a middle ground on regulation. He imposed export controls on Anthropic to bring them to heel—but has been more freewheeling than others in the White House.

Arvind Raman, Acting Director, CAISI

Photo-Illustration: Darrell Jackson; Getty Images

Arvind Raman has become Lutnick’s top deputy as the acting chief at the Center for AI Standards and Innovation, which sits inside the Commerce Department and serves as the industry’s primary point of contact with the government.

Tech.title: Best Laptops for College Students (2026): MacBooks and Beyond
Tech.content:
College laptops don’t have to be embarrassing. Nor do they have to be overly expensive. There are a lot of great, well-designed laptops for college students that combine long battery life, easy portability, and the performance needed for everyday coursework.

In my decade-plus of reviewing laptops, I’ve tested hundreds of models. If someone asked me what to buy for a college student, these are the ones I’d suggest.

Be sure to check out our other computing guides, including the Best Laptops, Best Budget Laptops, Best MacBooks, Best Windows Laptops, Best Gaming Laptops, Best Chromebooks, and Best Laptop Bags.

Updated July 2026: I’ve added the HP OmniBook 3 and Dell 14 Plus as picks, and the Dell 14S as an honorable mention. I’ve also removed some options that have become too expensive after price increases.

The Best Overall College Laptop

The MacBook Air (9/10, WIRED Recommends) is my choice for best overall laptop for everyone. But college students have specific needs—and often, specific budgets. In addition to being affordable, a college student’s laptop should be lightweight and easy to carry around. The MacBook Neo (7/10, WIRED Recommends) fits the bill perfectly. It’s only 2.7 pounds and starts at just $699. It also has a smaller display, which helps it fit on those tiny lecture-hall desks. What makes the MacBook Neo special, however, is its lack of compromise around quality. It’s a gorgeous piece of hardware, with fun colors, an excellent trackpad, a beautiful display, and that Apple “it” factor. I recommend the $699 model, which gets you twice the storage and a Touch ID fingerprint reader.

Of course, this isn’t a laptop without downsides. Apple invested its efforts in the front-of-screen experience, but made cuts to performance, ports, and memory to keep costs low. The limitation of 8 GB of memory is my biggest sticking point with this device; it means you’ll need to be mindful of how many applications, tabs, and background tasks you have running at once. Also, ghe Neo can connect to only one external display at a time.

The Best Windows Alternative

Laptop pricing has skyrocketed over the past few months, which has made it harder to recommend some of the flashier new laptops of the year. Fortunately, many really great laptops from 2025 are still available to buy. The Dell 14 Plus is a great example. It’s one of the few laptops you can get for less than $1,000 that doesn’t force you to make serious compromises. It’s not the world’s prettiest device, but the display is surprisingly sharp, bright, and colorful. The computer’s touchpad and keyboard are both high-quality, and it has tons of ports.

The newer Dell 14S came out more recently with the intention to replace the 14 Plus. The new model comes with an OLED display and superb battery life. While it’s a solid option (see Other Laptops to Consider, below), it starts at a pricey $1,350, and the screen has a lower resolution. For a college student, the Dell 14 Plus is the better buy right now.

A Featherlight College Laptop

If the idea of buying a laptop with only 8 GB of RAM in 2026 seems questionable (I don’t blame you for feeling this way), I recommend the Asus Zenbook A14 (WIRED Recommends, 8/10). Not only does it come with 16 GB of RAM, but it’s the lightest laptop you can buy right now at just 2.4 pounds. You’ll hardly notice it in your laptop bag when you’re trekking across campus.

The price of the Zenbook A14 varies quite a bit, typically between $600 and $1,000, but there’s often a deal available that makes it an affordable option. There’s also the 2026 model, which comes with the second-gen Snapdragon X2 chip. At $1,600, though, it’s just not worth the extra cash—especially for a college student on a budget.

The Best Cheap College Laptop

The options listed above are fairly affordable, all coming in at less than $1,000. But even if your budget is $600 or less, trust that you can still get a solidly performing laptop with good battery life. The HP OmniBook 5 frequently sells for around $600 or less, making it an adequate MacBook Neo alternative. Better yet, HP’s laptop ships with more memory and storage. The OLED panel display is fantastic too, and the laptop is remarkably thin. The only significant downside is the touchpad, which feels clumsy to use. I could get used to it over time, but it is the Achilles’ heel of this OmniBook 5 (and nearly all budget laptops, for that matter).

If you need a super-cheap Windows laptop, though, there’s really only one I’d recommend that’s cheaper than the OmniBook 5, and it comes from the same family. I tested the HP OmniBook 3 and found that it shares a lot of the positive qualities of its older sibling. The OLED screen is great, as is the keyboard and overall build quality. Most important, the battery life is top-notch for a device of this price. It’s not as thin as the OmniBook 5 though, and the 1920 x 1200 resolution stretched across the 16-inch screen is unfortunate. There’s also a 14-inch version, which I think is a smarter buy.

But there’s not a single other Windows laptop I’d feel good about suggesting someone buy at this price. Intel-powered laptops at this price tend to struggle with performance and battery life, while other cheap Qualcomm Snapdragon X laptops like the Asus Vivobook 14 use terrible displays to drag the prices down.

The Best College Laptop Under $500

Photograph: Luke Larsen Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Asus Chromebook CX15 $307 Amazon (8 GB)

Chromebooks are becoming increasingly tough to sell. Snapdragon X-powered laptops like the HP OmniBook 3 above have made budget-tier Chromebooks, with weak battery life and poor screens, harder to justify. Furthermore, Chromebooks have the added problem of incompatibility with certain software you might need in college.

However, Chromebooks are still the way to go if you need something—anything—for as little money as possible. If you’re low on cash and just need basic internet access, the $200 Asus Chromebook CX15 is your best bet. The screen and touchpad are the main downfalls, but it’s fairly portable and modern-looking, and the battery life is decent enough. My bar is fairly low for a $200 laptop, but the CX15 outdoes other competitors at this price.

Best Powerful College Laptops for STEM

Not everyone needs a powerful laptop to tote around campus. But if you’re in a STEM field, or even just like to play games on the weekend, buying a single, powerful laptop to serve as your main machine at college is a good idea. Unfortunately, no gaming laptop is powerful, portable, and affordable—you can only have two of those three things. Letting go of the portability priority, the best option I’ve tested is the Lenovo LOQ 15 (8/10, WIRED Recommends). It’s hard to beat a discrete graphics processing unit (GPU) for raw performance, which is exactly what the RTX 5060 in the LOQ 15 delivers. Though the price often creeps above $1,000, it’s still the most affordable gaming laptop you can buy that doesn’t suffer from severe performance compromises.

Photograph: Luke Larsen Save to wishlist Save to wishlist Razer Blade 16 (2025) $2,400 Razer

Now, if you can afford to dish out some more money, I’d point you to either the Razer Blade 16 or the MacBook Pro. Despite the thin profile of the Razer Blade 16 (8/10 WIRED Recommends), you can configure it with up to an RTX 5090 graphics card. Aside from the compromise of a high price, battery life is a limitation. You might run out halfway through your day, forcing you to find an outlet in a hurry. If you happen to need performance for gaming on the weekends in addition to your schoolwork, the Razer Blade 16 is expensive but totally worth it. I prefer the smaller Razer Blade 14 as a college laptop, but it’s no longer available to purchase right now.

The MacBook Pro, whether you opt for the M5 Pro, M5 Max, or an older chip, resolves the issue of battery life. Gaming isn’t its strongest capability, but it delivers exceptional performance in creative applications and can be equipped with up to 128 GB of unified memory for serious on-device AI workloads.

Other Laptops to Consider for College

Photograph: Luke Larsen

Dell 14S for $1,350: While this laptop is more expensive than I’d like, it’s a solid choice. The chassis is more polished than that of the Dell 14 Plus, and the glossy OLED screen gives the device a premium look. I wish it were brighter, or at least handled glare better.

Tech.title: Measles Is Becoming So Common That Treatments May Soon Be Needed
Tech.content:
Up until recently, measles vaccination has been so effective that there’s been little medical or financial incentive to develop treatments for the disease.

But as measles cases hit a 35-year high and vaccination rates continue to decline in the US, a handful of biotech companies and academic groups have started working on measles treatments for those infected with the virus as well as vulnerable individuals needing short-term protection. It will likely be years, however, before these countermeasures are available, and it’s even more uncertain if those who refuse vaccines would take such treatments.

Fueled by large outbreaks in South Carolina and Utah, the US had already surpassed last year’s 2,289 measles cases, and it’s only July. For comparison, there were just 285 cases in all of 2024.

Because measles is so contagious, at least 95 percent of people in a community need to receive both doses of the measles vaccine to protect immunocompromised individuals and infants under 12 months old who are too young to be vaccinated. But measles vaccination rates have dipped well below that in many places across the country.

Young children are the most susceptible to severe complications from measles. The virus can cause pneumonia by damaging the respiratory tract lining directly and by suppressing the immune system, leaving them susceptible to bacterial infections. It can also cause deafness and potentially fatal brain damage. Without a measles-specific treatment, doctors rely on supportive care such as preventing dehydration, managing breathing difficulties, and administering steroids for inflammation. Vitamin A is sometimes given to patients because the virus can deplete levels of it in the body, but the supplement has no effect on the virus itself.

“What we’re seeing now as we get a resurgence of measles in communities is a horrible lack of options when somebody gets exposed,” says Michael Mina, an epidemiologist and chief medical officer of Invivyd, a Connecticut-based biotech company.

Invivyd is developing a type of therapy for measles known as a monoclonal antibody, which mimics natural antibodies the immune system makes to fight off disease. Given via IV or injection, monoclonal antibodies were widely used to treat and prevent Covid-19, especially in immunocompromised individuals who didn’t mount a strong immune response to the vaccines. Their protective effects can last up to a few months.

Invivyd, which developed a monoclonal antibody for Covid, has been getting inquiries from health care providers about when a similar therapy will be available for measles. In the event of a local measles outbreak, a monoclonal antibody could provide short-term protection to those at high risk of contracting the virus. Invivyd has not yet tested its measles antibody in humans, but Mina says the company is compiling the data needed for the Food and Drug Administration to sign off on clinical trials.

At the La Jolla Institute for Immunology, president and CEO Erica Ollmann Saphire has been trying to understand the human antibody response to measles. In May, Saphire and her team published a study describing human antibodies capable of blocking infection by binding to key sites on the measles virus. An infusion of these antibodies resulted in a 500-fold lower viral load in rodents.

A key step toward getting these treatments into human trials will be manufacturing monoclonal antibodies at scale, which is a costly and complex process. Clinical trials cost millions of dollars to run, and pharmaceutical partners are usually needed to fund them. But measles treatments could be a hard sell for pharma companies. Drugs for infectious diseases aren’t usually big money-makers because of the sporadic nature of outbreaks and short treatment courses.

Tech.title: Soundcore Nebula P1i Projector Review: New Design, Classic Pitfalls
Tech.content:
Soundcore has been having some fun lately. Apparently, bored by designing tiny can-sized projectors like the Nebula Capsule 3, the brand has become much more adventurous in their designs. I've recently tested the Nebula P1 and enormous Nebula X1 Pro, both of which feature pop-out and positionable surround sound speaker options.

These are the flagship models, but I've spent the past couple of months with the Nebula P1i, which has those same pop-out speakers in a more budget-friendly bundle. It's well-priced and has an easy-to-use design, while the picture quality is solid and the audio is punchy. While it lacks more premium features of some of the best projectors, it could be a decent choice for impromptu movie nights around the house.

Getting Started

Google TV has transformed the projector market. I used to dread having to work through endless sub-menus and inputting Netflix and Wi-Fi passwords using a fiddly remote control. Here, a quick QR code scan and the convenience of my smartphone means I’m watching Kill Bill Vol. 1 on a 60-inch screen less than five minutes after unboxing.

Google TV provides easy access to all the major streaming platforms including Netflix, YouTube, Disney+, HBO Max, Apple TV and Prime Video. You can also plug in via USB-A or HDMI 2.0 with ARC.

Tech.title: It’s Becoming Clear Why Black Holes Never Run Out of Fuel
Tech.content:
It is believed that nearly every large galaxy in the universe has a supermassive black hole at its center, with a mass ranging from millions to billions of times that of the sun.

Black holes grow by consuming surrounding matter, but in the process they also eject powerful energy jets. These jets heat the surrounding gas, delaying the formation of new stars and affecting the growth of the galaxy as a whole.

This has long presented researchers with a puzzle. As a black hole emits jets and heats the surrounding gas, the gas that would otherwise be consumed by the black hole—that is, its energy source—is dispersed far away. And yet, why is it that black holes do not “run out of fuel” and instead continue to grow?

To explain this mystery, researchers proposed the following hypothesis: Gas blown away by the heat eventually cools in interstellar space and condenses into thin, thread-like structures called filaments. These filaments then fall back toward the black hole.

A newly published study has brought researchers closer to confirming this idea. An international team led by Julie Hlavacek-Larrondo, a professor at the University of Montreal, observed the central galaxy NGC 4696 in the Centaurus Cluster and demonstrated a connection between such filaments and its central black hole.

A “Cosmic Recycling System” of Heating and Cooling

NGC 4696 is located about 145 million light-years from Earth. It has been the subject of extensive observation in the past, including the discovery of an S-shaped spiral structure around its central black hole.

For this study, the team observed the galaxy's central region for approximately eight hours using the James Webb Space Telescope's (JWST) Near-Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec). The observations achieved a resolution fine enough to distinguish structures only about 30 light-years across. To put this into perspective, if a galaxy 300,000 light-years wide were scaled to the size of a soccer field, this would be equivalent to identifying a single marble placed on that field from a distance of 50 kilometers.

The observed motion of the gas revealed that the S-shaped spiral is actually a rotating disk of gas orbiting the black hole. The disk is about 800 light-years in diameter, with gas pulled by the black hole's immense gravity rotating at several hundred kilometers per second. A velocity difference of roughly 600 kilometers per second was measured between opposite edges of the disk.

Tech.title: Comic-Con 2026 Trailers Are Here: Check Out Carrie, Reacher, Queen of the Damned and More
Tech.content:
Saturday’s rollout of news and trailers at San Diego Comic-Con wrapped up three days of big reveals, and CNET was in attendance to keep up with it all. Marvel’s Hall H presentation was highly anticipated, but there aren’t any new teasers to share.

Still, we want to make sure you’re clued in to all the biggest trailer drops and release dates for upcoming movies and TV shows. Though fans got an early round of official trailers for Clayface, Other Mommy and Avengers: Doomsday ahead of the convention, Apple TV, Warner Bros., Prime Video, Paramount and more studios continued to push out sneak peeks and thrilling teasers for their slates.

What are the must-watch trailers so far? All of them, basically. You can catch Carrie, The Rings of Power, Lanterns, Avatar: Seven Havens and others, and also be sure to scroll through all the SDCC merch reveals that you may’ve missed, too.

Carrie

Stephen King gave his stamp of approval and is an executive producer for Prime Video’s Carrie TV series that’s set to premiere on Oct. 7. From director Mike Flanagan, the show drops Carrie into a modernized world where cell phones and the internet give bullies a larger audience. But just because the novel took place in 1974 and it’s 2026 now, it doesn’t mean this new take won’t have Carrie’s telekinetic abilities setting things on fire.

Lanterns

When the Earth-heavy Lanters teaser dropped from DC a few months ago, it felt pretty full. There was Kyle Chandler’s Hal Jordan challenging John Stewart’s worthiness to carry a Green Lantern Corp. ring, desert-bound conspiracy vibes, flashbacks to John’s childhood and even a flash of Guy Gardner on screen. DC teased the ring’s powers, but with its new Comic-Con trailer released on Friday, things ramp up when Manhunters arrive on the planet to take out the Lanterns. Take a look at the interstellar enforcers and Sinestro in the trailer, and prepare for the series to land on HBO Max on Aug. 16.

Blade Runner 2099

Several years in the making, Blade Runner 2099 will debut on Nov. 25 on Prime Video. The eight-episode limited series is a sequel to the 2017 film Blade Runner 2049 and stars Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer, along with Sheila Atim, Katelyn Rose Downey, Dimitri Abold and Daniel Rigby among the cast.

Set in an alternate version of LA where replicants run things, and the humans play second fiddle, the series sees Yeoh’s replicant Olwen chasing down outlaw replicants who’ve gone missing. With her own shelf life on a ticking clock, the stakes are high for her and for her human fugitive partner, Cora (Schafer).

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, Season 3

Remember in the Lord of the Rings trilogy, all that talk of “the One Ring to rule them all?” Well, season 3 of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is going to be all about that. These episodes take place five years after season 2, and by the looks of things, Sauron’s war with the elves is going strong, and he’s expanded his power across the majority of Middle-earth. Now all Sauron has to do is forge that pesky One Ring so he can, well, rule them all.

Jamie Campbell Bower joins the cast as the elven lord Celeborn, Galadriel’s husband and noble warrior in the fight against Sauron. This season will also introduce Nazgnagôl, better known as the Ringwraiths, in an early form of the corrupted ringholders in the story. The new season debuts on Nov. 11 on Prime Video.

Reacher, season 4

Season 4 of Reacher, which is based on Gone Tomorrow, the 13th book in Lee Child’s hit novel series, finds Jack Reacher traveling from rural America to the streets of Manhattan. Switching gears from previous seasons, the new installment finds Reacher immersed in a political conspiracy, leaving him with few people he can trust.

Stuck on the streets of New York, with the FBI and CIA on the hunt for Jack Reacher, this season finds our hero once again immersed in a mission to bring evildoers to justice. It just so happens that this time, that bad guy is apparently running for president. Alan Ritchson is back as Reacher alongside series newcomers Christopher Rodriguez-Marquette, Sydell Noel, Agnez Mo, Anggun and Kevin Corrigan.

Neagley

Maria Sten’s Neagley has been one of Jack Reacher’s fiercest and most skilled protégés. Now in her own spinoff show, she’ll be taking shots in the name of justice and ends up uncovering something grimmer than imagined. Season 1 of the action series debuts on Prime Video on Sept. 16.

Queen of the Damned

AMC’s Interview With the Vampire series is poised to slide into its fourth season with a focus on the vampire Akasha and has titled the new season as Queen of the Damned. Season 3 (titled The Vampire Lestat) brought her into the story and introduced actor Sheila Atim as the very first vampire. Atim, along with co-stars Jacob Anderson, Assad Zaman and Eric Bogosian, appeared in Hall H to share the news.

Matchbox The Movie

Kids who played with Matchbox cars when they were young grow up and learn their friend is a CIA agent who gets them caught up in a case. That’s the premise of Apple TV’s new comedy film starring John Cena as the spy and Jessica Biel, Teyonah Parris, Sam Richardson and Arturo Castro as said friends. You can stream the movie on Oct. 9.

Neuromancer

Apple TV’s sci-fi shows tend to be top-notch, and the cyberpunk-themed Neuromancer looks like it could be a remarkable addition. Callum Turner is Case, a hacker who gets drawn into a dangerous life-or-death game involving espionage, artificial intelligence and deceit. Based on William Gibson’s 1984 novel, the TV adaptation will have 10 episodes and premiere on Jan. 22, 2027.

Coyote vs. Acme

Formerly shelved by Warner Bros. Discovery, the film is an animation-meets-live-action story that Ketchup Entertainment picked up and will open in theaters on Aug. 28. Fed up with Acme’s unreliable products, Wile E. Coyote decides to hire a lawyer and sue the company. Will Forte plays Kevin Avery, who represents Coyote in his case, with John Cena as Buddy Crane, corporate counsel for Acme. The movie also features Lana Condor along with a host of Looney Tunes characters like Porky Pig, Tweety, Foghorn Leghorn and Granny (who gets dinged by an anvil).

Percy Jackson and the Olympians, season 3

A host of new gods and demigods are set to descend in season 3 of Percy Jackson and the Olympians, including Aphrodite and the children of Hades. The new eight-episode installment will premiere on Nov. 20.

Back in January, Disney Plus gave viewers a tease of what’s to come when it dropped with a scene of Percy (Walker Scobell) and Annabeth (Leah Sava’ Jeffries) hitting the dance floor at a middle school dance. But things get a little darker and more dangerous this time for the Camp Half-Blood kids.

Based on the third book in Rick Riordan’s series, The Titan’s Curse, this season takes Percy and crew on a rescue mission to save the goddess Artemis (played by Dafne Keen). Viewers will be introduced to the titan Atlas (Holt McCallany), Annabeth’s human dad (Jesse L. Martin), and Olympian gods Hera (Ming-Na Wen), Demeter (Jennifer Beals) and Apollo (Hubert Smielecki). Kate McKinnon plays Aphrodite.

Ebenezer

Johnny Depp made a surprise appearance at Comic-Con, donning a costume as Ebenezer Scrooge for the upcoming movie, where he plays Charles Dickens’ legendary miser. The film, due in theaters on Nov. 13, also features Rupert Grint, Ian McKellen, Daisy Ridley and Sam Claflin in a star-studded cast.

Avatar: Seven Havens

From the creators of Avatar: The Last Airbender, this new series picks up after The Legend of Korra and follows a pair of twin avatars, one of whom is Korra’s successor. Marked as an omen of destruction during a time when the spirit world and physical world are imbalanced, Pavi — and her sister Nisha — will need to look to the past to discover who they are and find a way to save the Seven Havens. The animated series debuts this fall on Paramount Plus.

Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO

Kenji Kamiyama is directing the new anime film from Sola Animation, which will serve as a sort of prequel. Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO takes place about 100 years before Gundam Rogue Orbit, breaking down the origins of the world that fans are familiar with. Guided by Kamiyama’s vision, the 2027 movie will also tie in with a video game universe.

Regular Show: The Lost Tapes

An extended sneak peek for the new season of Regular Show: The Lost Tapes is now out for our consumption. When the show was revived as The Lost Tapes, it gave viewers new adventures with Mordecai and Rigby through the lens of Pops keeping up with them from the afterlife. Well, there are more VHS tapes to dig through when the next season lands on Cartoon Network and HBO Max this September.

@regularshow_official Couldn’t make it to San Diego Comic-Con? Check out this first look at all new episodes of Regular Show: The Lost Tapes! Coming on: 🌍 Cartoon Network and HBO Max | September 7 🇺🇸 Cartoon Network | September 19 🇺🇸 HBO Max and Hulu | October 11 #regularshow ♬ original sound – Regular Show

Stuart Fails to Save the Universe

HBO Max’s spin-off of The Big Bang Theory follows Kevin Sussman’s Stuart as he tries to undo the damage he caused after breaking one of Leonard and Sheldon’s inventions. A multiversal, reality-hopping, trippy joyride ensues, where viewers see alternate versions of characters they know and much more. The first episode debuted on July 23, but a clip was shared during the show’s Comic-Con panel. You can stream new episodes on Thursdays at 9 p.m. ET.

Dark Matter, Season 2

Apple TV’s panel also included a preview of Dark Matter’s second season, which draws the Dessen family deeper into the mysteries of The Box. Their stability is threatened, as is that of Amanda and Ryan when the series returns on Aug. 28.

Star Trek: Strange New Worlds, Season 4

During Star Trek’s 60th anniversary celebration in Hall H on Saturday, the crew gave the audience a sneak peek of what’s coming in season 4 of Strange New Worlds.

Tech.title: Everything New Marvel Announced at Comic-Con 2026
Tech.content:
Marvel capped off Saturday evening’s Hall H presentations at San Diego Comic-Con, giving audiences a small taste of what’s next on the menu. And we mean small. Kevin Feige and cast members teased out some movies (no TV shows, today), and we’re breaking it down for you here.

Footage from Avengers: Doomsday was shown, with Doom commanding sentinels and a history lesson on the dynamic between the Fantastic Four and the doctor. But there were only two other major announcements, and nothing for X-Men, and no chart outlining Phase 6 or Phase 7.

Ryan Gosling as Ghost Rider

Johnny Blaze is making his MCU debut with Ryan Gosling in the role, which has been rumored for some time among Marvel’s fandom. Shawn Levy will be directing the new movie for the MCU after his successful run with Deadpool & Wolverine. Could this eventually segue into Midnight Sons? Fingers crossed, my friends.

Just announced in Hall H:



Ryan Gosling joins the MCU in Marvel Studios' Ghost Rider, directed by Shawn Levy. Only in theaters 2028. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/S0FQKt5RGn — Marvel Studios (@MarvelStudios) July 26, 2026

Agent Carter in Avengers: Doomsday

Hayley Atwell is now officially confirmed to be in Avengers: Doomsday as Agent Peggy Carter, who was first introduced in the MCU in Captain America: The First Avenger. She was in Hall H during Marvel’s presentation for the film.

Black Panther 3 coming in 2028

Feige pretended to exit the stage for the night but then walked back out with one more update: Black Panther 3 will arrive in December 2028. Actor David Jonsson will play T’Challa Jr. in the film, which is directed by Ryan Coogler. Jonsson is best known for roles as Andy in Alien: Romulus, Peter in The Long Walk and as Gus Sackey in Industry.

Tech.title: ‘Black Panther 3’ Introduces T’Challa Jr. at Marvel’s Comic-Con Presentation
Tech.content:
A new adult T’Challa is joining the Marvel Cinematic Universe. Kevin Feige hit the stage for Marvel’s Hall H Comic-Con showing on Saturday and, toward the end, gave the audience an update on Black Panther 3. Director Ryan Coogler and actors Winston Duke and Letitia Wright were on hand to welcome David Jonsson to the MCU, who will play T’Challa’s son, T’Challa Jr.

Jonsson has appeared in films such as Alien: Romulus and The Long Walk. While no official title has been shared, Feige revealed that Black Panther 3 is due to hit theaters Dec. 15, 2028.

Just announced in Hall H:



Ryan Coogler returns to Marvel Studios to direct Black Panther 3, only in theaters December 15, 2028. #SDCC pic.twitter.com/yB1HgvylvN — Marvel Entertainment (@Marvel) July 26, 2026

Coogler, who’s writing and directing the next installment of the series, has reportedly begun production. He helmed the first two Black Panther movies, which brought the late Chadwick Boseman to the screen as the royal hero. T’Challa Jr. appeared as a child at the end of Black Panther 2, and the character will clearly be aged up for the new movie.

It’s rumored that X-Men character Storm will be in the mix, who has a history with Wakanda (and Black Panther) in the comic books. With a standalone X-Men movie in the works and renewed enthusiasm for the mutants since the release of the animated X-Men ‘97 series, an interconnected storyline would make sense for the MCU. Black Panther: Wakanda Forever (aka Black Panther 2) introduced Tenoch Huerta’s Namor and his underwater kingdom into the MCU, and he’s slated to surface in this year’s Avengers: Doomsday, along with the new Black Panther, Shuri (played by Wright).

Tech.title: After Discovering 6,000 Exoplanets, Researchers May Have Found the First Exomoon
Tech.content:
Humans discovered the first exoplanet in 1992 and have since found approximately 6,000 other planets from outside our solar system. Not once have those researchers found a moon orbiting any of those planets, however. That may have changed with the recent discovery of the first moon-like object in another solar system.

The findings were published in a recent study. Kevin Hoy, lead author of the study and PhD student at the Instituto de Estudios Astrofísicos, says that this potential moon, known as CD-35 2722 B, orbits a brown dwarf instead of a traditional planet. It’s also approximately 90% the size of Jupiter and bigger than Saturn. This moon-like object takes 170 days to fully orbit its host.

Hoy and other researchers used a fairly old trick to discover this moon: radial velocity analysis, which is used to detect wobbles in stars and is an indication that an exoplanet is nearby. Planets get dimmer as they move away from their host star, and exoplanets are found by viewing the changes in spectral shift.

This is the same method scientists used to detect the first exoplanet, and it was used to detect this exosatellite, which is the name granted to objects that have not yet been defined as an exoplanet or an exomoon.

“This is the first time, to our knowledge, this technique has produced evidence of satellites around a companion brown dwarf,” Hoy said in the study.

Most people understand that a moon is an object that orbits another object that isn’t a star, like Earth’s moon or the various other moons in the solar system. NASA

Schrödinger’s Moon?

The study’s findings aren’t without their controversy. Arguably, the biggest question is whether this is actually a moon. Brown dwarves, often referred to as failed stars, are far larger than a standard planet but did not have the chemical reactions in their core necessary to become a star. The exosatellite orbiting this brown dwarf is also bigger than all but one planet in our solar system and larger than most of the exoplanets discovered by researchers so far.

Complicating matters is the fact that no one actually knows what a moon is. There is no standard definition from the International Astronomical Union, the authority that usually comes up with such definitions. Most people understand a moon to be a naturally occurring object that orbits a larger object, like our moon orbits Earth.

There are some rules to this. The host object can’t be a star because then the orbiting object would be a planet. It also can’t be made by humans, or it’s deemed a satellite. The definition has expanded as astronomers find additional, unique types of moons. One example is Zoozve, a quasi-moon that would look like a moon from the surface of Venus but is actually an asteroid that orbits the sun and is close enough to look like a moon.

For CD-35 2722 B, Hoy told me that one problem is the special nature of brown dwarfs. Brown dwarfs are considered substellar objects because they’re too big and dense to be a planet but lack the hydrogen fusion needed to be a star. They exist in a middle ground between the two, so it’s unclear whether something orbiting a brown dwarf would be considered a planet or a moon.

That isn’t the only roadblock. “The object itself is at least the mass of Jupiter, which is far larger than the rocky and icy moons in the solar system,” Hoy said. “It’s not clear that anything that big should be considered a moon.”

Hoy says that the currently accepted IAU definitions group brown dwarfs in with stars, in that an object orbiting a brown dwarf of sufficient size would be considered a planet. However, this brown dwarf orbits its host star like a planet and CD-35 2722 B orbits the brown dwarf like a moon; therefore, it fulfills both the behavior of a moon and the definition of a planet.

“Maybe when a definition for exomoons is written, objects like this will meet both the definitions of planet and moon, but we’ll have to see,” Hoy said. “Those terms are mutually exclusive in the solar system, so I wouldn’t be surprised if they wrote the definition in such a way as to preserve that.”

Until that day comes, no one is quite sure what to make of CD-35 2722 B, and until the IAU opens up the metaphorical box and comes up with an official definition for what a moon is, CD-35 2722 B could realistically be considered both a moon and a planet.

Tech.title: 3 Apple Watch Running Features I Wish I’d Known About Sooner
Tech.content:
As a longtime Apple Watch wearer and runner, I thought I knew everything there was to know about the watch’s running features. Turns out, there was still plenty I hadn’t explored, and a few of those features could’ve made training a whole lot easier.

With the San Francisco Marathon happening this weekend, I got a crash course in Apple Watch running features from Apple. Most of these work on every model running the latest version of WatchOS, while others are exclusive to the Apple Watch Ultra series. These are the features I’m adding to my own training routine.



@cnetdotcom I got a crash course in Apple Watch running features from the pros, and these are the ones I’m adding to my own training routine: 1. Custom Workouts Build your own training plan in the Fitness app based on time, distance or heart rate zones. Your watch keeps track of each segment and taps your wrist when it’s time to move on. 2. Pacer Set your target pace before a run, and your Apple Watch will help keep you on track so you don’t start too fast or fall behind. 3. Race Route Turn your usual running route into your own personal race. Compare against your best or most recent time and see if you can beat it. I also share a few bonus tips (including a couple of Apple Watch Ultra exclusives) in the full guide linked in our bio. #AppleWatch #SFMarathon #MarathonTraining #allthingsmobile #fitness ♬ Volt Slope – Guitar Whisperer

1. Custom Workouts

Instead of trying to remember every interval or warmup, let your Apple Watch guide you through the workout.

To build your own workout, open the Fitness app on your iPhone and tap the Workouts tab. Find your workout of choice (Running, in my case), tap the timer icon, select Custom Workout, then scroll to the bottom and tap the + button.

Give your workout a name so it’s easy to find later on your watch (try adding an emoji or three), then build your routine. I started mine with two-minutes of warmup drills, but you can also create segments based on distance, time or heart rate zones. You can even repeat an entire sequence so you don’t have to re-create each interval individually, then finish it off with a cooldown if that’s your jam.

Once you’re done, the workout automatically syncs to your Apple Watch. The next time you start a run, tap the timer icon, select your custom workout and go. The watch keeps track of every segment and buzzes your wrist when it’s time to move on, so you can focus on running instead of watching the clock.

2. Pacer

If you’re the type who gets a little too hyped at the start of a race and ends up burned out halfway through (like me), Pacer can help.

From the Running workout on your watch, tap the timer icon, scroll down to Pacer, tap the + button, choose your race distance and enter your goal finish time. The watch calculates the pace you’ll need to maintain.

Next, go back to that timer icon on the top right-hand corner of your running workout on the watch, then scroll down to find the Pacer plan you just created. The interface will now show a progress bar on screen instead of your usual stats, which moves to show whether you’re ahead or behind your target pace. Red means you’re falling behind, green means you’re moving faster than your target, and the sweet spot is right in the middle.

You can also swipe between screens to see your usual workout stats throughout the run.

3. Race Route

If you always run the same neighborhood loop or trail, you might be able to use it to compete against yourself.

Open the Running workout, tap the timer icon, scroll down to Race Route and select one of your saved routes. Then choose whether you want to race against your personal record or your latest run.

I’m still working my way back from an injury, so I’ll be using it to chase my previous best.

Bonus Features for Apple Watch Ultra

The Ultra models in Apple’s smartwatch line, like the latest Apple Watch Ultra 3, add a few running features you won’t find on the standard Apple Watch.

Precision Start

If you’ve ever started a workout with an Apple Watch, you’re familiar with the three-second countdown after you press start. This, among other things, gives the watch time to find a GPS signal. But it’s not great for race day if you just want to get up and go.

To get rid of it and enable precision start, open Settings on your watch, scroll down to Workout and turn on Precision Start.

Now when you begin a workout, the timer starts immediately. It may not have locked into GPS off the bat, but you’ll know if it has when the compass icon in the upper-left corner turns blue.

Action button running shortcut

If you want to get into a run even faster, you can assign the Action Button to launch your favorite workout.

Go to Settings > Action Button, choose Workout, then under First Press select Outdoor Run. You can even assign it to launch one of the Custom Workouts you just made.

Quick Pause Shortcut

Instead of relying on Auto Pause, an Apple Watch Ultra model also lets you instantly pause and resume a workout by pressing any two buttons at the same time — no sweaty screen swiping for me.

More AI running features in your future

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPhone (iPhone 15 Pro or later) paired with an Apple Watch running WatchOS 26, you’ll also be able to use Workout Buddy.

Workout Buddy is an AI-powered voice companion that uses your workout history, pace, heart rate and fitness data to give you real-time personalized encouragement during your run.

Instead of generic prompts, it can say things like, “This is your fastest mile yet,” or remind you that you’ve already run 40 miles this month. With the upcoming WatchOS 27 set to roll out in September, Workout Buddy will also be available in Spanish.

Whether you’re running the San Francisco Marathon this weekend, training for your next race or just trying to get back to your personal best, I hope a few of these tips help make your next run a little smoother.

Tech.title: I Tested the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 for a Week and It’s a Rugged Scene-Stealer
Tech.content:
Samsung’s new rugged smartwatch hasn’t changed much on the outside, but the biggest upgrades on the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 are all hiding inside.

It has a larger battery, more powerful processor and new adventure features to take you from the office to the trails without extra gear. At $700 ($50 more than the original Galaxy Watch Ultra), it’s the most expensive watch in Samsung’s lineup, but it’s also the most durable and arguably the most interesting.

I’ve spent the past week testing the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, and while the verdict is still out on its long-term features, like health tracking and battery life, it’s clear that it can pull double duty as both an adventure-ready companion and a luxury smartwatch.

Whether its $700 price tag is justified depends on what you’re looking for. If you want Samsung’s most rugged watch with the biggest battery, brightest display and the most outdoor features, it could be worth the premium. But if the package matters less than the core smartwatch features, you may be better off getting the standard Galaxy Watch 9 (or even older models) for nearly half the price.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 keeps the squircle frame, but increases size and brightness of the screen.

Galaxy Watch Ultra 2: First impressions

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 looks identical to the original. It has the same premium titanium case, sapphire crystal display, signature squircle design and three programmable physical buttons. But look closer and you’ll notice a few subtle upgrades.

The display is slightly larger (1.52” compared to 1.5” on the original), even though the overall watch is smaller and lighter. Samsung also redesigned the bands, making them thinner and more breathable so the watch sits flatter against your wrist, which the company says improves sensor contact. The new clasp mechanism makes them easier to swap than traditional watch bands, though it also locks you into Samsung’s proprietary system.

Side by side look of the two new Galaxy Watches: Galaxy Watch 9 and Ultra 2. Andrew Lanxon/CNET

The fact that I slept a few nights without ripping it off halfway through the night says a lot for a watch this size. I still wouldn’t choose to sleep with it long-term, but it’s noticeably more comfortable than I expected.

Samsung watches already have the best displays in the business, and the Ultra 2 kicks it up a notch with an even brighter, 5,000-nit display (vs 3,000 nits on the original) that looks flawless even in harsh mid-morning summer sun.

Galaxy Watch Ultra 2’s new trail running and diving features

The Ultra 2 edges closer to sports watch territory with a dedicated trail-running mode that surfaces real-time climb and elevation data, has offline trail map access and hydration reminders. I live near a regional park with hundreds of trail options, and I’ve been frustrated by traditional smartwatches that don’t account for uneven terrain or give me enough credit for the extreme elevation changes.

I took the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 on a trail run to test the new feature.

After a 5-mile trail run through the Northern California hills, I was impressed by two things: turn-by-turn audio navigation and real-time elevation tracking. I don’t like wearing headphones when I trail run because I prefer to stay aware of my surroundings, so hearing directions through the watch speaker is the perfect solution. It’s worth noting that getting a route onto the watch for those directions was tedious. Samsung says you’ll eventually be able to search for nearby trails directly from Google Maps, but that feature wasn’t ready during my testing, so I had to load a trail route from a .gpx file on my phone.

With real-time elevation tracking, the watch automatically broke my route into individual climbs and showed my progress. Having a live progress bar as I approach a hill gives me a tangible goal, making it easier to push through steeper sections.

The trail running feature on the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 shows real-time elevation.

I was less enthused about the hydration reminders. I’d traded my water bottle for my tripod that day, so the three reminders I received during my hour-long trail run mostly fell on deaf ears. Considering the heat, I probably should have listened. But because the reminders are based on AI estimates of hydration loss rather than a dedicated sensor that measures sweat loss directly, I found myself trusting them less.

The Ultra 2 also debuts a recreational diving feature developed in partnership with Italian diving company Mares. Because it doesn’t track gas or oxygen consumption, it’s not meant to replace a dedicated dive computer. Instead, it seems aimed at casual recreational divers who want basic dive information on a device they’re already wearing. The app won’t be available at launch, so I’ll reserve judgment until I can test it myself later this year.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 has big changes under the hood with a new processor and bigger battery.

Galaxy Watch Ultra 2’s raise-to-talk Gemini

My favorite feature, however, has nothing to do with rugged adventure sports. It’s Gemini. I’ve already raved about how useful Google’s AI assistant is on your wrist in smartwatches like the Google Pixel 4, and the new raise-to-talk feature makes it even better.

No button presses or wake words required, just raise your wrist and start talking. This added layer of convenience made me much more likely to use it and helped me get things done completely hands-free. At the risk of sounding like a trad wife, I use it a lot in the kitchen. I had meat sitting in the fridge that was about to go bad, so I asked for a simple slow cooker carnitas recipe, and it delivered. I didn’t even have to smudge the screen with meat juice to get the step-by-step instructions read aloud. It’s also been handy for settling debates with my endlessly curious 9-year-old before he loses patience and I have to dig my phone out of my pocket.

Better battery life in theory, in practice its still TBD

The Ultra 2 packs an 800-mAh battery, up from 590-mAh on the original, paired with Qualcomm’s new Snapdragon Wear Elite processor, which should be more power efficient. On-device AI that optimizes battery life as it learns your habits. Samsung rates it for up to 60 hours with the watch’s always-on display enabled.

The Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 is rated for 10ATM and be used for recreational diving.

It’s still too soon to know if that 60-hour claim is realistic because my initial results haven’t been great. That five-mile trail run chewed through nearly 30% of the battery, and I have yet to reach the watch’s promised 60-hour mark. I have gotten closer to 48 hours before needing to recharge, though.

Either way, don’t expect sports watch-level endurance. A Garmin Fenix 8 Pro, for example, can last more than a week on a charge. The Ultra 2 powers a brighter display, Wear OS and always-ready Gemini, all of which demand far more energy than what a dedicated sports watch.

Extra health and recovery tools

Both watches also get a new suite of health features, which feed into the redesigned Samsung Health app on your phone.

Vitals tracking can flag possible signs of illness by monitoring metrics like heart rate variability, resting heart rate, respiratory rate, blood oxygen and skin temperature. There’s also a new Heart Health Score, Daily Cardio Load to help guide recovery, and a Fitness Index assessment that uses AI to build you a personalized training plan.

Many of these features require at least seven nights of sleep before they unlock (which I haven’t yet logged), so I’m holding off on judging for now.

I appreciate that Samsung isn’t putting these health insights behind a subscription the way companies like Whoop and Oura do. Some guided workouts and iFit content still require separate subscriptions, but the core health features are included with the watch.

Samsung also hasn’t confirmed whether these software features will come to older Galaxy Watches. So, for now, they’re another point in favor of upgrading.

The three new Galaxy Watches: Galaxy Watch Ultra 2, Galaxy Watch 9 (44mm) and Galaxy Watch 9 (40mm). Joe Maldonado/CNET

Should you upgrade to the Galaxy Watch Ultra 2?

After a week of testing, the Ultra 2 feels like more of an upgrade than its familiar design would suggest. If you’re coming from an older Galaxy Watch and want the latest hardware with the peace of mind that it’ll hold up to the elements, this is the one I’d be looking at.

But I still have plenty left to test. Many of the health features haven’t unlocked yet, and I need to spend more time with the battery before delivering a final verdict. Battery life, in particular, will make or break my recommendation — both over the Galaxy Watch 9 and for anyone considering upgrading from the original Ultra.

Tech.title: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Flip 8 Gets the Cover Screen Right — for a Price
Tech.content:
Samsung’s Galaxy Z Flip 8, announced Wednesday during the company’s Unpacked event, launches with the price hike we expected, along with a few welcome tweaks to its design and software that could make the phone easier to use.

I got to demo the $1,200 Z Flip 8, and even though that’s a $100 spike from the starting price of last year’s Z Flip 7 for the same 256GB of storage, the phone is noticeably lighter and thinner than prior iterations. Samsung says that at launch, the 180-gram Flip 8 will be the lightest flip-style foldable phone on the market. When unfolded, the phone is 6.1mm thick, which is noticeably thinner than the Z Flip 7 (6.8mm) and Motorola Razr Ultra (7.2mm).

Samsung’s Galaxy Z Flip 8 now lets you add apps with a simple function in the app drawer on the cover screen. Joseph Maldonado/CNET

But I was more impressed by a number of software tweaks coming to the Z Flip 8 that make it easier to use while closed. For starters, you can now add apps to the cover screen by scrolling up on the app drawer and tapping “Add apps” to access any app installed on your phone. Previously, you had to dig through various settings menus to do the same thing. This is also much closer to how the latest Motorola Razr phones let you use any app you want on their cover screens.

The Z Flip 8’s cover screen is also getting the “Recent apps” shortcut button for the first time — which is wild, since quickly switching tasks is such a basic function on the rest of Android. When I test flip-style phones, I’m most likely on the cover screen using Maps for transit directions while playing music and texting friends — that simple button means I can now swap between these directly without having to kick back to the lock screen. That’s also a feature already available on the Razr.

You can now easily switch apps on the cover screen. Joseph Maldonado/CNET

The Z Flip 8 carries over several features that debuted on Samsung’s Galaxy S26 phone line — for instance, the foldable’s video camera includes Super Steady with horizontal lock to smooth out movement while filming. And I had a lot of fun playing with a new camera feature called My Fan Cam, which uses Galaxy AI to identify subjects in a video and create a crop that only follows that person throughout the recording, as if the camera is exclusively focused on them.

Samsung’s My FamCam lets you make videos focusing on individuals within a clip. The center example is the original, while the other two focus on me and my colleague Tara Brown. Mike Sorrentino/CNET

The Flip 8 is powered by Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy — which is the same custom version of the processor used for the Galaxy S26 phones as well as the foldable’s pricier siblings, the Z Fold 8 and Z Fold 8 Ultra, which were also announced at Unpacked.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 has a 6.9-inch display when unfolded. Joseph Maldonado/CNET

Other specs carry over from last year’s Z Flip 7, including the 6.9-inch internal display and the 4.1-inch cover screen. It’s the same for the cameras, which are a 50-megapixel wide-angle, 12-megapixel ultrawide and 10-megapixel selfie camera. The phone’s 4,300-mAh battery, 25-watt max wired charging speed and 15-watt max wireless charging are also the same. We’ll have to see when testing the phone whether the newer processor is efficient enough to improve the overall battery life.

The Galaxy Z Flip 8 in pink, cream and graphite colors. A mint color is also available as an online exclusive. Joseph Maldonado/CNET

The Galaxy Flip 8 comes in four colors: pink, graphite and cream, as well as mint as an online-exclusive offering. The phone goes on preorder today and will go on sale Aug. 7.

Tech.title: NordVPN’s New HangUp App Screens Calls and Texts for Scams
Tech.content:
The phone rings. There’s a sense of dread. Friend or foe? Scam or no? NordVPN — known more for encrypting internet traffic and hiding IP addresses — has launched an Android app named HangUp that screens incoming calls for potential scammers and telemarketers. The app is free to everyone. You don’t need a paid NordVPN account.

HangUp uses call protection technology from Hiya, which has its own mobile app to block spam and fraud calls and detect AI deepfakes. HangUp also can scan incoming text messages by incorporating NordVPN’s Message Protection, which the company launched in June. HangUp app customers can choose to use only call screening if they wish.

Flagging calls might be a new feature for a VPN that CNET deems the fastest, but scam screening is already available via many cellphone service providers as well as devices themselves. AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon, iPhones, Google Pixel and Samsung phones can identify and block unwanted calls, as can major landline services.

HangUp is currently available only for Android and can be downloaded in the Google Play Store. After downloading the app, you’ll need to sign in with your NordVPN account or create a free one on its website. Finally, you’ll need to give permission to the app to identify caller ID and spam.

NordVPN premium customers already have call and message protection built into the app.

Worldwide problem

Scam calls aren’t just annoying — they defraud people out of billions of dollars annually. It’s a far cry from the quaint beginning of telemarketing in 1957.

Nearly 80% of Americans got at least one scam call in the past year, and 40% report feeling unsafe because of scam calls, according to a NordVPN survey. Hiya research found that Americans receive an average of 10 unwanted calls per week and that 30 million people lost money — at an average of $682 apiece — to a phone scam in the past year.

See also: Scam Calls Have Gotten Out of Control. This One Strategy Actually Helps

NordVPN’s survey said the most common scam in the US is fake telemarketers or sales agents (43%), followed by fake healthcare providers (20%) and fake government or tax officials (18%).

“What these numbers reflect is a deeper anxiety about not being able to trust a call,” NordVPN Product Director Domininkas Virbickas said in a statement.

How HangUp works

When a call comes in, HangUp checks the number and warns you if it could be a scam, spam or telemarketing attempt before you answer the call. The app is able to do this by using caller reputation data that Hiya uses for its own service.

You can’t block individual phone numbers with the app, but instead, you can block categories — for instance if you want to stop all calls that are categorized as telemarketers.

You can also employ HangUp to scan incoming text messages. The app says it can detect scams, fraud, malicious messages and deceptive content. The app says it “may analyze message content, including links, sender information, and other relevant signals, to assess potential risks.”

If you’re worried that this is another way of getting your data, NordVPN says it will not record or listen to calls, nor will it store any text message content.

NordVPN has another disclaimer about HangUp. It says the app is only an “informational assistance tool” and can’t guarantee that it will be able to identify and block all unwanted calls. HangUp users can’t “rely exclusively” on the app and are “solely responsible” for calls and texts that they get.

So be sure you know the warning signs of scam calls and the steps you can take. The Federal Communications Commission lists them out, including not answering calls from numbers you don’t know and hanging up immediately if someone asks for money or personal information.
